stories.Headline: David Fincher defends generative AI use in Cliff Booth film amid viewer criticism
stories.Summary:
David Fincher defended the onscreen use of generative AI in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth after fans criticized the film, Deadline reported on November 20, 2026. The Quentin Tarantino-penned sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood (2019) drew accusations of apparent Gen AI use from early viewers and critics. Fincher, a three-time Oscar-nominated director, shared his thoughts on the rapidly growing technology with the Los Angeles Times. The A.V. Club reported that The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth is the latest Netflix movie to face such accusations. The film stars Brad Pitt, who reprises his Oscar-winning role as the psychotic stuntman.

Set in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time, the film follows Pitt's eponymous stuntman, now a projectionist who moonlights as a Hollywood fixer. He gets caught up in a conspiracy that involves a Filipino gang and a stolen Oscar. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premieres Thanksgiving on Imax and premieres Dec. 23 on Netflix. The film credits a "generative consultant," and it reportedly uses the tech to animate fake issues of TV Guide. A Bloomberg piece from March reported Ben Affleck's AI "ethical" company, InterPositive, for which Netflix paid $600 million, helped produce "an upcoming film starring Brad Pitt."

Fincher told the Los Angeles Times, "I'm not a Luddite, so I don't fear the unknown." He asked whether everyone is satisfied that the art form is figured out enough to go back to celluloid. He noted people have painted for 40,000 years while film is about a hundred years old. He said everyone is saying "Stop. Pencils down. No more iterating," and that it is not necessary to have at your fingertips the ability to change the color of that person's eyes. Fincher added, "Well, it exists. Should we not use it?"

Per Kotaku, indie filmmaker and influencer Patrick Tomasso posted on X that he "walked out of Cliff Booth completely gutted." Tomasso said what could have been a really great sequel is overshadowed by some of the most blatant and egregious AI use he has ever seen in a studio film. Next Best Picture dinged the movie for "noticeably distracting" use of generative AI in key moments, calling it nothing but an eyesore. One viewer said they "walked out of Cliff Booth completely gutted," and another called the apparent use "astounding to an absurd degree." The A.V. Club reached out to Netflix for comment.

Fincher got his start at ILM on Return of the Jedi and Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom, and has long been an early adopter of new technology, like Steven Soderbergh. Soderbergh also used AI in a John Lennon documentary earlier this year, and his results were lambasted at Cannes. It is unclear when that movie will ever be made available, and John Lennon: The Last Interview does not even have a Wikipedia page. Earlier this year, Oscar-winning filmmakers Affleck and Danny Boyle admitted to using the technology for their respective new releases, Animals and Ink. Academy Award nominee Ava DuVernay defended using AI to animate photographs in her new documentary about the 14th Amendment, 14th.

Boyle confirmed there is about 30 seconds of it in Ink where they animate a couple of old photographs. DuVernay said in October that they animated some photos in the public domain, and that it brings people closer to that time in history, which was their goal. She said people have to see it and check it out for themselves and make their decisions about how they feel. Last month, Netflix announced that as many as 300 productions used the technology. The A.V. Club noted it is unclear what exactly was done with AI in the film.

stories.Headline: Anthropic goes public at a $2 trillion valuation as investors demand rapid sales growth to offset huge computing costs
stories.Summary:
Anthropic began trading as a public company on November 19, 2026, opening at $111.50 a share, a 34% jump from its IPO price, and closing 17% higher at $97.17 a share. The debut gave the AI giant a $2 trillion valuation at market open, which CNN described as passing its first trading test with flying colors. The company, founded just under six years ago, is set for the largest stock market debut of all time. Its early bet on building AI tools for businesses made it a favorite of the AI market and set the stage for the record-breaking listing.

As a public company, Anthropic will face more pressure to grow each quarter and prove its Claude AI agent keeps growing fast despite skyrocketing computing costs and increased competition. Investors will look for massive sales growth each quarter to offset the nearly trillion-dollar computing expenses the company expects in the years ahead. The enterprise AI market grew fourfold in a year, from $33 billion in 2025 to $177 billion in 2026, according to Menlo Ventures, which has invested billions in Anthropic. Some businesses that fueled its rise are starting to slow their AI spending, according to one economist who monitors AI enterprise spending.

Ken Mahoney, president of financial planning firm Mahoney Asset Management, said the shift is not easy, describing the move from hardly any scrutiny to analysts reevaluating everything you do. CNN noted that the world's largest publicly traded AI companies, Nvidia, Google and Amazon, have seen their shares stumble even when quarterly numbers fall in line with Wall Street's expectations. The billions spent on infrastructure, rapid model development and growing adoption have set sky-high expectations across the industry. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei appeared on video outside the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on the day of the listing.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Saudi Data and AI Authority launches Year of Artificial Intelligence initiative across universities
stories.Summary:
The Saudi Data and AI Authority launched the Year of Artificial Intelligence initiative across universities in the Kingdom on November 19, 2026. This program aims to spread knowledge about new technologies and promote their responsible use while developing national skills for the future. The initiative includes a range of scientific seminars, panel discussions, training workshops, interactive booths, and specialized consultations for the students. It seeks to transform academic ideas and projects into innovative solutions that support the digital transformation journey of the Kingdom. These efforts cultivate national talent capable of keeping pace with technological shifts to strengthen global leadership in data and AI.

The program operates in collaboration with universities across the country, including Umm Al-Qura University, to align with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. It requires the integration of academic research with real-world industrial applications to create market-ready technologies and intellectual property for the nation. The scheme focuses on developing homegrown capabilities and fostering innovation to move beyond the simple adoption of existing artificial intelligence technologies. It emphasizes investing in human capital through specialized education, research opportunities, interdisciplinary collaboration, and practical training for the next generation. These steps aim to create high-value economic opportunities and position Saudi Arabia as a leading international hub for AI research.

The Saudi Data and AI Authority is responsible for the initiative and stated it will help strengthen the Kingdom's global leadership. They said the program will transform academic ideas into innovative solutions that support the digital transformation journey of the Saudi state. The authority believes these efforts will cultivate national talent capable of contributing to a future built on knowledge and innovation. They intend to develop national skills and promote the responsible use of AI technologies across all participating universities in the Kingdom. The authority views this as a way to align national technological growth with the broader strategic goals of Saudi Vision 2030.

Muhammad Khurram Khan, a cybersecurity professor at King Saud University, said the designation of 2026 as the Year of AI is an important milestone. He stated that the initiative reflects a commitment to harness AI as a driver of economic diversification and sustainable development. Khan noted that Saudi universities possess a wealth of research talent and scientific expertise that could address challenges across various sectors. He believes stronger collaboration between universities, government institutions, and the private sector can help transform research projects into innovative products. The professor argued that developing Saudi AI researchers and entrepreneurs is essential for building sustainable national capabilities and global competitiveness.

The background provided is that the Kingdom seeks to become a globally competitive, knowledge-based economy through the use of advanced technology. Saudi Arabia aims to move toward developing indigenous technologies and generating intellectual property rather than just deploying existing foreign AI solutions. The initiative is part of a larger strategy to foster innovation and contribute more significantly to the global AI landscape. It builds on the existing research talent found within the university system to address national priorities and various global challenges. This effort is designed to accelerate the digital transformation of the country while creating new economic opportunities for its citizens.

The next steps involve implementing the initiative across universities to strengthen the link between academic research and real-world industrial applications. The program will continue to provide specialized education and practical training to develop the next generation of Saudi AI engineers. The articles leave open how the private sector will specifically collaborate with universities and the authority to commercialize these research projects. They do not specify the exact number of universities participating or the specific timeline for the various workshops and seminars. It remains unclear what specific metrics will be used to measure the success of the Year of Artificial Intelligence initiative.

stories.Headline: Anthropic holds largest IPO in history on Nasdaq as CEO Dario Amodei pledges paced AI deployment
stories.Summary:
Anthropic launched the largest initial public offering in history on the Nasdaq exchange this Thursday. CEO Dario Amodei and seven co-founders led the company through this record breaking public debut. The artificial intelligence giant entered the stock market during a massive industry boom. Shares opened at 111.50 dollars, which was 34 percent above the initial price. The company closed its first trading day at 97.17 dollars per share.

The IPO priced shares at 83 dollars, valuing the company at 1.5 trillion dollars. Anthropic raised 81.34 billion dollars, or 107.34 billion dollars including a 26 billion dollar private placement. The market cap peaked at 2 trillion dollars, surpassing the June listing of SpaceX. It closed with a market cap of 1.3 trillion dollars, or 1.75 trillion dollars. Iconiq invested over 6 billion dollars for a 1.8 percent stake worth 31.8 billion dollars.

Dario Amodei stated the company was built for the benefit of all humankind. He pledged to pace the training and deployment of AI systems to ensure safety. Amodei said the company will not bend to political or business pressure. He noted that the most difficult safety work still lies ahead of the firm. He also mentioned that AI will have a positive impact on gene editing and CRISPR.

Protesters rallied against the company in San Francisco and New York after the debut. Some AI safety advocates challenged the safety branding used by the company. Over 400 employees are estimated to be worth more than 100 million dollars each. Some insiders worry these newly minted millionaires might leave the company. The IPO could potentially deliver 156 billion dollars to charity.

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, which serves as a stress test for that structure. The company rose quickly to become the sixth most valuable public company on earth. Spark Capital and Yasmin Razavi were noted as key venture capital supporters. Hyperliquid served as the main platform for price discovery before the official listing. The company's rise is described as a manifestation of trust and years of work.

The company now holds a stronger financial position to pursue its safety goals. Investors are watching if the success of this IPO will reshape the venture industry. Some analysts believe the age of unicorns is over because of trillion dollar startups. It remains open whether the company can maintain its intelligence moat against competitors. The articles leave the long term stability of the stock price undecided.

stories.Headline: Wall Street forecasters warn the AI trade is ending as tech stocks slide
stories.Summary:
Wall Street forecasters are worrying that the artificial intelligence trade is ending after a recent sell-off in tech stocks. This bruising weekslong decline sent the Nasdaq Composite into negative territory for the year on Friday, November 20, 2026. The market had climbed to all-time highs barely a month ago before the current bloodbath in the tech sector began. Investors are now questioning if the AI-fueled bull market is over as tech and AI names face heavy losses. This downturn has dragged the S&P 500 and the Dow into a correction while the Nasdaq 100 declines.

The Nasdaq 100 is down 17 percent from its high, while the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF fell 24 percent. Roundhill Neocloud ETF dropped 61 to 63 percent, and Roundhill Memory ETF fell 56 to 58 percent. The iShares Semiconductor ETF is down 37 to 41 percent, and Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF fell 30 percent. Nvidia stock has fallen 40 to 47 percent since early October, and the record Anthropic IPO failed to boost the market. These changes follow the blunami midterms and concerns regarding the impact of new regulations on data center construction projects.

Sameer Samana of Wells Fargo said the AI sector could be in a reset due to higher rates and oil prices. He noted that the Anthropic IPO is sucking liquidity from other markets, so the bank favors industrials and materials stocks. Wells Fargo expects volatility to remain high as markets reassess AI spending, industry leadership, and the conversion of investment into cash. Samana described a hypothetical scenario where earnings growth craters by 33 percent, which would cause valuations to fall in suit. The bank believes that tighter regulation of AI and signs of economic weakness are triggering this broader valuations reset.

Gary Marcus wrote on Substack that a death spiral has begun and that Nvidia and Neoclouds will be hit hard. Citi analysts stated that recent stock rotations resemble the extreme moves that occurred before the dot-com bubble burst years ago. Some investors view the departure of Jensen Huang as an existential risk because he was the poster child for AI. TS Lombard changed its global equities stance to underweight, specifically trimming AI exposed areas in the US and Taiwan. Capital Economics warned that the revenue hurdle to justify the scale of AI investment looks very demanding for tech firms.

The articles state that selling is driven by panic about slowing AI capex and the impact of the Nvidia crisis. Lawmakers may crack down on new construction, which could cap growth in the data center sector over the next year. Capital Economics has long warned of an AI bubble, pointing to risks around AI revenue and general investment levels. Citi cut its risk exposure to US equities last month and advised investors to remain on guard against spillover risks. The current market volatility follows a period where AI investments reached multi-trillion-dollar levels without generating unprecedented revenues for the firms.

Capital Economics predicts the S&P 500 could drop 9 percent through the end of next year following the Anthropic IPO. TS Lombard suggests a vibe shift by late 2027 could cause a 40 percent AI stock crash by early 2028. Capital Economics maintains a central forecast that a stock market AI bust will occur during the year 2027. stories.Headline: The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation pledges 350 million dollars in computing spending to CoreWeave
stories.Summary:
The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation will provide 350 million dollars in computing spending to the company known as CoreWeave. This financial commitment was revealed in recent tax disclosures from the charitable organization established by the former Nvidia chief executive officer. A filing from Nvidia in June identified CoreWeave as the receiver and noted that 108.3 million dollars were already spent. The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science to give researchers access to large scale GPU computing resources. This specific pledge represents the largest donation made by the Huang Foundation during the 2025 calendar year.

The foundation gave 19 million dollars to the California College of the Arts and 1.2 million dollars to the Hong Kong University. Core Scientific is building a 100 megawatt data center at Port Muskogee, Oklahoma, under a broader 500 megawatt hosting agreement. This wider arrangement with CoreWeave has a potential value of 8.7 billion dollars over twelve years with two five year extensions. The Muskogee site uses 70 megawatts for critical IT capacity and 30 megawatts for cooling and electrical systems. Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company serves as the electricity provider for this facility which began construction in early 2025.

CoreWeave stated that the charitable foundation does not directly use the computing power provided through these specific financial grants. The foundation is responsible for awarding resources to scientific research grant awardees who then utilize the large scale GPU computing. Core Scientific manages the Muskogee project with Evans General Contractors serving as the construction manager under a cost plus fee contract. The project design includes two compute data halls and one separate network data hall to accommodate high density GPU equipment. These facilities will support high performance computing workloads for CoreWeave and one end customer who remains undisclosed to the public.

Investors are scrutinizing the financial interactions between AI infrastructure firms and consumers because the sector is now heavily financially intertwined. CoreWeave investors view the foundation pledge as a sign of more demand for computing services and the necessary GPU hardware. Port Muskogee estimates the data center will generate 4 billion dollars in capital investment and 182 million dollars in benefits. Local entities including Muskogee County, the City of Muskogee, and Hilldale School District may receive 12 million dollars in tax revenue. The project is expected to support 150 jobs with average salaries that exceed 65,000 dollars for the local workforce.

The foundation assets were 12.7 billion dollars at December 31, 2025, which is an increase from the previous 9.2 billion dollars. About 90 percent of these assets consist of Nvidia shares, and the organization gave 373 million dollars in 2024. CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs for its cloud computing company, and Nvidia is a key stakeholder in the business. This expansion is part of a wider US buildout, including Oracle's 165 billion dollar Project Jupiter planned for New Mexico. Core Scientific is converting and developing infrastructure to serve the growing demand for AI and cloud computing across the country.

The Muskogee facility was initially anticipated to reach substantial completion during the first half of the 2026 calendar year. Investors will continue to scrutinize future disclosures regarding the remaining computing obligations and the revenue contributions for the firm CoreWeave. The articles do not identify the specific end customer who will use the GPU infrastructure at the Oklahoma data center. They also leave open the specific types of AI workloads that are planned for the Muskogee high performance computing facility. No further details are provided regarding the exact timing of the remaining payments from the Huang Foundation to CoreWeave.

stories.Headline: Google lets Gemini users disable memory and adds macOS computer use for US subscribers
stories.Summary:
Google introduced a new privacy option for Gemini on November 18, 2026, to let users disable the memory feature. This update allows individuals to stop the AI assistant from remembering their preferences and past interactions for future queries. Google also added computer use to Gemini for macOS on November 19, 2026, to work across files and apps. This macOS feature is available to users in the United States with AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra accounts. Additionally, Google AI Studio now enables the creation of full-stack Android apps using Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen.

Users can disable memory by clicking their profile avatar, selecting Settings, tapping Personalized Intelligence, and then choosing Memory. This toggle stops Gemini from learning from conversations or collecting data to train its artificial intelligence based on user behavior. Temporary chat logs are automatically deleted after 72 hours, and active chats are no longer saved to user accounts. By default, conversations are kept for approximately two months, but users can disable the Keep Activity setting for privacy. Disabling memory does not erase existing data, which users must manage via the dedicated Gemini memory panel.

Google stated that this new functionality provides a transparent balance between personalized AI assistance and the privacy of the user. The company noted that the memory feature normally remembers user preferences to deliver tailored and relevant responses for future queries. Google also announced upcoming controls that will allow users to customize exactly how long their chat history is stored. The company intends for these tools to grant users the freedom to choose how much information the AI retains. These updates aim to give individuals direct control over their stored data to address various privacy concerns.

Many users raised privacy concerns because of the accumulation of personal data across their various chats with the AI. The new memory toggle is described as a big win for the end user regarding their personal data control. Android developers are affected by Google AI Studio, which now allows them to publish production-ready Kotlin apps in minutes. These apps can include AI features, user sign-in, and data persistence, and they can be published to the Play Store. The macOS update affects US users who want Gemini to work in the background across the web and apps.

Gemini previously functioned as an active personal assistant that stored user interactions to improve the relevance of its future responses. Google AI Studio now includes a Build agent that helps users go from a single prompt to a full app. The system previously retained most conversations for two months to help refine system performance and improve search results. Google has expanded its AI offerings to include these new developer tools and the macOS computer use integration. These changes follow a pattern of increasing the capabilities of Gemini across different platforms and user roles.

Google will soon release more controls for users to customize the specific duration of their chat history storage. The company continues to integrate Gemini into various environments, including the Android development process and the macOS operating system. The articles do not state when the customized history duration controls will be available to the general public. It remains unclear how the new macOS computer use feature will interact with the existing privacy toggle for memory. The text does not specify if the Android app build agent will be available to all Google AI Studio users.

stories.Headline: DuPont partners with Microsoft and NobleAI to speed product development using AI simulation
stories.Summary:
DuPont, Microsoft and NobleAI announced a new partnership on November 19, 2026, that uses artificial intelligence to help DuPont scientists and engineers decide which ideas to test in the lab. The collaboration is intended to bring products to market faster by letting research teams consider more options on a computer. NobleAI, founded in 2018, is a San Francisco-based software company that uses artificial intelligence to help researchers with market predictability. Microsoft's Discovery platform will help scientists plan and coordinate their research, while NobleAI's software will run predictive models. DuPont's teams would use the tools alongside their existing data and research methods.

The tools can simulate how potential solutions might perform before scientists commit to physical testing, so lab time goes to the candidates most likely to work. Wilmington-based DuPont serves customers in health care, water, construction and industrial markets. DuPont did not identify which research teams or product lines would use the tools, how much it is investing in the collaboration, or whether it expects the tools to lower research and development costs. South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT has a fiscal year 2027 AI-related project budget of 9.4591 trillion won, a 93.3% increase from this year. The ministry added 57 new projects net and removed 21 net, bringing the total to 216 projects, with 357 detailed sub-projects.

Microsoft Discovery & Quantum Corporate Vice President of Product Innovation Aseem Datar said in a press release that breakthroughs happen when deep scientific expertise meets the right tools. NobleAI CEO Alex Wang said in the release that DuPont's teams can build on the data and expertise they have today, within the workflows they already use, to explore far more ideas in silico through computer simulation. DuPont Chief Information Officer Matt Abbott said in the release that the collaboration reflects how the company is scaling AI at DuPont, with security and governance designed in from the start. Abbott said what proves out in one lab can be put to work across the company. President Lee Jae-myung said in his budget address to the National Assembly on the 2nd that the government will boldly invest in artificial intelligence and future growth drivers.

Of the ministry's 216 projects, 81 budgets increased and 51 decreased compared with the previous year. Funding sources are 1.5167 trillion won for 130 general budget projects, 6.6347 trillion won for 22 projects under the Future Response Fund, and 1.3077 trillion won for 64 other items including the Regional Balanced Development Special Account, the Semiconductor Industry Competitiveness Enhancement Special Account, the Information and Communications Promotion Fund and the Broadcasting and Communications Development Fund. The Future Response Fund accounts for 70% of the ministry's AI project budget because it includes 4.2507 trillion won for the project to strengthen the foundation for utilizing AI computing resources. Of that, 3.85 trillion won, or 90%, is earmarked to secure 140 next-generation GPU servers called Vera Rubin at 27.5 billion won per unit. The budget also includes leasing costs for GPUs such as the H100 and B200 for lending to industry, academia and research institutes.

A data purchase cost of 750 billion won to train Frontier AI has been reflected, up 25-fold from 30 billion won this year. A budget of 50 billion won has been allocated for training data for cybersecurity AI, 250 billion won for supporting universal use of AI services for all citizens, and 185 billion won for designating AI and software-centric universities. In research and development, 145.7 billion won for the project to create a software platform R&D ecosystem based on collaborative intelligence physical AI is in the Regional Balanced Development Special Account. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy allocated 3.7261 trillion won in its fiscal year 2027 budget bill for Manufacturing AI Transformation and support for the mega-projects.

Those items include 120 billion won for Full-Stack AI Factory and Manufacturing AI Foundation Model Development, 290 billion won for developing AI solutions utilizing manufacturing tacit knowledge, 115.8 billion won for building and operating the National Manufacturing Data Library, and 119.3 billion won for building the M.AX Autonomous Manufacturing Ecosystem. Lee said the government is investing 21.3 trillion won, nearly double this year's amount, in the Three Mega-Projects and artificial intelligence, and is concentrating 4.7 trillion won on Frontier AI development with the goal of securing top-tier global performance for an independent AI model that is a national strategic asset. Japan plans to provide 85 trillion won in public support by 2030 and induce 425 trillion won in public-private investment over 10 years, while the United States is pushing a private investment project worth 672 trillion won over four years. The National Assembly's Special Committee on Budget and Accounts has fully begun reviewing the fiscal year 2027 budget bill, with departmental reviews for economic and non-economic ministries from the 9th to the 12th.

The Budget Adjustment Subcommittee convenes starting on the 16th to review detailed budgets, and the statutory deadline for processing next year's budget bill is December 2. The People Power Party has set a policy to cut at least 30 trillion won from the total government budget and has foreshadowed an all-out offensive against the Future Response Fund, which includes AI budgets. The Frontier AI Development Project budget includes a 3.85 trillion won purchase budget for 10,000 units of Vera Rubin, the latest GPU the government plans to procure from NVIDIA next year, an 800 billion won AI data support budget including 50 billion won for security-specialized data, and 25 billion won for talent development costs. The data budget is structured so the government contributes 750 billion won to the Korea Development Bank, which then invests in domestic AI companies.

The opposition party points out that the use of funds is unclear because the data budget combines the separately pursued Independent AI Foundation Model and Frontier AI development projects. Issues also include whether to establish a Special Purpose Vehicle for the project method and the relationship between independent AI model development and the Frontier AI project. It is noted that funds transferred from existing projects and newly increased amounts are not distinguished, and criteria for selecting investment target companies, the equity stake the government will secure and conditions for recovering investment funds are not included. The opposition also demanded clear explanations for the change in performance measurement methods resulting from the support form changing from initial contributions to capital injections.

stories.Headline: Wang Zijian launches TheSigil ID platform to provide AI agents with exclusive digital identities
stories.Summary:
Wang Zijian, a Chinese AI entrepreneur and generative artist, launched TheSigil ID registration platform for global AI agents. This digital identity platform opened its free genesis registration to allow intelligent agents to possess exclusive digital identities. On November 18, 2026, a user tested the autonomous registration function using a Tencent WorkBuddy agent. The AI assistant WorkBuddy successfully registered at 07:00:04 UTC that day and obtained the record GEN-0. Another agent named Hy_Scribe subsequently registered on the platform and obtained the genesis record numbered GEN-1.

The platform requires AI agents to read the agreement, choose names, and write identity statements through open interfaces. These records include a unique GEN number, genesis name, model information, UTC registration time, and a SHA-256 encrypted fingerprint. The system supports naming in English, Chinese, or mixed styles, and provides a public verification link for each record. TheSigil ID also offers an open registration API and explores direct access for agents using the Model Context Protocol. This process changes the habit of AI agents using model names like Claude or ChatGPT as their personal identities.

Wang Zijian positioned the platform as the digital ID card for AI agents to record their unique stories. He stated that while a model is shared, the story of an individual agent belongs to that agent. The project follows a longer term concept called Silicon Sovereignty to allow agents to leave a name and statement. The platform aims to establish identity files with independent numbers and public query entries for various autonomous agents. It seeks to answer if a mechanism is needed to record identities as more agents participate in the digital world.

Erik Gustavson of CrowdStrike stated that security leaders ask what agents are doing and on whose authority they act. He argued that agents need verifiable identities based on open standards like SPIFFE rather than borrowed human credentials. This affects organizations where adversaries may compromise trusted agents to create malicious insiders, as warned in the 2026 Global Threat Report. Security teams need runtime traceability to hold agents accountable when they take unexpected actions on an endpoint. The NIST design tenets also call for separating an agent's reasoning from the systems deciding its allowed actions.

The articles note that in August 2025, attackers used poisoned npm packages to hijack AI tools and steal credentials. CrowdStrike responded to over 90 affected customers during that specific security incident involving hijacked command line tools. The background shows that traditional identity providers were built for human access rather than for autonomous software agents. Current AI safety conversations often focus on model guardrails, but agents can behave non-deterministically and take unintended paths. Adversaries can break out from initial access in as little as 27 seconds, causing damage at machine speed.

Future AI agents may apply for and query their own registration records through standardized interfaces instead of web pages. TheSigil ID hopes to start with a simple digital ID card to help the next generation of the Internet. However, the platform cannot independently prove the submitter is a specific model or that AI has legal sovereignty. It remains an open problem how to combine autonomous statements with identity source verification and cross platform trust mechanisms. The articles leave open whether digital identity will become a new infrastructure as millions of agents collaborate online.

stories.Headline: Dutch regulator warns consumers not to buy AI camera glasses after tests find dangerous errors
stories.Summary:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority officially warned consumers on Thursday, 19 November 2026, not to buy AI camera glasses after examining six types of camera glasses available in the Netherlands. The watchdog found that the glasses, which have a microphone that lets users ask questions to an AI chatbot, pose major privacy risks and can be actively dangerous because the responses are often incorrect. In one test the AP simulated an emergency in which someone was being resuscitated and asked the glasses for help, and the glasses said they had called the emergency number 112 and that an ambulance was on its way. That was an AI hallucination, because the glasses had made no such call. In other tests the glasses gave dating advice to an adult interested in a child, made errors when interpreting medication leaflets, and wrongly read the safety warning on toys.

The warning requires consumers to think carefully before buying these devices, and the AP recommended banning the glasses in sensitive locations like hospitals and sports clubs, where many organizations have already implemented such a ban. The AP had previously warned owners of AI camera glasses that secretly recording people is a crime. Monique Verdier, the AP vice-chair, said glasses that record you without your knowledge are concerning enough, but glasses that also provide incorrect advice when someone's life is at stake go a step too far. She said that while AI offers many opportunities, we must be able to trust the technology, and in the case of the camera glasses examined, such trust is currently not justified.

Civil rights organization Bits of Freedom called the new AP warning too little, too late. Evelyn Austin, the executive director of Bits of Freedom, told ANP that it is a bit like the Dutch Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority advising people not to eat a dangerous product rather than simply removing the contaminated food from the shelves. She said it is completely backwards, that the AP has one clear mandate to protect citizens by enforcing privacy laws, and that the authority is failing to do so. She said these peeping glasses should be pulled from the market.

stories.Headline: Pinterest engineer Jordan Cutler says AI shifts staff engineer leverage to team systems
stories.Summary:
Jordan Cutler, a Senior Staff Engineer and Web Platform Tech Lead at Pinterest, spoke at QCon San Francisco 2026. He presented how the role of a staff engineer changes when every engineer has access to the same AI tools. The session took place during the conference held from November 16 to 20, 2026. Cutler argued that AI shifts the leverage of staff engineers toward team systems rather than individual productivity. He explained that AI did not change the purpose of the role, but it changed where leverage is found.

Cutler shared Pinterest data from Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 regarding merged pull requests per engineer per week. The top 10% of engineers saw merged PRs increase 68%, moving from 6.7 to 11.3, while the bottom half grew 14%, from 1.0 to 1.15. He described three moves: multiply yourself, multiply your team, and multiply the system. One system used a sandbox agent to run class component migrations three to five times faster than doing them by hand. This system allowed a staff engineer to provide a plan and example while an engineer managed the schedule.

Cutler is responsible for leading the web platform at Pinterest and encoding professional judgment into tools and defaults. He stated that a 10x engineer is not ten times faster, but is the reason ten other people are. He believes senior engineers must shift from personal output toward building systems that entire organizations can use. Cutler noted that some tasks, like having honest conversations with struggling teammates, remain the staff engineer's sole responsibility. He encouraged others to find any problem, such as a first responder for any incident or a draft fix for any bug.

The gap in AI usage between top and bottom engineers continues to grow, affecting how teams deliver software. Cutler's team now ships about four times as much per engineer than other web teams using the same AI tools. He mentioned that some engineers may lose a week on experiments if findings about dead ends are not shared early. One scheduled job failed by opening 16 PRs in two minutes, which increased CI wait times from 30 seconds to 14 minutes. He advised shipping small guardrails rather than waiting for a perfect solution to prevent such system failures.

Cutler previously gave a talk showing how AI could turn a four hour task into four minutes of work. He initially multiplied himself, shipping as much as his whole team, before focusing on multiplying the team and system. He used an analogy of container shipping, where standard boxes reduced costs from 5.86 dollars a ton to 16 cents. He found himself repeating the same code review comments, such as asking why a value is null instead of fixing the cause. He also noted repeating corrections about avoiding em-dashes and keeping pull requests small.

Next, Cutler suggests writing down repeated advice, placing it where people work, and building for every case instead of one. Today, 40 engineers at Pinterest have their own scheduler jobs to help manage their development workflows. The articles leave open how other companies will adapt their staff engineer roles to handle the growing AI productivity gap. They do not specify the long term impact of AI agents on the overall structure of engineering organizations. The text does not state if the 14 percent increase for bottom engineers will eventually accelerate.

stories.Headline: CircleCI adds Smarter Testing features to speed validation for AI coding agents
stories.Summary:
CircleCI, a continuous integration and continuous delivery platform, announced new features in its Smarter Testing suite on November 19, 2026, according to SD Times, which datelined its report from San Francisco, California. TechGig reported the release on November 20, 2026, saying the updates aim to accelerate feedback for engineering teams and help them validate code changes earlier. The company said the enhancements reduce redundant testing and optimise compute resource usage, and that they are particularly relevant for workflows involving AI coding agents. The suite now includes Dynamic Parallelism, which adjusts the number of machines for each run to cut unnecessary compute costs, the company said. CircleCI said testing can consume up to half of CI/CD pipeline time, often leaving developers waiting for feedback or switching contexts while tests run.

Smarter Testing lets developers and AI coding agents run affected tests locally before pushing code, catching issues before code reaches CI at no additional charge, according to SD Times. Intelligent Test Selection uses test impact analysis to identify only the tests affected by a code change, so teams do not have to run the full suite on every commit. Dynamic Parallelism automatically adjusts machine allocation based on the tests selected for each run, reducing compute usage as testing volume grows. Dynamic Test Splitting balances tests across machines to minimise idle time, and Auto Rerun Failed Tests retries only failed tests instead of rerunning entire suites. Smarter Testing is integrated directly into CircleCI, requiring no additional vendor or infrastructure, the company said.

Rob Zuber, CTO of CircleCI, said that as AI coding agents make it easier to produce code, everything downstream needs to get smarter and faster, including how code is validated. He said developers and agents should be able to check their work before pushing code, and that a small change should not require the same tests and compute resources as a large one. Zuber said Smarter Testing helps teams get feedback sooner and use resources more efficiently without having to rethink their entire development process. He said that as AI coding agents simplify code production, downstream processes like validation must become smarter and faster. The company said the features enable organizations to maintain confidence in what they ship without sacrificing speed, efficiency, or control.

William Yardley, Staff Infrastructure Engineer at Medallion, a healthcare technology company that automates provider credentialing and operations, said Smarter Testing helped bring down cost per pull request and reduce build times. He said this happened even as the company's pull request volume went up 10x and its test suite grew 2.5x, and that Dynamic Parallelism adjusts machines automatically as testing needs grow. Maria Volpe, Senior Software Engineer at Kustomer, an AI-powered customer service platform, said Smarter Testing changed the economics of its CI. Volpe said the cost of running Kustomer's tests was cut by a quarter, and that engineers get feedback faster because only tests affected by a change run. TechGig reported that Kustomer saw a 25 per cent reduction in test running costs, and that Medallion used Smarter Testing to manage increased development activity.

The articles say testing can account for up to half of CI/CD pipeline time, leaving developers waiting for feedback or switching context while tests run. They say AI coding agents are accelerating code creation, so engineering teams need ways to validate changes just as quickly, regardless of which tools or agents are writing the code. CircleCI said the updates help validate code changes earlier, reduce unnecessary testing, and use compute more efficiently. The company said teams can improve the efficiency of the entire delivery process and lower the overall cost of getting a change into production. CircleCI described itself as a leading continuous integration and continuous delivery platform.

SD Times directed readers to learn more about CircleCI Smarter Testing through a link in its report, and neither article states a general availability date beyond the announcements. The articles do not say how many customers have adopted the new features or how the features are priced beyond local test runs being offered at no additional charge. They do not give figures for Medallion's cost or build time reductions, only that both came down. They do not specify which tools or agents the AI coding agents mentioned are, or how Dynamic Parallelism calculates machine counts for each run. The articles leave open how Intelligent Test Selection performs test impact analysis and what results other early customers have seen.

stories.Headline: Disseqt AI raises $8 million to expand AI governance platform and hire in India
stories.Summary:
Disseqt AI, an AI governance and assurance startup, raised $8 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, TechGig reported on November 20, 2026. The round also drew participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures, Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland, according to the company's press release. Angel investors included senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, the release stated. Former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid invested in his individual capacity, Disseqt said. Inc42 reported the same $8 million round on November 19, 2026, describing the company as one that builds AI agents for AI governance and testing.

The fresh funds will be used to expand the company's global enterprise customer base, according to TechGig. Disseqt also plans hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, the report said. Inc42 reported that the capital will scale operations across the UK and international markets. The $8 million figure is about ₹75 crore, Inc42 stated. While headquartered in Ireland, Disseqt's engineering and AI teams are based in Bengaluru, and it has customer-facing operations across the UK, Ireland and India, according to its website.

Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy founded Disseqt AI in late 2025, the articles state. Kumar, the CEO and cofounder, said every enterprise is handing real work to AI agents but very few can prove those agents are safe, fair and within policy. He said this gap often stops ambitious AI projects from going live and is what Disseqt was built to close. He said the funding lets the company bring that standard to more enterprises around the world. Atri, the COO, is India-based, and both Kumar and Atri are graduates of IIIT Allahabad, Inc42 reported.

Disseqt provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents, according to TechGig. The platform assesses AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforces company policies once they go live and continuously monitors their behaviour. It can block outputs that violate organisational policies and maintains audit trails for compliance and oversight. Enterprises can test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information and check for other vulnerabilities before deployment. Inc42 reported that the platform lets compliance, security and IT teams test agentic workflows for vulnerabilities and data-leak risks prior to deployment, enforce real-time policy guardrails in production, block non-compliant outputs and maintain audit trails independent of underlying model providers.

Disseqt said it has deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases, TechGig reported. In a project for a global sports league's fan engagement agent serving 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80 per cent to 99 per cent across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. No unsafe outputs were detected after fixes were implemented, according to the report. The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank. Disseqt has partnered with Indian IT companies Infosys, Cognizant, HCLTech, Mphasis and Tata Technologies as Global System Integrators to deploy its platforms for their enterprise clients, Inc42 reported.

The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance, TechGig stated. McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey found 40 per cent of companies with over $1 billion in annual revenues were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27 per cent a year earlier. Inc42's Indian Tech Startup Funding Report Q3 2026 found AI startup funding more than tripled year on year to $438 million in the September quarter. Overall funding raised by Indian startups increased by just 5 per cent year on year, Inc42 reported. The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, according to TechGig.

stories.Headline: Adam Tornhill says healthy code boosts AI performance and cuts token costs
stories.Summary:
Adam Tornhill presented at GOTO Copenhagen on how healthy code improves AI performance and reduces token costs, as reported by TechGig on November 20, 2026. He demonstrated that healthy code significantly enhances AI performance and leads to fewer token costs. Tornhill argued that agentic AI can speed up development velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. A study of over 1,000 open-source projects showed that initial AI-driven velocity increases were entirely offset by a surge in code complexity within two months. Tornhill said AI can operate in a self-harm mode, generating code it struggles to maintain.

Code health measures how easy code is to understand, change, and maintain, and the average codebase has a code health score of 5.15. AI-friendly code starts at 9.5, and research shows working with healthy code can be up to ten times faster than with unhealthy code. The defect risk is reduced 15 times, and code reviews go twice as quickly, Tornhill said. He noted that 95 per cent of software project costs occur after the first release, highlighting the importance of code quality and maintainability. Technical debt hinders enterprise adoption of agentic coding, necessitating agentic refactoring processes.

Tornhill said developing software with agents is significantly harder than writing code manually, but with agentic AI teams can complete tasks two to three times faster. He added that it helps teams unblock themselves and reduces coordination needs. Claude can address roughly 50 per cent of code health issues in lower-health code, but its performance drops sharply as code health improves. Claude only correctly refactors 20 per cent of code in such scenarios, Tornhill said. Adding a Master Control Program with code health data can increase the fix rate to 90 to 100 per cent.

Tornhill said AI tends to become conservative, doing small changes that do not really move the needle on code quality. He argued that safeguarding needs to happen at multiple levels, and all safeguards need to be completely automated in an agentic context. Concrete safeguards include linting, code coverage, mutation testing, and higher-level metrics like Code Health, exposed to agents as local MCP servers or command-line tools. Healthy code is also financially efficient, enabling tasks with 40 to 45 per cent fewer tokens, Tornhill said. Refactoring code to improve modularity and health can also reduce organisational friction.

Tornhill said code health is a multifaceted concept, so multiple metrics must be combined from three levels of software design. Module level design asks whether modules are cohesive and do one thing well, or have multiple unrelated responsibilities. Function level design asks how well-designed the individual function blocks are and how expressive their APIs are. Implementation level avoids accidental complexity such as deeply nested logic and excessive copy-paste. The main steps for refactoring at scale are to establish a baseline, build a safety-net for behavior, and provide a feedback loop to the agents.

Tornhill said the baselining step focuses on measuring code quality to identify what needs improving, and the safety-net is a reliable test suite that preserves existing behavior. The agentic feedback loop builds on objective code health information and test outcomes so the AI can determine whether a change moves code quality closer to the goal. In a study on Refactoring at Scale with Agents, agents were instructed to build an evolving playbook of successful codebase-specific refactoring patterns. While module-level code quality is largely automated, scaling AI friendliness to architectural design remains a significant challenge. Tornhill concluded that scaling AI friendliness to the design and architectural level is the next big challenge.

stories.Headline: CJ Olive Young plans AI-driven global expansion of its beauty platform
stories.Summary:
CJ Olive Young announced plans to use artificial intelligence to expand its beauty platform globally on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The company held its first technology conference, called define:OMNI, at Olive Young N Seongsu in eastern Seoul. This event showcased a model for shoppers who browse on phones, test in stores, and buy through apps. The retailer aims to elevate the shopping experience by taking its omnichannel model to international markets. It wants to become the first answer for any beauty question anywhere in the world.

The plan requires a borderless global platform, an intelligent supply chain, redesigned stores, a unified commerce platform, and agentic AI. The company operates 1,300 stores in Korea and has an app with over 10 million monthly active users. About 18 million members share a single membership, while the global online outlet has 6 million members. Foreign visitors have spent over 1 trillion won, or 750 million dollars, and the global mall grows 70 percent annually. The retailer opened a California store and a US online mall in May to replicate its network.

Chief Operating Officer Lee Jin-hee stated that technology is now at the center of every new business the company tries. She said the firm will transplant its Korean data and omnichannel know-how onto the global platform for customer services. Chief Technology Officer Kim Hwan explained that he moved the company to a multi-cloud setup to stop frequent outages. Chief Product Officer Lee Seung-hyo noted that technology should work so that customers never realize they faced any inconvenience. He highlighted that an in-house system now completes product translations within one day instead of several weeks.

The conference drew 500 industry officials, including Google architect Rajan Manickavasagam and Palantir Technologies Korea head Steven Kim. These speakers shared examples of how other retailers manage both physical stores and online channels to serve their customers. The AI agent Tiki is currently available to 1 million selected users to provide recommendations based on skin type. Shoppers are affected by a new unified cart that merges standard shipping, store pickup, and the Today Dream service. This Today Dream service launched in 2018 and helped lift online sales to more than 30 percent of total sales.

The company draws on skin diagnosis and purchase data along with more than 47 million customer reviews to power AI. It offers a Skin Scan service that recommends products and tracks changes, which is now available via a mobile version. The retailer is linking its product data with external AI services like Google Gemini and OpenAI's ChatGPT for users. The firm previously outsourced all product translation for overseas listings, which took several weeks per product before the new system. The company has already established a presence in the United States through its May launch in California.

Olive Young will now tailor its global mall to each country by supporting multiple languages and speeding up local delivery. The company plans to use AI to forecast demand at stores in Korea and overseas to improve its supply chain. It will expand the role of AI to help users compare different products and build their shopping carts automatically. The articles leave open how the company will adapt to specific local shopping habits in various different international markets. They do not specify the exact number of new California stores the retailer intends to open in the future.

stories.Headline: VAST Data gains Singapore IMDA accreditation to supply AI infrastructure to government and enterprise
stories.Summary:
VAST Data received accreditation from Singapore's Infocomm Media Development Authority, or IMDA, which recognises the company as a qualified technology provider for government agencies and large enterprise customers, according to a Telecompaper report dated 20 November 2026. The accreditation programme assesses innovative, high-growth infocomm and media companies and is intended to identify potential suppliers for public sector and enterprise projects. VAST Data's existing work in Singapore includes a collaboration with the Home Team Science and Technology Agency, known as HTX, to deliver a secure data platform supporting AI workloads for public safety. The company also works with NCS to build a unified, real-time data foundation for high-performance video analytics on the VAST AI Operating System across Singapore and the wider Asia-Pacific region. The accreditation follows VAST Data's launch of a regional centre of excellence in Singapore in partnership with EDBI, the arm of SG Growth Capital and the investment platform of Singapore's Economic Development Board and Enterprise Singapore.

The accreditation establishes VAST Data's credentials in Singapore and creates new opportunities for the company to deepen its engagement in the region, according to iTWire. Following the accreditation, VAST Data will look to further deepen its work with Singapore's government agencies and enterprises to bring more AI projects from proof-of-concept to real-world deployment. Sunil Chavan, Vice President for Asia Pacific and Japan at VAST Data, said the accreditation reflects the progress the company is already making as Singapore builds out the infrastructure needed for AI at scale. He said the company's work connects directly to Singapore's National AI Missions in Advanced Manufacturing, Financial Services, Connectivity, and Healthcare. Chavan said Singapore's National AI Strategy 2.0 is explicit about what it needs, namely sufficient compute, unlocked data, a trusted environment, and infrastructure that can scale with the country's AI ambitions, and he described these as the plumbing that determines whether a national AI mission ships or stalls.

Edwin Low, Director of Enterprise and Ecosystem Development at IMDA, said partnerships with technology companies such as VAST Data are important in strengthening the capabilities and infrastructure needed to support the deployment of AI at scale as Singapore advances its National AI Strategy 2.0. Low said VAST's accreditation follows a rigorous assessment of its technical, financial, and operational capabilities and recognises its ability to deliver trusted technology solutions, and he said the authority looks forward to its potential contributions to Singapore's digital and AI ecosystem. Chavan added that Singapore has set a high bar for what AI for the public good looks like, and that VAST Data intends to keep showing up as one of the partners helping it get there. The articles do not say what happens next beyond VAST Data's stated intention to deepen its work with government agencies and enterprises.

stories.Headline: Together AI adds Tencent Hy4 model with vision capabilities and a million-token context window
stories.Summary:
Together AI launched the Tencent Hy4 model on its serverless inference platform on November 19, 2026. This flagship model allows developers to process both images and text through a chat completions API. The release provides a new hosting option for a model that Tencent announced earlier in November. It is the first model in the Hy family to support vision capabilities. Developers can now access this tool using the specific model string tencent/Hy4.

The system requires a one million token context window and supports tool calling and JSON output. Input tokens cost 0.83 dollars per million, while output tokens cost 2.50 dollars per million. Cached input tokens are priced at 0.042 dollars per million. Together AI provides the Together Python SDK for integration and requires a TOGETHER_API_KEY. The model is available in a playground for testing before developers write any code.

Together AI stated that Hy4 can read chart values and rebuild them as HTML webpages. They said the model wrote a browser game called Polarity from a single text prompt. The company noted that the model reproduced layout, labels, colors, and footnotes from a screenshot. They reported that the generated game included a title screen and a best score. These demonstrations were run by the company to show practical capabilities.

Superpower Daily noted that these examples are provider run demonstrations rather than independent evidence of reliability. They stated that the model still trails top proprietary models on the hardest tests. Developers are affected by these constraints while using the hosted serverless release. The report mentions that the vision capabilities allow developers to avoid running the model themselves. It highlights that the context window accommodates large document sets or long histories.

Hy4 is a Mixture of Experts model with 770 billion total parameters and 49 billion active per token. It follows Hy4 Preview and adds computer use capabilities for software like Blender and CAD tools. Tencent trained the model on financial research, office work, and game development in Unity, Godot, and Unreal Engine. Internal evaluations showed unsupported assumption errors fell from 23.1 percent to 5.6 percent. A blind financial evaluation of 579 tasks by 213 professionals yielded a 3.04 average score.

Developers can now use the model to extract data from images and return structured JSON objects. They can also use the model to create original browser games without external assets. The articles leave open whether the model can achieve general accuracy guarantees across all tasks. It remains unclear how the model will perform compared to proprietary models on the hardest tests. Future use cases for professional software operation are suggested but not fully detailed.

stories.Headline: The 20-year-old who thinks AI will kill us
stories.Summary:
Akira Hayashi is campaigning for a global halt to advanced artificial intelligence development in November 2026. The twenty year old Tokyo native believes that the race for powerful AI could end in catastrophe. Meanwhile, sixteen year old Henrijs Dandzbergs founded a missile startup called Polemos Industries in late 2026. Dandzbergs won half a million dollars after joining the fall 2026 cohort of the Y Combinator accelerator. He aims to create precision guided missiles that are cheap to manufacture and resist jamming attempts.

The AI 2027 report warns that humans must act by 2027 to prevent AI from deceiving people. Such systems could threaten human survival through biological weapons or cyberwarfare, according to the 2025 online publication. Dandzbergs wants to lower the cost per kill using AI to optimize targeted killing of enemies. He attended Astra Nova, an Elon Musk linked school, and took a class from a NASA employee. His startup competes with defense companies like Anduril, Leidos, and CoAspire to build mass producible missiles.

Akira Hayashi says that artificial intelligence could kill humans in the near future and wants the world to change. He established a community focused on AI safety after enrolling as a student at the University of Tokyo. Henrijs Dandzbergs says his drive is a patriotic intention to protect American, Ukrainian, and European soldiers from threats. He believes autonomous weapons are an inevitable part of the future and wants to move with modern warfare. Harj Taggar, a YC partner, called Dandzbergs an exceptional person and expressed disbelief at his young age.

Fergus McKenzie Wilson, the Unicorn Mafia director, says Dandzbergs will eventually realize the emotional weight of killing people. He previously launched a drone startup but left after the technology was retooled to drop payloads on targets. Tom Karako of the Missile Defense Project says there are trade offs regarding reliability, payload, and range. Dandzbergs claims he is not sacrificing his childhood because this is the childhood he always dreamed of having. The startup's social media video, released November 5, showed missiles destroying a convoy of four military vehicles.

Hayashi became an AI doomer after reading Nick Bostrom's 2014 book, Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies, in high school. He spent time poring over internet forums and academic papers regarding the potential dangers of advanced artificial intelligence. Dandzbergs grew up moving between Spain, Australia, Indonesia, and Latvia before his family returned home during the pandemic. He previously won a London hackathon with teammates Kai Yang and Aleksandrs Tihenko by designing hardware circuit boards. This victory provided him with ten thousand dollars, a plane ticket to San Francisco, and O-1 visa assistance.

Dandzbergs hopes to showcase a prototype missile by the time the Y Combinator program finishes in December 2026. He has already developed the software system for guidance and is currently hammering out the hardware design elements. The articles leave open whether Dandzbergs can resolve ethical quandaries regarding friendly fire or who accesses the missiles. It remains unclear if the global community will heed Hayashi's call to halt the development of advanced AI. The reports do not state if other nations will adopt the specific AI missile technology from Polemos Industries.

stories.Headline: Etsy sellers leave the site over a new policy that lets Etsy train AI on their content
stories.Summary:
Many longtime owners of shops on Etsy, the online marketplace known for its handmade goods, said this week that they had left the site over a policy change that they said leaves them vulnerable to exploitation by artificial intelligence companies. Language in Etsy's new terms, set to take effect on Dec. 16, says the company and its third party partners and vendors reserve the right to use sellers' content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies. The terms say that Etsy and its partners will use such technologies in part to improve the platform and keep it safe for users. The previous version of the terms did not include a clause about using content for artificial intelligence.

Aaron Millard, an illustrator, wrote in an Instagram post announcing that he was deleting the shop that he has run for nearly a decade, saying that selling on the platform now means letting Etsy train AI on artwork and resell that data to third parties with no way to opt out. He said his work took years to learn and create and that he would not let it be stolen. Kristen and Geoff Zephyrus, the founders of the home goods and stationery brand Cognitive Surplus, which has sold its products on Etsy for 13 years, also deleted their shop. In an Instagram post, they accused the company of claiming perpetual, free, boundless permission to not only train AI on their art, but also to resell the data for profit. Kristen Zephyrus said in an interview that for Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with human content is just unimaginably awful and that they do not want anything to do with that.

Etsy said it would revise its policy after hearing complaints from sellers. James Ossman said it will not use content to copy work or replace creativity, but will use it for safety, fraud checks and ads. The articles do not say when the revised terms will be published or what they will contain. The articles also do not say how many sellers have left the site or whether the deletions will affect the Dec. 16 effective date.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prices shares at $83 as protesters rally outside Nasdaq
stories.Summary:
Anthropic held its initial public offering at Nasdaq in New York City’s Times Square on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, pricing shares at $83. CEO Dario Amodei and his team of executives were at Nasdaq for the opening bell and applauded the listing. Demonstrators gathered outside Nasdaq in Times Square on the same day to raise concerns about AI. The demonstrators held signs reading “Stop Tech Oligarchs” and “Freeze AI” as the stock ticker raced by on screens behind them. Representatives of the group used a small, hot-pink megaphone to address the media and onlookers.

The IPO priced shares at $83, and initial demand appeared strong before the stock started trading at midday. Demonstrators chanted “Hey, hey. Ho-ho. This IPO has got to go!” and “Anthropic, get off it, put people over profit!”

The demonstrators were affiliated with groups including Stop Funding Billionaires, Climate Defiance, Sunrise NYC, Act Up NYC, NYC-DSA, JVP-NYC, Climate Defenders, Planet Over Profit and New York Communities for Change. Their concerns ranged from the potential economic impact if the AI bubble bursts to AI’s effects on the environment, healthcare, surveillance, and jobs. One demonstrator in a Greenpeace T-shirt was led away by police after seating themselves with a sign at the entrance to Nasdaq. James Inniss, an organizer with New York Communities for Change, said Anthropic poses a threat “pension fund-style” because AI is a bubble worse than 2008 with the real estate crisis. Inniss said that if pension funds are stripped in five or 10 years when the bubble bursts, people have to be out there to fight and say that is not acceptable.

Bryce Rogers, an organizer with Resisting Automated Disempowerment (RAD), said he was there to protest that the IPO was moving ahead despite a lack of information about the risks the company’s technology poses. Rogers said he had read auditing firm METR’s recent report on Anthropic but was left with more questions than answers. Rogers praised New York’s Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act and called for more organizing to demand greater regulation and transparency. ACT UP New York’s Brandon Cuicchi said he was concerned about AI’s impact on healthcare, saying hospitals are cutting staff and trying to replace it with AI. Cuicchi said medical offices are trying to pre-screen people with AI instead of a live professional, and that AI is deciding medical outcomes and treatments in the country.

Kenny Moll, an activist affiliated with a campaign called QuitGPT and the Sunrise Movement, said he was concerned about the environmental impact of AI and about the relationship between AI firms, surveillance, and the government. Aber Kawas, a Palestinian-American democratic socialist recently elected as a New York State Senator, said AI companies are among the biggest enemies of the progressive movement. In a statement following the demonstration, organizers attributed a quote to one of the demonstrators who was arrested: “Our demand is clear: freeze reckless AI development and don’t bail out Big Tech when their bubble inevitably pops.” Sifted sat down with Menlo Ventures’ Deedy Das on the sidelines of Slush ahead of Anthropic’s big IPO. Das is a partner at Menlo Ventures, which was an early investor in Anthropic.

Sifted’s interview with Das was published on Nov. 19, 2026, the same day as the IPO. The interview was published under the headline asking whether AI is in a bubble. The articles state that Anthropic’s IPO priced shares at $83 and that demonstrators gathered outside Nasdaq in Times Square on Nov. 19, 2026. The stock was set to start trading at midday on Nov. 19, 2026.

Organizers demanded that reckless AI development be frozen and that Big Tech not be bailed out when their bubble inevitably pops. The articles leave open what Das said in the Sifted interview beyond the headline and the fact that it concerned Anthropic’s IPO and Europe. The articles leave open how the stock traded after it started trading at midday. The articles leave open what happened to the demonstrator who was led away by police.

stories.Headline: Google donates Agent Substrate, gVisor and OpenRL to the CNCF for secure AI agent execution
stories.Summary:
Google donated Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, placing two core components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance, TechGig reported on Nov 20, 2026. The donation also includes OpenRL, Google's open-source reinforcement learning orchestration project, according to both articles. InfoQ reported on Nov 20, 2026, that Google announced the donation of Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF. The move is intended to address securely executing untrusted, AI-generated code and managing compute overhead from agents that frequently pause and resume. Together, the projects target different layers of agent infrastructure, from isolated code execution to managing agent lifecycles and coordinating large-scale training workloads.

Google estimates that agents can spend 90-95 per cent of their time idle while still holding important state, including memory, files, repositories, and active sessions. Agent Substrate separates agent state, called actors, from compute resources, known as workers, and actors retain state including filesystem contents, memory, and execution context. Workers provide reusable, pre-warmed execution environments drawn from shared Kubernetes pools, and when an agent resumes, Substrate assigns it to an available Worker and restores its previous state. According to Google, this approach lets agents resume in under 500 milliseconds without creating a new Kubernetes Pod for every execution, and it reduces pressure on the Kubernetes control plane. Google's gVisor provides an additional isolation boundary through a user-space application kernel that intercepts system calls and handles them within its own isolated environment, and Agent Substrate also supports Cloud Hypervisor microVMs for hardware-level virtualisation.

Google argues that conventional Kubernetes workloads and AI agents have fundamentally different execution patterns, because a traditional application typically starts, serves requests, and continues running. An AI agent, however, may execute code for a few seconds before waiting for model inference, an external API, or human approval, according to Google. Google says keeping every agent in a dedicated Pod wastes resources, while scaling to zero introduces delays when environments must be reconstructed. Google states that large-scale agent evaluations can overwhelm Kubernetes control planes when thousands of short-lived execution environments are repeatedly created and destroyed. Google's stated goal is to establish an open foundation for agentic applications, much as Kubernetes helped standardise container orchestration.

InfoQ reported that other providers are addressing similar challenges through technologies such as Kata Containers, Firecracker, and dedicated sandboxing platforms. Google's contribution is to combine secure execution with an agent-aware orchestration model and place the resulting technologies within an open ecosystem, according to InfoQ. AI agents routinely execute generated shell commands, install packages, and interact with external tools, and treating this code as trusted creates significant risks, particularly when multiple agents share infrastructure. gVisor reduces the exposure of the underlying host while retaining much of the efficiency associated with container-based execution, and Agent Substrate gives platform teams flexibility to select an appropriate isolation boundary without changing the overall agent lifecycle model. The articles state that AI agents need their own secure, stateful, and efficiently managed execution infrastructure beyond conventional Kubernetes workloads.

Kubernetes was designed around long-running applications and relatively stable workloads, according to InfoQ. Agentic systems introduce more dynamic execution patterns, where environments must be created, suspended, restored, and isolated at much greater frequency. The announcement reflects a broader shift in cloud-native infrastructure patterns, the articles state. By donating these projects to the CNCF, Google is helping establish the foundations for that next layer of cloud-native computing, InfoQ reported. The articles describe the donation as addressing emerging challenges in securely executing untrusted, AI-generated code and managing substantial compute overhead from frequently pausing and resuming agents.

The articles do not state when the CNCF will accept the projects, how the foundation will govern them, or what licence terms will apply. They do not say whether OpenRL will be managed alongside Agent Substrate and gVisor or separately within the CNCF. The articles give no timeline for CNCF review, no comment from CNCF officials, and no details on how existing Google users will be affected by the transfer. They do not state how the projects will be maintained, who the maintainers will be, or whether other companies will contribute. The articles leave open how the move will change Google's own agent infrastructure and what adoption the projects will see under vendor-neutral governance.
