stories.Headline: AMD opens Lux AI supercomputer at Oak Ridge for Genesis Mission science
stories.Summary:
AMD announced on Nov. 16, 2026 that the Lux SI + HPC supercomputer is open to scientific users at the U.S. Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory. AMD said Lux was developed through a public-private partnership between AMD and the DOE. The system was built by HPE and brings together AMD EPYC processors, AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, AMD Pensando networking and AMD ROCm software. Lux is ranked 14th on today's TOP500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers. Lux provides the first dedicated U.S. AI Factory for the Genesis Mission, the DOE-led initiative to advance AI-driven science.

Genesis Mission projects allocated to run on Lux span AI-assisted fusion power plant design, an AI-based foundation model factory for materials development and advanced manufacturing, and Earth system prediction to forecast water availability, streamflow and river temperature in the Tennessee Valley Authority region. Lux combines AI with high-performance modeling and simulation to expand U.S. capabilities in science, energy and national security. Lux marks the first major addition to DOE's computing infrastructure in support of the Genesis Mission. Lux builds on the computing foundation established at ORNL by the Frontier supercomputer, the first supercomputer to break the exascale barrier. The upcoming Discovery supercomputer will extend this commitment with deeper integration of AI and high-performance computing.

Thomas Zacharia, senior vice president, Global Public Sector and Strategic Partnerships at AMD, said Lux shows what is possible when national laboratories, government and industry work together to advance scientific discovery. Zacharia said bringing high-performance computing and AI closer to researchers helps them explore new approaches to complex problems and make better use of simulation and experimental data. Zacharia said the partnership builds on a strong foundation at Oak Ridge and supports an open, sovereign AI stack with tools that can benefit researchers across the country. Georgia Tourassi, associate laboratory director for Computing and Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, said Lux represents the first major addition to DOE's computing infrastructure in support of the Genesis Mission. Tourassi said Lux will help accelerate the integration of SI, modeling and simulation, and experimental data to advance discovery in areas critical to the nation's energy, economic competitiveness and security.

Trish Damkroger, senior vice president and general manager, HPC & AI Infrastructure Solutions at HPE, said HPE, together with Oak Ridge National Laboratory and AMD, has delivered breakthrough engineering innovation to advance the nation's scientific computing resources. Damkroger said HPE is proud of its continued collaboration and investment in the Genesis Mission to stand up one of its first AI systems. AMD is also working with ORNL to support DOE's American Science Cloud, a national platform designed to extend advanced AI and high-performance computing capabilities across DOE laboratories, universities and mission partners in support of the Genesis Mission. For researchers, Lux provides an opportunity to train and refine models using scientific data, to combine AI with established simulation methods, and to investigate problems that require computing beyond their home institutions. Its delivery extends the AMD and ORNL collaboration behind Frontier into dedicated capacity for AI-driven science.

At SC26 in Chicago, AMD said it now powers 202 systems on the TOP500 list, capturing over 40% total market share. AMD revealed deployment progress for next-generation supercomputers in Finland and France using Instinct MI430X and 6th Gen EPYC "Venice" processors. AMD unveiled a roadmap for next-gen Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC "Venice" processors, with native 288 TFLOPS of FP64 high-precision compute and PCIe 6.0 support, targeting the Scientific AI market including nuclear physics and climate modeling. AMD announced alliances with IBM, PsiQuantum, Cornelis Networks and Rancher Government Solutions, spanning quantum error correction, high-speed interconnects and secure container scheduling. AMD is partnering with IBM and Cornelis to build an open heterogeneous ecosystem, leveraging its exclusive Versal FPGA advantage for Quantum Error Correction hierarchical decoding while challenging NVIDIA's proprietary interconnects with standard Ethernet technology.

The SC26 conference kicked off in Chicago the week of the announcement, following NVIDIA's reveal of its Rubin HPC architecture, slated for 2028, and the 20th anniversary of CUDA. AMD is launching an "Open Heterogeneous Computing" counter-offensive in the national-level supercomputing space. AMD's press release carries forward-looking statements concerning the features, functionality, performance, availability, timing and expected benefits of AMD products, including the Lux and Discovery supercomputers. The release also covers expected benefits of the collaboration among AMD, the DOE and Oak Ridge National Laboratory, including support for the Genesis Mission and the American Science Cloud. The release states that forward-looking statements are based on current beliefs, assumptions and expectations, speak only as of the date of the press release and involve risks and uncertainties.

Researchers and organizations interested in using Lux to advance Genesis Mission research are encouraged to contact ORNL's Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility to discuss their computing needs and applicable access pathways. AMD directs readers to visit the ORNL Lux resource page to learn more about the system and connect with the OLCF team. The articles do not state when Discovery will arrive or what its capabilities will be beyond deeper integration of AI and high-performance computing. The articles do not give the timing or terms of the alliances with IBM, PsiQuantum, Cornelis Networks and Rancher Government Solutions. The articles do not state when the Finland and France systems will be deployed or their full configurations.

stories.Headline: Manipal University Jaipur adds AI and emerging technology electives to five online degree programmes from January 2027
stories.Summary:
Manipal University Jaipur announced significant curriculum enhancements for five of its online degree programmes on November 19, 2026. The university introduced these changes to meet the evolving needs of the professional landscape and modern industry. These updates affect the Master of Business Administration, Master of Computer Applications, Bachelor of Computer Applications, and Master of Commerce. The final programme receiving these enhancements is the MA Economics, which now includes updated elective pathways for its students.

The Academic Council approved these revised curricula, which will officially come into effect during the January 2027 admission session. New electives include Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, emerging technologies, data analytics, finance, and digital business in Jaipur, Rajasthan, India. The online MCom programme will reduce its total credit requirement from 100 to 80 under the NEP-related credit framework. The online BCA programme now introduces six elective pathways, including Full Stack Software Development and Agentic AI and Intelligent Systems. The online MA Economics programme now offers three pathways, including Global Economics and Finance and Public Policy and Development Economics.

The university is responsible for these changes and stated that the initiative aims to strengthen the industry relevance of programmes. They said the enhancements will equip learners with specialised knowledge and skills aligned with the changing demands of the professional landscape. The university believes these updates reflect a commitment to keeping academic offerings responsive to emerging requirements across various professional sectors. They stated that the revised programmes allow learners to explore interdisciplinary domains while building on their foundational academic knowledge. The university intends to enable learners to build relevant competencies, strengthen professional capabilities, and enhance their overall career readiness.

Learners in the online MBA programme are affected and can now choose Artificial Intelligence for Business as a new elective. These students can also select one elective for super specialisation or two electives for a dual specialisation for flexibility. MCA students are affected by new options in Next-Generation Technologies, Business Analysis, and Enterprise Resource Planning and Digital Transformation. These students can also study Generative AI and Agentic Systems alongside existing options like Cloud Computing and Cyber Security. MCom students are affected by new pathways in Accounting, Taxation, and Global Financial Reporting, and Banking, Fintech, and Digital Financial Services.

Manipal University Jaipur was established in 2011 as a multidisciplinary university committed to providing quality education across many diverse disciplines. Its online degree programmes are UGC-entitled and are recognised as being at par with the corresponding on-campus degree offerings. The university currently offers nine degree programmes in the online mode to a community spanning over 85 different nationalities. These learners come from more than 7,000 towns and cities across India and attend live interactive classes with experienced faculty. The university also provides placement assistance through skill assessments, industry-readiness sessions, resume-building support, and various virtual placement drives.

The university will implement these revised curricula starting with the admission session that begins in January of the year 2027. Graduates will use these new competencies to navigate a professional environment that is becoming increasingly driven by new technology. The university will continue its efforts to enhance the quality, relevance, and flexibility of its online higher education offerings. The articles do not state when the university will next review the curricula or if more programmes will be added. They also leave open whether the credit reduction for the MCom programme will be applied to other online degrees.

stories.Headline: Orangeburg lawmaker Gilda Cobb-Hunter hosts forum on artificial intelligence and data centers
stories.Summary:
State Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter hosted a public education forum on artificial intelligence and data centers at Orangeburg-Calhoun Technical College in Orangeburg, South Carolina. The forum was held on November 20, 2026, according to WRDW and WIS. The University of Dubuque hosted a public forum on the potential benefits and drawbacks of artificial intelligence and data centers on Tuesday night, November 17, 2026, in Dubuque, Iowa. Students spent the semester researching data centers from several perspectives. The Orangeburg forum followed Orangeburg County's September approval of a moratorium halting new data center development and applications for at least 12 months.

The Orangeburg forum aimed to bring community members together to learn about the technology before making quick judgements. Elected officials, technology professionals and infrastructure representatives participated in the discussion. Warren Harley, general manager of the city of Orangeburg's Department of Public Utilities, said no plans are in motion for a data center at this time. Harley said any data center seeking to use the utility's system would pay the cost of service rather than passing it on to customers. The University of Dubuque students researched data centers' potential impact on water use, energy demand, land use and the environment, as well as ethical and public policy concerns.

Cobb-Hunter said she suspects many people, like her, are using the technology without really recognizing it. She said the point of the evening was to connect the dots, educate the community and enable informed decisions. Harley said whatever is done with respect to data centers or any big customer must not negatively impact the system or the customers served, from a rate perspective and a cost perspective. Harley said any data center looking to come onto the system will pay whatever cost it is to serve, and the utility will not pass that on to the customer. Donavan Tann, an English professor at the University of Dubuque, said the technology is inevitable and communities have to learn how to live with it.

Tann said he hopes people leave the event with a sense that the community gets to decide what that looks like. Tate Glaspie, who examined the potential environmental impacts of data centers, said communities must weigh the benefits of the technology against its potential consequences. Glaspie said it could be a huge beneficial thing to overall improve the quality of life, but the main concern is whether a huge aspect of quality of life is being sacrificed to make life simpler and more convenient. Glaspie said it is more of a moral obligation to take into account all factors that could potentially harm quality of life in order to make sophisticated and educated decisions. Orangeburg resident Rick Leonard said the discussion changed his thinking about the technology and its potential impact.

Leonard said he is glad a positive step is being taken, not just saying no, and instead saying this might be a great thing and he does not want to miss the boat. Several academic divisions across the University of Dubuque collaborated on the event, including aviation and flight, computing and applied technology, humanities, natural sciences and theology. In addition to student research presentations, the Dubuque forum featured a 90-minute panel discussion and question-and-answer session with three journalists from across the region. The panelists included Dubuque-based freelance journalist Benjamin Fisher, Wisconsin Watch reporter Tom Kertscher and The Gazette's Linn County local government reporter Grace Nieland. The Dubuque forum aimed to help community members better understand the technology and make informed decisions about data center development.

Cobb-Hunter said she is working to host a similar event in the near future. The articles leave open what the Orangeburg moratorium will mean after its at least 12-month period ends. The articles leave open what decisions community members will make about data center development after the forums. The articles leave open what further events Cobb-Hunter will host. The articles leave open what the University of Dubuque will do with the student research presented at its forum.

stories.Headline: Wenge AI adds Google and Apple sign-in options for international ScienceOra users
stories.Summary:
Wenge AI announced a new update for its ScienceOra platform on November 20, 2026. The company added Google and Apple sign-in options for users of its international site. This change happened in Shenzhen, China, to help researchers access the platform. The update streamlines the registration and sign-in process for overseas scientific researchers. It provides a faster and more convenient way to enter the AI for Science platform.

Users can now authenticate using existing Google or Apple accounts instead of lengthy forms. Apple sign-in is currently available on the web version of the ScienceOra platform. The system identifies whether to create new accounts or sign in based on email status. It improves how third-party accounts link and provides clearer prompts for the Hide My Email feature. These changes aim to reduce duplicate registrations and resolve common sign-in friction for users.

Wenge AI is an enterprise AI company that develops proprietary foundation models and platforms. The company was founded by a team of AI scientists from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. They stated that the refinements maintain a consistent account experience for their international users. The firm intends to continue refining the product experience based on the needs of researchers. They aim to make scientific exploration and access to research tools more seamless.

Overseas researchers are affected by these changes to the AI-powered scientific research and decision-support platform. ScienceOra uses the ScienceOne Scientific Foundation Model to bring together data, tools, and specialized research agents. Meanwhile, the Korean Fair Trade Commission is requiring overseas platforms to appoint legal representatives by January 21. This rule affects companies like Apple, Google, Alibaba, and OpenAI to resolve consumer disputes. The FTC official said that failing to comply will lead to immediate investigations.

The FTC rule applies to businesses with global annual sales of at least 1 trillion won. It also covers platforms with at least 1 million average monthly Korean users during a specific period. Another criterion includes businesses that caused significant consumer harm after violating local e-commerce laws. The FTC met with Alibaba, Temu, and OpenAI on October 28 to review industry feedback. These guidelines clarify the obligations for overseas businesses under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.

The FTC will operate a three-month grace period after the system takes effect in January. This period helps companies adjust but does not delay the January 21 appointment deadline. The domestic representative will serve as a formal communication channel for legal notices and investigations. The regulator plans to monitor the implementation of this system and consider further improvements. The articles leave open how many companies will successfully appoint representatives before the deadline.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA and Microsoft partner to build AI-native industry solutions for enterprises
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, NTT DATA deepened its strategic collaboration with Microsoft to build a new generation of AI-native industry solutions for enterprises. Simultaneously, VeriSilicon announced a low-power, high-performance wearable subsystem solution designed specifically for next-generation augmented reality and artificial intelligence glasses in Shanghai. These two separate initiatives aim to advance how artificial intelligence is integrated into both large-scale business processes and wearable consumer hardware. Both companies released these announcements on the same day to highlight their latest technological advancements in the field of artificial intelligence. The efforts focus on moving beyond simple experimentation toward scaled business transformation and efficient computing for advanced wearable device applications.

The NTT DATA and Microsoft effort requires deep industry expertise, scaled forward-deployed engineering capabilities, and frontier technology platforms to succeed. It initially focuses on telecommunications, media, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, automotive, and insurance, utilizing the AI Vista platform and 400 reusable assets. NTT DATA plans to mobilize over 500 Microsoft Frontier engineers globally to work directly with clients and domain specialists. VeriSilicon's solution uses FLEXA subsystem architecture and DECNano compression technology to optimize memory bandwidth, data transfer, and overall computing efficiency. This wearable system integrates the Nano-XR series, including ISPNanoUltra-XR, ISPPico-XR, DCNanoUltra-XR, and GCNanoOptimaV-XR, to handle various processing tasks for glasses.

Edwina Fitzmaurice, Corporate Vice President of Industry Solutions Delivery at Microsoft, stated that combining their resources helps clients reimagine how work gets done. She noted that merging Microsoft's cloud and AI platform with NTT DATA's global engineering scale delivers meaningful business outcomes for their clients. The companies believe that technology alone cannot redesign industry processes without people who understand business workflows, data, and regulatory environments. They argue that AI-native solutions should be designed from the start to solve specific problems rather than adding AI to existing workflows. The goal is to identify where artificial intelligence can fundamentally change how industry-specific work is performed to create new value.

Clients in the insurance sector may be affected by reimagining underwriting and claims processes around decisions that are assisted by artificial intelligence. Manufacturing clients could use real-time operational data and AI to identify quality issues and determine the most appropriate response. Healthcare providers might orchestrate complex workflows while keeping clinicians in the loop, and telecommunications firms could improve network and customer operations. VeriSilicon's technology affects the wearable market by providing smartphone-level photo and video quality with optimized power consumption and silicon area. Their ISPPico-XR specifically supports always-on functions for users, such as gesture recognition and eye tracking, within augmented reality glasses.

NTT DATA and Microsoft have a relationship spanning more than 25 years, supported by 23 advanced specializations and six Microsoft Solutions Partner designations. The company holds more than 24,700 Microsoft certifications and currently has approximately 120,000 Microsoft Copilot users globally, including many users in Japan. They use Microsoft AI internally for marketing, IT service management, and employee productivity to gain firsthand experience in driving AI adoption. VeriSilicon built its new wearable solution on a broad portfolio of low-power processing IPs and previous experience in the wearable market. Their existing IP portfolio includes Neural Network, Video, Digital Signal, Image Signal, and Display Processing Units with various configurable options.

NTT DATA will now apply its codified agent patterns, architecture, and connectors to help clients prepare their IT environments for transformative technologies. They will continue to monitor performance and measure business value while determining where human judgment must remain in the loop. VeriSilicon will offer its comprehensive portfolio of processing IPs to address different power and performance requirements for various glasses applications. The articles leave open how these AI-native solutions will specifically perform across different global geographies and diverse regulatory environments. It remains unclear how VeriSilicon's new subsystem will be integrated into specific consumer hardware brands or the final retail pricing.

stories.Headline: Ouray County commissioners approve the county's first AI policy for employees
stories.Summary:
Ouray County commissioners on Tuesday approved the county's first-ever artificial intelligence policy, the Ouray County Plaindealer reported on November 18, 2026. The guidelines restrict employee use of AI and require training, and they take effect for county employees starting in January. The story was reported by James Hanlon and Gabrielle Porter. The approval came at a Tuesday commissioners meeting. The policy covers how county employees use artificial intelligence tools in their work.

The policy gives Ouray County employees new guardrails for AI use beginning in January. It is the county's first AI policy. It restricts employee use of the tools. It requires training for employees. The commissioners approved it on Tuesday.

Pittsylvania County Schools superintendent Steve Mayhew said the goal is a human-centered policy that is ethical and equitable, protects users and the school division, and provides adequate training for those most in need of it. He said the goal is also for students to develop important life skills and succeed academically without using AI to do the work, while balancing digital literacy and education. He said people use AI for a lot of things and that it is a tool but not supposed to be used instead of creativity. He suggested forming a taskforce on AI and its regulation made up of teachers, principals, division administrators, parents and potentially a school board member. Emily Reynolds, chief information technology officer with Pittsylvania County Schools, said students do not have access to AI and teachers only have access right now to MagicSchool, which is geared toward instructional purposes.

Kevin Mills, Westover district representative, was concerned with AI's reputation for spitting out erroneous information or producing information that aligned with user bias, telling individuals what they want to hear rather than strict facts, and said use of the technology could mislead students trying to use it as a study aid. Mark Shields, school board chair and Chatham-Blairs district representative, said his biggest concern with AI in schools was growing reports of students using AI programs such as ChatGPT to write essays. Kelly Merricks, Dan River district representative, pointed out that if teachers give students assignments to complete on the spot during class, it gives educators the chance to recognize students' authentic work, and that familiarity makes it easier to spot a student's use of artificial intelligence to complete essays or other assignments. The impacts and implications of AI relate not only to students but also to educators. Privacy and security are two major concerns in the dialogue surrounding AI in schools, staff said.

Pittsylvania County Schools has joined other school divisions in Virginia and across the nation in contending with the rise of artificial intelligence and its impacts within the education realm. Division administrators acknowledged that AI is not going anywhere and that school divisions have to craft policy and regulation around its usage, seeking to be strategic, careful and responsible as the technology changes many aspects of life and education. PCS has kept tight reins on unrolling AI in the division so far, administrators said, and that has been much to their benefit as other school divisions in the Commonwealth are trying to rein the technology in. The issue is something IT directors in school divisions everywhere are talking about, Reynolds said. Within MagicSchool, teachers can create AI-resistant assignments for students, and Reynolds said that really is the way, the push, to go, rather than trying to determine whether or not AI was utilized, to teach teachers how to build assignments that are more resistant to a student putting a prompt into a chat bot and getting some type of output of an assignment from that.

While programs do exist where teachers could upload content to see whether it has AI-generated components or not, Reynolds said even that gets murky, because effectively it is AI telling users whether something was AI generated. In the broader education realm, proposals have been made to begin introducing digital citizenship to students beginning in Kindergarten, effectively starting to teach five-year-olds about AI, computer technology and responsible use, and the premise of this push would level up digital literacy and AI education through the grade levels. Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, in part of her administration's recently announced Moving Virginia Forward agenda, aims to target finding a better balance that limits student screen time in school and encourages use of more traditional educational methods where possible, and this agenda is set to get in motion in 2027, per the governor's office. The memo reads that the agenda would require school divisions to minimize unnecessary student screen time, prioritize teacher-led and high-quality instruction, and regularly assess and develop plans to reduce excessive or low-value use of instructional technology. Adopting an AI policy was the first official step into the fray, and regulation and implementation will follow that baseline as the situation develops.

The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors approved a policy Tuesday governing the safe, ethical and transparent use of artificial intelligence technologies across county government. The policy establishes standards, responsibilities and governance requirements for AI systems developed by the county, procured from outside vendors or accessed through third-party platforms. According to a board letter from the county's chief executive officer, AI technologies are increasingly used across county departments to enhance service delivery, improve operational efficiency and support data driven decision making, and as these technologies advance it is critical for the county to maintain clear governance structures, safeguard sensitive information and ensure that AI is deployed responsibly and ethically. The policy requires county departments to follow its terms.

stories.Headline: OpenAI reports its internal agents independently complete 46% of research tasks
stories.Summary:
OpenAI released an internal Agent research report titled “Research acceleration: The jagged frontier” on 2026-11-20, as reported by 36Kr and written by QbitAI’s Wen Le. The report states that Agents within OpenAI can now independently complete 46% of research tasks that originally took humans 2 to 4 hours. In March this year that proportion was only 23%, and in just 7 months it has doubled. For tasks that originally required 4 to 8 hours, the independent completion rate of Agents rose from 13% to 35%. The median daily spending of researchers on Agents rose from 1,500 USD to 2,400 USD.

For the top 10% of heaviest users, single-day usage cost hit 23,000 USD, about 160,000 RMB, up from 11,000 USD. Each researcher can now drive an average of 5.7 Agent workdays per day, with 8 hours of cumulative Agent running time counting as one workday, 11 times the previous benchmark. More than two-thirds of researchers run at least 4 Agents simultaneously daily, and more than 10% of heavy users run at least 16 at once. The equivalent API value of Agents has reached twice the non-equity compensation of researchers, which does not include the large equity portion. Agents perform well on “communication” at 69% and “analysis” at 58%, but lag on “construction” at 43%.

Most respondents said they would give up 40% of their team’s headcount, or 30% of their computing resources, to regain access to the most cutting-edge Agents for the next 3 months. Researchers said the model usually cannot come up with well-defined problems it cannot solve at one time, and one said asking it to “do this task just like that other task” led to being tricked many times. Agents cannot come up with good problems on their own, cannot tell good code from bad, and cannot distinguish high-quality data from low-quality data, and must be watched like a supervisor or they churn out “AI slop.” Human researchers propose ideas, set directions, define problems, make key decisions and conduct final quality control, while Agents act as a superpowered “hand” and “eye.” One researcher said evaluating whether an open source project works well previously took no less than one or two weeks, but now takes one day at most a few days.

The success rate of monitoring training tasks is 79%, but the success rate of writing reasoning and service code is only 25%. When developing GPT-6.2 Astra, the pre-training team for the first time attributed the generation of a key idea to collaborative conversations with Codex, where a researcher proposed the idea and Codex put forward a key modification that made the whole solution work. In 2026 the number of lines of code produced by each active contributor has been increasing sharply compared to the period before 2025. The number of experiments run by each active experimenter has reached 1.68 times the 2025 benchmark. Since August 2025, the frontier of OpenAI model capabilities, measured by OpenAI’s internal capability index (OECI), has increased by 16.4 points per year, exceeding the previous annual industry trend of 14 points.

OpenAI’s report emphasizes that this AI-driven progress may not be linear, and it is necessary to be alert to sudden, leapfrog breakthroughs like those that recently occurred in the field of mathematics. Among all research directions, the field of safety has the largest increase in manpower input and the highest workload growth rate. A large number of researchers, whether newly recruited or transferred internally, are flocking to safety projects. The report’s title refers to a jagged frontier, uneven across different scenarios. The original report is at https://openai.com/index/research-acceleration-jagged-frontier/.

The article is from the WeChat official account “QbitAI,” written by Wen Le, and authorized for release by 36Kr. The article states that its views only represent the author, and the 36Kr platform only provides information storage space services. 36Kr Europe (eu.36kr.com) delivers global business and markets news, data, analysis and video, and lists business@36kr.com for media inquiries, interview requests, business collaboration and recruiting global ecological partners. The article lists Partner: startuprad.io and Friendly Links: ai.36kr.com. The report describes Agents as a top “execution co-pilot” but by no means a “chief scientist.” The article asks whether AI is really accelerating the birth of new AI and whether recursive self-improvement has actually happened.

stories.Headline: ServiceNow survey finds 92% of Indian organisations faced AI agent security incidents in the past year
stories.Summary:
Attackers now have powerful AI on their side, and AI agents can scan, plan and run intrusions at machine speed, improving every month. The result is more attacks, more often and at global scale, so more companies will face a security incident at some point. What separates them is how they respond, and machine-speed threats call for a modern playbook with 4 pillars. The article shows the trend through 6 months of incidents and looks at a few companies, with Fireworks AI as a model of mature, structurally sound response. Several AI platforms disclosed security incidents between May and November 2026.

The playbook has 4 pillars: detect and contain automatically, communicate fast and securely over out-of-band channels, eradicate thoroughly with outside forensic experts, and keep shrinking the blast radius. In November, Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said AI misuse had reached a "critical inflection point", reporting that attackers use AI to shorten timelines and run multi-stage intrusions at machine speed. CrowdStrike reported that 1 group used AI agents against more than 200 organizations in 11 days, and Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 found attacks moving about 4 times faster than a year earlier. In 2025, Anthropic disrupted a campaign where AI did 80 to 90% of tactical work with little human input. On May 10 and 11, the "Mini Shai-Hulud" campaign altered about 170 npm packages and some PyPI libraries, affecting AI SDKs from Mistral AI and Guardrails AI, and the NHS cyber alert lists the specific versions to avoid.

Klue, a market intelligence platform, disclosed misuse of OAuth tokens it held for customers. Microsoft described intrusions into exposed, unpatched LiteLLM, RAGFlow and Kestra deployments, fixed versions exist for all 3 tools, and CISA had listed the LiteLLM flaw as known exploited on June 8. Anthropic's September threat report described attempts to obtain AI keys through software vendors, and in 1 case instructions were injected into a vendor's automated evaluation sandbox. At least 9 AI developer and hosting platforms disclosed incidents involving stored customer secrets in October, Wiz's tracker later listed further disclosures for 16 platforms in total, and a tampered LiteLLM release, version 1.107.0, was identified with users told to roll back. On November 16, an attacker abused a flaw in Optimizely's account signup flow to inject code into customer projects, reaching 178 organizations' websites according to Report URI, including HSBC, Salesforce, the BBC and Ledger, and the code swapped crypto wallet addresses and skimmed payment forms.

Optimizely removed the payload and fixed the flaw, and Hudson Rock traced similar code through three other web services, beginning November 13. A survey of 500 security leaders by ServiceNow showed that 92 per cent of Indian organisations had an AI agent security incident in the past year, but only 36 per cent of them were able to contain it within 24 hours. Half of the Indian security leaders surveyed described their agentic security as established, but the findings showed uneven foundations, according to the report "Deployed but Ungoverned: The State of Agentic Security in India". Only 19 per cent have a single named individual accountable for agentic AI security governance and 18 per cent have unified, single-interface visibility into their agents. Only 30 per cent enforce an automated deployment gate that blocks agents until they pass security checks, while 47 per cent can produce a complete evidence package on demand.

Kulmeet Bawa, GVP and Managing Director for India and SAARC at ServiceNow, said India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to understand, monitor and govern the agents enterprises deploy. He said knowing what an agent can reach is not the same as seeing what it is doing, and automated controls and continuous oversight will be essential to keeping AI innovation underpinned by trust and cyber resilience. He pointed out that AI agents are now part of how Indian enterprises operate, but security has not kept pace. He noted that every agent should be registered, owned and visible in one place, with controls enforced automatically and responses at machine speed, so that security teams can detect problems and contain them in time. About half of the organisations, 51 per cent, have automated real-time detection for anomalous AI agent behaviour, but 67 per cent cannot automatically act when an agent behaves anomalously.

As many as 37 per cent of organisations discovered AI agents running in production in the last 12 months that were never registered or known to security teams. AI has changed the economics of attacking, and tasks that took skilled people days can now be delegated to agents. The tools keep improving, so the pace will keep rising, and AI infrastructure is an especially attractive target because AI access itself has value. The shift started earlier, and incidents appeared across every layer of the AI stack, together showing how broad the activity has become. The last 6 months show what that looks like.

The articles leave open what happens next beyond the pillars and the calls for registration, ownership and automated controls. They do not say whether the 4 pillars were adopted by any named company or what results followed. They do not give the outcome of the Optimizely incident beyond the payload removal and fix, or say how the Hudson Rock tracing through three other web services ended. They do not state what ServiceNow recommends beyond Bawa's remarks, or whether Indian organisations plan changes after the survey. They give no date for when the pace of AI-powered attacks might change.

stories.Headline: Apple negotiates four to five year DRAM supply deal with Samsung starting 2027
stories.Summary:
Apple is currently in advanced talks with Samsung Electronics to start a long-term DRAM supply contract. This agreement is scheduled to commence in the first half of 2027 and will last four to five years. The company is moving toward these multiyear deals because an artificial intelligence boom is boosting chipmakers. Apple already signed a separate agreement with SK hynix to secure its memory supply for the future. These moves come as bargaining power shifts toward suppliers during an AI-driven shortage of high-bandwidth memory.

The proposed deal with Samsung Electronics guarantees minimum supply volumes, while the final prices are determined by market conditions. SK hynix has secured long-term supply agreements with 14 major global customers, covering over half of its 2027 and 2028 capacity. Samsung signed long-term agreements with 10 major customers last month and is currently negotiating with another 10 different customers. Micron Technology uses five-year contracts that include cash deposits, price floors, price ceilings, and specific take-or-pay clauses for buyers. These strict terms force buyers to pay for committed volumes even if they actually purchase less than the agreed amount.

Industry sources state that memory makers previously adjusted supply volumes and prices to meet the specific demands of their customers. One source noted that chipmakers will likely use long-term contracts to secure stable revenue as AI infrastructure investment continues. Another source explained that buyers must now commit to longer-term purchasing plans to get the volumes they actually need. These sources suggest that the way memory makers and customers do business is changing due to limited available supplies. The shift in power allows suppliers to demand firm commitments and shift the risks of market downturns onto buyers.

Technology firms like Google and Amazon are investing heavily in AI data centres, which drives demand for server DRAM. This prioritization of higher-margin components leaves less capacity for conventional memory used in personal computers and smartphones. TrendForce data shows server DRAM demand rising to 43 per cent this year from 38 per cent in 2025. Meanwhile, the share of total demand for mobile DRAM drops to 32 per cent from 36 per cent in 2025. These market shifts affect how Apple and other device makers must secure the components needed for their hardware.

The articles explain that long-term deals provide clearer visibility over future orders in a sector known for sharp price swings. This background explains why Apple is seeking to lock in its memory supply amidst the current artificial intelligence boom. The rush for supplies is linked to the growing influence of chipmakers like Samsung and SK hynix in the market. High-bandwidth memory is particularly sought after for AI initiatives, creating a shortage that impacts the entire electronics supply chain. This environment encourages the adoption of multiyear contracts to ensure that production needs are met consistently.

Apple and Samsung are now in the final stages of talks to finalize the four to five year supply agreement. The articles leave open whether Samsung's specific deal with Apple will include the strict terms used by Micron Technology. It remains unclear if the final contract will include price floors, ceilings, or the specific take-or-pay clauses mentioned. The reports do not state the exact minimum supply volumes that Apple and Samsung have agreed to guarantee. Future pricing will depend on market conditions, leaving the exact cost of the memory components unknown for now.

stories.Headline: Pontifical Gregorian University forum participants develop solutions for Catholic AI accountability in Rome
stories.Summary:
The Builders AI Forum, an interdisciplinary conference hosted by the Pontifical Gregorian University, held a two-day program of workshops in Rome on Nov. 5-6, 2026, aimed at identifying problems facing Catholic AI development. The forum was formed two years ago and holds annual gatherings in Rome. This year's theme was "Uniting to Shape AI Before It Shapes Us." The gathering brought together church leaders, technology developers, venture capitalists and policymakers from around the world. It took place in the same weekend that Pope Leo XIV spoke to Argentines about the "challenges posed by artificial intelligence and unregulated automation."

The conference examined the lack of human accountability within AI models, potential system biases against particular languages and cultures, and the dangers of treating machines as human persons. Participants then worked together to develop possible solutions for their communities and dioceses. The conference focused on the need for positive action in addition to technology regulations. It emphasized that forming thriving Catholic communities, building responsible and properly sourced AI tools, and calling governments and tech developers to protect human labor are essential tasks for the church today. The forum's theme framed the two-day program of workshops held at the Pontifical Gregorian University.

Matthew Harvey Sanders, founder of the forum and CEO of Longbeard, the company behind AI tools such as Magisterium AI and Vulgate, framed responsible human development of AI as a duty for the church in his opening address. He quoted Leo and called Catholic developers to fill the gaps of agency, instances where AI lacks human oversight and accountability, that are often created by AI developers. Sanders said a machine that can be blamed is a convenient place for everyone above it to leave the blame. He said that before any parish, school or hospital lets an agent act for a person, someone must be able to stop it, and someone must answer for it. Sanders presented a vision for "digitizing the church's patrimony and universalizing access to it" that he has worked to implement through Longbeard's AI products.

Cardinal Michael Czerny, who heads a Vatican commission on artificial intelligence, used an image from Magnifica Humanitas contrasting two biblical construction sites, Babel and Jerusalem, as examples of different ways that technology can be developed. He said both are collective efforts, yet the manner of constructing and the outcome are very different in the two sites. Czerny said the difference between Babel and Jerusalem lies in the desire that guides the act of building. He said the contrast between the two cities presents today's primary question: out of what desire shall we build, deploy and employ artificial intelligence? Sanders told the National Catholic Reporter that he sees AI as an "unfortunate means" to evangelize the world, emphasizing that building authentic Christian community is the ultimate goal.

Sanders said he does not think Catholic AI should need to exist, and that if everyone were well formed and living in good, vibrant Catholic communities, pressing fundamental existential questions would get answered by osmosis. He said the only reason they decided they needed to develop Catholic AI was that they could see a wave of interest in the Catholic faith and were not prepared for the scale. He said their thinking was AI could be a really good instrument in the short term to help ensure people get answers to fundamental questions, but then they need to get this person into community. In his closing speech, Sanders encouraged participants not to stand idle in the face of AI's challenges, but to take action in building communities and technologies that uphold and promote human dignity. Sanders said that a year ago, Pope Leo prayed that this forum's work would bear fruit, and that fruit is something you can see and hold, and it feeds someone.

Leo's encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, called AI "a valuable tool ... [that] calls for a measured and vigilant approach." Leo warned tech developers to "embed values in their projects with due seriousness: with transparency, responsibility toward affected communities and careful attention to ensuring that what is being cultivated is a genuine good." Leo's Nov. 6-17 Latin America trip included a stop in Argentina, where he spoke to representatives of the country's work community about the dignity of labor and the dangers of encroaching technology.

On Nov. 8, the pope addressed workers, business and trade union leaders, and teachers and students at the Catholic University of Argentina in Buenos Aires. Leo reminded the crowd of "the dignity of the human person ... [who] is the author, the center and the goal of all economic and social life." Leo warned that "the challenges posed by artificial intelligence and unregulated automation can put countless jobs at risk and become a real threat to proper integral human development."

The pope's address came as Argentina's Congress considers legislation submitted by the Javier Milei administration that would grant legal recognition to companies operated solely by AI. Milei's proposed legislation comes after an announcement last October that a massive AI data center project, Stargate Argentina, will be constructed in Patagonia. The articles leave open what the forum's participants will do with the solutions they developed for their communities and dioceses. They also leave open the outcome of Argentina's Congress consideration of the Milei administration's legislation on companies operated solely by AI.

stories.Headline: Lenovo beats revenue estimates with 48 percent growth driven by AI sales
stories.Summary:
China's Lenovo reported a forty eight per cent increase in second quarter revenue on November 19, 2026, due to strong artificial intelligence sales. The company earned US$30.2 billion, which exceeded the LSEG consensus estimate of US$27.6 billion based on six analysts. This growth was driven primarily by hardware and servers, with AI related revenue climbing seventy nine per cent to US$10.8 billion. These AI sales now represent thirty six per cent of the total revenue for the group.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group achieved its strongest quarter ever as revenue for data centre equipment rose one hundred seventy eight per cent to US$11.3 billion. The division for smartphones, tablets, and personal computers grew fifteen per cent and accounted for roughly sixty per cent of total revenue. Under Hong Kong accounting standards, the company posted a net loss of US$640 million compared to a profit of US$340 million last year. However, adjusted net profit rose one hundred sixty six per cent to US$1.4 billion after removing non cash items.

These adjusted figures exclude costs related to convertible bonds and warrants issued during a strategic partnership with the Saudi Arabian technology firm Alat. The company attributed its success to high demand for AI servers and the technical capabilities of its hardware divisions. Lenovo also noted that the Asia Pacific region contributes a reasonable part of its US$21 billion AI server pipeline. The company continues to expand its reach through initiatives like a twenty four month accelerator for startups based in Singapore.

stories.Headline: Viz.ai and rural health group run AI education events for hospitals
stories.Summary:
Viz.ai, an artificial intelligence disease detection and care coordination platform, entered a partnership with the National Rural Health Association about seven months before HLTH 2026, which the organizations marked at the conference in November 2026. Viz.ai Chief Clinical Officer Andrew Ibrahim discussed the collaboration with Fierce Healthcare at HLTH, describing its first year and his goals as it approaches the one-year mark. Since the partnership began in April, the two organizations have held three educational events for rural health systems. These sessions aim to show rural health administrators the specifics of AI tools and help them decide whether to adopt such technology.

Ibrahim said many rural hospitals lack the information technology expertise and infrastructure to adopt some AI tools, and he described the partnership as a force function to strengthen their hub and spoke relationships. He said it has been beautiful to see those relationships strengthened with the AI tool as the conduit, giving the hospitals a reason to interact more and a way to build their capabilities. In addition to the educational series, frameworks are in development to help rural health systems navigate, implement and deploy AI, and those frameworks will be built into a toolkit. One of Ibrahim's personal goals for the partnership's one-year mark is to ensure any rural health administrator can understand what an AI tool is when it is pitched to them. He said getting to 100% of hospitals at year one would be ideal but probably unrealistic, calling it the ultimate goal.

For measuring the collaboration, Ibrahim said he is looking for numbers showing that participants are keeping more care local and retaining their workforces. He said it would be great to connect the dots and understand whether adoption of an AI tool gives rural clinicians confidence, enthusiasm and a willingness to stay in their community rather than dropping services and moving back. Ibrahim also pointed to a new Viz.ai partnership with Wolters Kluwer Health to integrate the Viz.ai One platform into UpToDate Expert AI, which he said has disproportionate benefit in rural communities. He said he is excited about bringing that level of clinical decision support into rural hospitals.

stories.Headline: Chinese internet giants push AI short dramas to the global cutting edge
stories.Summary:
Chinese internet giants pushed AI short dramas to the global cutting edge by 2026. This industry evolved from small workshops to film level production over eight years. AI now empowers these dramas to reach a state of cyber ascension. One popular AI drama this year gained 6.6 billion views without real actors. These platforms now dominate the leisure time of many Chinese people.

The market size exceeded 50 billion yuan in 2024, surpassing the total Chinese film box office. By 2025, viewers exceeded 600 million, with over half of internet users watching. In 2026, the market exceeded 100 billion yuan and viewers surpassed 800 million. The Hongguo App daily active users surpassed iQiyi, Youku, Tencent Video, and Mango TV. These figures show the rapid growth of the short drama sector.

Internet giants are responsible for this growth as part of a commercial war. They view the short drama sector as a game between competing platforms. These companies use quantified advertising indicators to create highly addictive, formulaic content. They focus on hooks, emotional pushes, and suspense to retain their audiences. The platforms hold the power of traffic distribution and make steady profits.

Traffic placement operators are affected because they determine if a producer makes money. They edit clips for specific audiences, such as young women or agricultural video lovers. If the return on investment is lower than 70 percent, placement is stopped. Producers and placement companies only take 10 percent of the total market revenue. The platforms take 90 percent of the revenue through traffic placement fees.

The industry began with advertisements like the Crooked Mouth Dragon King in 2020. These ads used real people to perform exciting plots from online novels. Platforms like Qimao, Fanqie, and Midu provided free novels and monetized through ads. This model used short videos on Douyin and Kuaishou to attract users. Entrepreneurs from advertising distribution then flooded the marginal short drama market.

Next, companies will integrate production and placement to try and increase their revenue. They will continue using specific timing units, like reversals every three seconds. Some memes from these dramas may appear in next year's Spring Festival Gala. The articles leave open how producers can earn more than 10 percent. They do not say if AI will replace all real actors.

stories.Headline: Anthropic lists on Nasdaq at $1.5tn valuation and raises a record $107bn
stories.Summary:
Anthropic became a listed company on Thursday, 19 November 2026, when its shares began trading on the Nasdaq in New York. Dario Amodei, the co-founder, rang the Nasdaq MarketSite opening bell with his sister and fellow co-founder Daniela at the start of trading. The shares were priced at $83 each, above the indicated range of $70 to $78, and began trading at £111.50. The listing raised $107bn, a record sum, and the company was valued at $1.5tn at the listing price. At the opening trading price its market capitalisation reached $2tn, and only 14 months earlier it had raised money at a valuation of $183bn.

The prospectus detailed $900bn of spending commitments for computing power and infrastructure, and $26bn of the listing proceeds came from a cornerstone placement. That placement went to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC, and the banks collected $550m of underwriting fees. Anthropic is loss-making, with projected revenues in 2026 of $50bn-ish, and tech analysts have pencilled in roughly $600bn of revenue in 2030. Nasdaq entry will be quick, but S&P 500 inclusion will take at least a year, and the company was founded five years ago.

Dario Amodei said as trading started that the company was hoping to be investment grade at some point in the future. He said: "Obviously, at some point in the future we're hoping to be investment grade," and the article noted that the price at which Anthropic borrows matters fundamentally. The prospectus said the technology "could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity". The article asked whether Anthropic, loss-making and with projected revenues in 2026 of $50bn-ish, can possibly be worth $1.5tn-plus.

The European Central Bank issued a reminder this week about how much capital is being bet on the AI revolution and how little transparency there is around the funding of hyperscalers and other suppliers. Its report said big tech firms are estimated to have total off-balance-sheet commitments of more than $4tn as of the second quarter of 2026. It warned of "historical parallels with the dotcom and sub-prime bubbles". Truist chief market strategist Keith Lerner noted that tech valuations have fallen 42% over the past year, and the sector has gone from outperforming the S&P 500 by 25% over six months to underperforming it by 6%. Bank of America's latest fund manager survey shows investors have cut tech exposure by the most since June 2006, and "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary told the second article that investing in Anthropic is like investing in a young Amazon.

The second article said Thursday is supposed to be a celebration of AI, with Anthropic heading toward its long-awaited IPO at the Nasdaq. It said the very stocks that fueled this AI boom are still under pressure, pointing to sell-offs this week in CoreWeave, Salesforce and AMD. It said investors are questioning the AI spending, the valuations, the financing arrangements and whether the returns will ever justify the billions being poured into this technology. It said the AI build-out isn't disappearing, as seen from Nvidia on Tuesday, and that companies are still spending and the technology is still evolving. Lerner pointed out that previous tech pullbacks of more than 10% during this bull market were followed by an average rebound of 47%.

The first article said there was a late risk that investor sentiment towards the AI universe could be jinxed, or Jensened, by the soap opera at Nvidia. It said there was a worry that the AI bubble could burst when somebody tried to unload too much stock on the stock market in one go. It said the assembly of AI and AI-adjacent names in the cornerstone placement fed worries about the industry's circular financing. It said executives grumble that their IT budgets are finite and that nine-month-old versions, or cheaper "open weight" models from rivals, do the job for basic work. It said "commoditisation risk" could be the next year's valuation debate, and that debt, not just equity, will be a crucial part of this story.

stories.Headline: AI SPERA launches Criminal IP AITEM to pair asset discovery with AI exposure management
stories.Summary:
Criminal IP, a cyber threat intelligence platform developed by AI SPERA, officially launched Criminal IP AITEM on November 18, 2026, according to a GlobeNewswire release dated November 19, 2026, from Torrance, California. AITEM stands for AI-Powered Threat Exposure Management and is an evolution of Criminal IP ASM. It combines internet-facing asset discovery with AI-assisted investigation, public-source exposure analysis, and dark web monitoring. It also introduces AI Pentest to help security teams assess and validate security risks in their web assets. The release says discovering an unfamiliar server or a leaked credential is only the first step, and analysts still need to establish how it relates to their organization.

Criminal IP AITEM continuously discovers internet-facing assets and collects IP addresses, domains, certificates, open ports, cloud assets, and technologies. Its dashboard summarizes asset inventory, risk distribution, recent findings, and exposure trends, and analysts can drill down into individual assets and explore related infrastructure. Public-source exposure analysis finds sensitive files, administrative pages, and exposed directories indexed by search engines, while GitHub exposure detection uncovers publicly accessible credentials, API keys, and configuration files. Dark web monitoring surfaces leaked credentials, exposed information, and mentions of the organization across monitored sources. The release says AITEM applies AI across detection, investigation, prioritization, and automation, supports natural-language queries across assets, vulnerabilities, and exposures, and uses daily scans, historical tracking, and automated notifications.

The release states that prioritization considers exposure severity, asset impact, and threat context to help teams decide which findings need attention first. Automated alerts and investigation workflows support follow-up and reduce manual tracking as risks change. When AITEM discovers an unfamiliar server, the release says, analysts can review its open ports, exposed services, SSL/TLS configurations, and related CVEs, while Criminal IP threat intelligence adds context through connected infrastructure, malicious activity, abuse history, and associated threat indicators. The release says AI Pentest lets security teams run AI-powered penetration tests on their web assets to identify potential vulnerabilities and validate suspected security weaknesses. The release says monitoring can also extend to partners and suppliers.

The release says Criminal IP is used in more than 150 countries and provides threat visibility through Criminal IP Search, Criminal IP ASM, Criminal IP FDS, and Criminal IP TI Feed. It says Criminal IP continues to expand its global security ecosystem through integrations and strategic partnerships. Its threat intelligence is also accessible through major cloud and data marketplaces, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Snowflake. The release names Michael Sena of AI SPERA as the contact and lists four photo links accompanying the announcement. The release says forgotten servers, publicly accessible configuration files, and compromised credentials can be difficult to assess when findings are scattered across separate tools.

A Qualys blog post dated November 18, 2026, says security teams have never had better visibility into their assets, vulnerabilities, and threats but lack the speed to act on it. It says frontier AI models are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than ever, attackers are using the same models to exploit them within hours, and most remediation still depends on scans, tickets, and change windows. It says exposure management needs a new operating model that detects exposures as soon as they are disclosed, focuses only on what is proven exploitable, and remediates autonomously without breaking the business, and it calls that model the AI-native Risk Operations Center, or AI-ROC. The post says that on October 13, 2026, Microsoft released the largest Patch Tuesday in its history, fixing 1,414 vulnerabilities, more than seven times the 193 vulnerabilities Microsoft fixed in October 2025.

The Qualys post says one of the new vulnerabilities was already being exploited, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency set a deadline of just three days to patch it. It says that at ROCon Americas 2026, Qualys made the case that most organizations are focused on the wrong question, and that knowing how many exposures you have is no longer useful on its own. It says what matters is how quickly you can turn those exposures into verified risk reduction. It says that over the last twenty years the security industry has gotten very good at finding things, and organizations now have more data on assets, vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, threat intelligence, and alerts than ever before, but the ability to fix what matters has not kept up. The post says frontier AI is not creating new vulnerabilities but surfacing flaws that already existed in code much faster than before.

The Qualys post says the last two Patch Tuesdays, with 974 vulnerabilities in September and more than 1,400 in October, show how fast this is moving. It says attackers have access to the same AI tools and are using them to weaponize new vulnerabilities within hours. The post's table of contents lists sections on the vulnerability surge outpacing remediation, what the surge means for security teams, the ideal operating model for exposure management, how Qualys operationalizes the AI-ROC, what comes next for the AI-ROC, a conclusion, and frequently asked questions. The Criminal IP release says teams can learn more about Criminal IP AITEM and directs readers to a learn-more page. The release says Criminal IP connects asset visibility with exposure investigation and ongoing monitoring, so security teams can better understand what is exposed, why a finding matters, and where to focus their next action.

stories.Headline: Professor Sarfo warns students that over-reliance on AI blunts critical thinking
stories.Summary:
Professor Frederick K. Sarfo, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development, cautioned students against over-relying on Artificial Intelligence, according to a Ghanaian Times report published on November 20, 2026. He warned that unchecked dependence on digital tools risks blunting students' critical thinking skills and their memory retention. The report said he made the remarks in Kumasi, in a story filed by Kingsley E. Hope. The caution was carried in the Ghanaian Times, which also invited readers to follow its WhatsApp channel.

Professor Sarfo said it is a universal fact that AI is fundamentally changing the way students learn and conduct research, and that AI is useful to students for several reasons. He said research evidence shows that heavy reliance on AI reduces brain activity, critical thinking skills, and students' ability to recall events, facts, or information. He advised students to use AI or technology wisely and appropriately in their academic activities. Otherwise, he cautioned, they will become passive learners instead of active learners.

Separately, a University of the West Indies professor warned that excessive dependence on Artificial Intelligence could weaken students' ability to think critically, ABS TV Radio Antigua & Barbuda reported on November 19, 2026. The warning came during a Vice Chancellor's Forum on Tuesday marking the 30th anniversary of the School of Graduate Studies and Research. Dr Dwyane Devonish, Director of Graduate Studies at the UWI Cave Hill campus, said navigating the technology is critical. He provided the caution while making it clear that AI presents significant opportunities.

Both reports place the warnings in the same week of November 2026, one from a Ghanaian university leader and one from a Caribbean graduate studies director. The Ghanaian Times report was published on November 20, 2026, and the ABS TV Radio report on November 19, 2026. Neither article says what policies, if any, the two institutions will adopt in response to the warnings. Neither article states what happens next beyond the advice given to students.

stories.Headline: CareSource Foundation commits $1 million to scale proven AI for Medicaid care
stories.Summary:
The CareSource Foundation has committed $1 million to a single artificial intelligence project intended to improve health care for Medicaid members and people who face barriers to getting care, and it opened the request for proposals, titled “Advancing AI-Enabled Models for Care and Community Transformation,” on Nov. 10. The foundation is seeking applicants who are past the concept stage, saying it wants more than a promising idea. The funding provides up to $500,000 a year over two years, with one award expected. Concept papers are due Jan. 6, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. EST, full proposals from invited applicants are due Feb. 12, the award will be announced March 18, and the project starts in the second quarter of 2027.

Every proposal must show relevance to Medicaid, underserved and high-need populations, and the foundation is most interested in AI-enabled solutions with existing capabilities or proven models that are ready to be put into operation, evaluated and scaled. At the full-proposal stage, 30% of the score goes to the solution and technical approach and 15% goes to data, privacy, security and responsible AI, with reviewers also weighing measurable impact, organizational experience and capacity, operational readiness, cost effectiveness, and the potential to sustain and scale the work. The lead applicant must be an eligible nonprofit, and technology vendors cannot apply on their own. Applicants must name specific outcomes and key performance indicators and explain how their approach addresses equity, and the selected organization will send regular performance and progress reports along with qualitative material such as case studies and impact stories.

The foundation said AI has the potential to fundamentally improve how people experience health care, and it described responsible AI as fundamental to making innovation useful and trustworthy rather than separate from it. It pointed to places AI could help for Medicaid and underserved populations, including spotting emerging risks sooner, improving care coordination and navigation, personalizing outreach, connecting people with community resources and lowering barriers to care, and it said it wants the benefits to show up in people’s real experiences with the health care system. On scalability, the foundation said it will assess whether there is a credible path to sustaining and expanding impact beyond the grant period, not simply whether a pilot worked during its two years of funding. Details are at caresource.com/foundationgrant.

stories.Headline: AI Inspo launches an AI social media agent that combines strategy, content creation, publishing and performance review
stories.Summary:
AI Inspo launched its AI-powered social media agent on Nov. 18, 2026, according to PR Newswire, bringing strategy, content creation, publishing and performance review into a single workflow. The company said the agent combines two core capabilities, social media strategy and creative content creation, which help users set priorities, turn plans into content and use performance insights to shape what comes next. AI Inspo described the platform as an all in one AI powered social media management platform for content creation, scheduling, account management, performance tracking and social media growth. The launch announcement was dated San Francisco, Nov. 18, 2026. QuVideo produced the analysis in the Quad City Herald, reviewed and distributed by Stacker, and AI Inspo is a flagship product from QuVideo.

AI Inspo said managing multiple social platforms and accounts often requires moving among planning tools, creative software, publishing schedulers and analytics dashboards, a fragmented process that adds repetitive work and can make it difficult to turn insights into action. The agent's strategy capability assesses account performance and recommends next steps based on each user's goals and stage of account development. AI Inspo also finds trending topics relevant to the account and helps turn them into content ideas, giving users a way to identify trends their audience may care about and connect those opportunities with publishing plans. Its creative capability lets users choose a viral reference and add their topic, and AI Inspo adapts the reference's format into ready-to-publish content built around that topic. Users can take an idea from trend discovery through creation and publishing, then review how it performs, and those insights inform the next content brief and help users refine their choice of topics and formats over time.

Dong Lin, CEO of QuVideo and Project Lead for AI Inspo, said AI Inspo was built around the real-world needs of creators and marketers managing multiple accounts across social media platforms. He said that by bringing research, data analysis and content creation together, the company aims to reduce repetitive tasks and give users more time to focus on strategy, informed decision-making and creativity. The agent remembers how users manage their accounts and create content, then tailors recommendations to their changing goals and workflows. That continuity lets users build on earlier work and receive guidance aligned with their current priorities, and account context and performance insights help users judge which trends and formats deserve further creative effort. AI Inspo said the workflow is designed to reduce routine work, leaving users more time for creative decisions and planning.

AI Inspo said an account's needs change as it develops, and for a creator launching a new account, early priorities may include choosing a content direction and establishing a consistent production routine. As the account matures, attention may shift to refining formats or improving an existing strategy. Alongside its AI agent, AI Inspo provides ongoing user support and a Discord community where creators, marketers and businesses can exchange ideas, seek guidance and refine their social media workflows. The company said this combination supports its mission to make high-quality content easier and more affordable to produce. The platform is designed for creators, marketers and businesses.

The Quad City Herald analysis said social media managers handling multiple accounts often find the difficult work falls between tools, with audience research in one document, content plans in another and performance data across several dashboards. It said publishing connects these activities only superficially, and a team can keep its calendar full while losing track of why a post was made or what its results should change. Marketing professor Mary Beth McCabe, in her account of the 2026 Social Media Marketing World/AI Business World event in Anaheim, highlighted agent autonomy, repeatable workflows and human leadership, and the 2027 AI Business World program lists workflow automation and AI operations. The analysis said AI should support human judgment, not replace it, and that by connecting strategy, content creation, publishing and performance analysis, AI could help teams streamline workflows, make better decisions and improve their results over time. It said the question is whether these systems connect evidence to decisions rather than simply accelerate production.

Sprout Social's 2025 Impact of Social Media Marketing report describes data silos and the demand for audience and competitor context, and Glimpse conducted the online survey for Sprout Social from May 30 to June 20, 2025, among 1,200 marketing leaders in the U.S., U.K. and Australia, respondents ranging from managers to CMOs, all with social media responsibilities. YouTube's official guidance states that from March 31, 2025, Shorts views counted starts and replays without a minimum watch time, and engaged views remained available as a separate metric. Buffer's AI Assistant supports brainstorming, rewriting and adapting posts for individual platforms. In a 2023 Sprout Social case study, San Francisco-based Plaid social media lead Matthew McConnell described handling publishing, responses and reporting as a team of one, tagging posts to compare performance, investigating weaker results and adjusting strategy for different audiences. A 2024 Science Advances study found that AI-generated ideas could improve evaluations of individual short stories while increasing their similarity among them, and in Generative AI at Work, Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li and Lindsey Raymond found larger gains among novice and less-skilled customer support workers, with minimal effects among experienced workers, while a Harvard Business School field experiment likewise found that effects depended on the task.
