stories.Headline: New government leaders urged to prioritize tech talent as AI, modernization reshape public services
stories.Summary:
Following the 2026 midterms, a new class of elected officials is preparing to take office, and government technology experts say building stronger in-house technology teams should be among their top priorities. Jennifer Anastasoff, executive director of the Tech Talent Project, a nonpartisan nonprofit that helps U.S. federal and state governments recruit technology leaders, made the case in an interview with StateScoop. She said artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and major changes to federal benefits programs are putting additional pressure on government systems. Incoming state and federal leaders will need to recruit experienced technologists and give existing employees the resources to modernize how government operates, she said. Anastasoff is a founding team member of the U.S. Digital Service.

Anastasoff said 36 states held gubernatorial elections this year, and incoming governors should prioritize technology-fluent leadership across their cabinets, including chief information officers, chief data officers and potentially chief AI officers. She said agency leaders do not necessarily need to be technology experts themselves, but need enough understanding to make informed decisions and access to trusted advisers. She said states are preparing for new Medicaid and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program requirements under H.R. 1 while managing cybersecurity threats and aging technology infrastructure. The Trump administration recently announced an optional six-month hold harmless period through June 30, 2027, allowing states to delay disenrolling or denying Medicaid coverage over new work requirements originally set to take effect on Jan 1. The Tech Talent Project recommends each state needs a dedicated data analyst embedded in state Medicaid agencies so beneficiaries do not lose access and caseworkers do not get backlogged.

Anastasoff said AI adoption requires more than hiring a chief AI officer, and governments need software engineers, data specialists, product managers and user experience experts who can evaluate whether AI-generated information is accurate and appropriate for public services. She said governments need people with the expertise to see where AI is real confident and real wrong. She said attracting those workers requires governments to rethink how they recruit, and while public-sector salaries may not compete with private industry, many technologists are motivated by public service. She said the bigger challenge is making sure qualified candidates can find positions and move through hiring processes quickly, and she urged incoming administrations to review job descriptions, recruitment systems and internal promotion opportunities early in their terms. She said many people reach out directly to say they are thinking about government, and the question is how effectively and how quickly they can be connected with the right role.

A recent report by the National Association of State Chief Information Officers found that many state AI officials lack the staffing, funding and authority needed to manage the technology across government agencies. The report found that while AI oversight has become a priority for state technology offices, establishing an AI leadership position is only the first step. The report states that when NASCIO first started tracking in 2023, less than 20 percent of states had a state chief artificial intelligence officer or a similar title. It states that just three years later, at least 46 states have identified at least one person tasked with directing artificial intelligence, and by its count 25 states have someone with AI in their title. Anastasoff said without investment, outdated systems and inefficient processes could continue to burden both government employees and residents who depend on public services.

In the Scottish Parliament on Wednesday, SNP MSP Zen Ghani asked what plans the Government had to use artificial intelligence to improve decision-making and increase efficiency as part of its public service reform agenda. Cabinet Secretary for Public Service Reform Ivan McKee said AI was being used to support human workers, not replace them, but confirmed the technology was being used to redesign services. He said public service reform is about redesigning services around people's needs, and digital services, data and technology is a key enabler through a dedicated work stream within the public service reform strategy. He said the government is scaling intelligent automation across core government and key public bodies, including identifying opportunities to pilot AI technology in public sector processes. He said within the Scottish Government it is scaling responsible and ethical AI and automation, including the rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot premium and developing AI agents to reduce administrative burden and support better decision-making while retaining professional judgement.

Ghani pointed to figures from Skills Development Scotland which found that while 87% of businesses in Scotland now use AI in their daily practices, 74% of businesses reported no change to staff headcount. He asked how the Scottish Government intends to ensure AI is used to streamline governance and not as a tool to replace workers. McKee said the approach is to use AI to support the workforce, reducing routine administration and freeing staff to focus on what requires human judgement, expertise and empathy. He said responsible adoption is supported by guidance in the Digital Scotland Service Manual, transparency through the mandatory Scottish AI register, and developing an AI ethics and assurance framework alongside safeguards on data protection and security, responsible procurement and investment in AI skills. Tory MSP Craig Hoy asked if the Scottish Government was considering replacing ministers with AI given how poor some are at answering questions, particularly the Cabinet Secretary for Transport, Stephen Flynn. McKee responded that this comes from a party that used AI to generate thousands upon thousands of irrelevant, trivial questions to the Government, running up an enormous bill. Douglas Lumsden, the former Tory MSP who became an MP in the Aberdeen South by-election after Flynn was elected to Holyrood, submitted around 1000 written questions to the Scottish Government in January 2025, reportedly costing around £100 each to answer, and the SNP accused Lumsden of costing the taxpayer £100k by using AI to ask nonsense questions about bees, straws and pepper sachets.

Dmitry Tikhomirov of EPAM Systems discussed agentic AI for financial services and insurance on November 10, 2026. Ant Digital Technologies and JB Financial Group signed a memorandum of understanding on November 18, 2026. This partnership occurred during the Singapore FinTech Festival 2026 to explore AI powered innovation. The collaboration focuses on applying AI agents to banking operations for risk management and efficiency. These developments highlight a shift toward autonomous systems that can plan tasks and execute actions.

The MOU involves Ant Digital Technologies, a subsidiary of Ant Group, and Korea's JB Financial Group. JB Financial Group includes Jeonbuk Bank, Kwangju Bank, JB Woori Capital, JB Asset Management, and JB Investment. Their overseas network includes PPCBank in Cambodia, JB Capital Myanmar, JB Securities Vietnam, and PT Bukopin Finance. Microsoft provides a stack including Entra ID, Agent 365, Purview, Defender, Work IQ, Fabric IQ, and Foundry IQ. The Foundry Agent Service acts as the runtime for deploying and managing agents in production.

Dmitry Tikhomirov stated that agentic AI is a good fit for industries full of rules and documents. He argued that AI agents excel where humans currently act as costly middleware between different systems. Leo Li of Ant Digital Technologies said he looks forward to developing responsible and practical AI capabilities. Ki Hong Kim of JB Financial Group said the technology will strengthen competitiveness in credit assessment. He also noted that the collaboration will improve financial access for their various foreign customers.

Banking clients are affected through improved onboarding, KYC refresh, alert handling, and financial crime investigations. Insurance users benefit from better underwriting intake, claims triage, policy servicing, and fraud referral processes. Capital markets see changes in post-trade exceptions, reconciliations, and surveillance triage to reduce manual coordination. McKinsey research from October 2026 notes a banking industry shift from AI copilots toward agentic AI systems. These systems are designed to collaborate across business workflows to create lasting value for the industry.

Ant Digital Technologies has operated independently since April 2024 and established Hong Kong headquarters in 2025. The company has partnered with over 300 partners to serve more than 30,000 enterprise customers worldwide. They have established collaborations in Asia with Ryt Bank, Touch 'n Go, Kenanga Investment Bank Berhad, and Bank CenterCredit. Omdia recognized Ant DT as a Market Leader in the 2026 Market Radar for agentic AI solutions. The 2026 Future of Fintech in APAC report describes a transforming landscape for digital lending and payments.

The partners will now identify practical AI applications that address the evolving needs of the financial industry. Firms are encouraged to redesign workflows from the ground up around digital labor rather than adding AI. Leaders must calibrate autonomy by setting specific mandates, clear permissions, and visible boundaries for every AI agent. The articles leave open how regulators will eventually use telemetry from Azure services for necessary audit trails. It remains to be seen how these firms will measure business outcomes like leakage and false positives.

stories.Headline: Alibaba Cloud expands global data center network to meet rising AI demand
stories.Summary:
David Rubinstein hosted Jason Eichenholz on a podcast on November 19, 2026, to discuss the power needs of AI. Alibaba Cloud also announced plans to expand its global data center network over the next year on November 18, 2026. These developments occur as the adoption of artificial intelligence expands and creates a growing demand for computing power. Eichenholz believes that electricity availability has become a major bottleneck for the expansion of AI and its data centers. Alibaba Cloud is prioritizing Hong Kong because its three leased data centers there can no longer meet current demand.

The expansion requires new infrastructure like 500 megawatt or multi gigawatt buildings, which often have four to six year wait times. This process involves grid upgrades, new substations, cooling, permitting, and construction in the physical world. Alibaba Cloud is expanding its network to support financial firms that are adopting AI in their core workflows. Eichenholz notes that companies must now consider water use and the impact of siting on local communities. The new AI geography era requires next generation connectivity to link geographically dispersed data center footprints across the world.

Jason Eichenholz, the founder and CEO of Relativity Networks, said that power will be the forever bottleneck in AI expansion. He explained that the industry is shifting from a race for chips to a race for productive computing capacity. Eichenholz stated that the optical industry must now focus on how quickly information moves rather than just total bandwidth. He suggested that data center operators and municipalities can find win win partnerships to benefit local communities. Yuan Zhiming, a vice president at Alibaba Cloud, outlined the company's expansion plans at a summit in Hong Kong.

Local communities are affected by the noise, huge land requirements, and the potential for rising electricity prices from data centers. Some residents are propagating a Not In My Backyard movement to oppose the construction of these large facilities. However, sophisticated municipalities can use these partnerships to pay for new schools, fire stations, training, and local jobs. Hyperscalers and co location providers are now making investments in clean energy that utilities could not previously afford. Financial firms in Hong Kong are specifically affected as they seek more AI computing power for their workflows.

The fiber market is currently growing rapidly, moving beyond its previous primary drivers of telecommunications for homes and cities. There is now a need for fiber inside data centers, across metropolitan campuses, and across continents via submarine networks. Investments in solar energy storage and next gen modular reactors have become economically viable in the last few years. AI is creating a demand for an entirely new generation of optical infrastructure to connect computing power. This shift is moving the industry away from a period where companies chose sites without worrying about connectivity.

Alibaba Cloud will expand its global data center network over the next year to meet the growing demand for AI. The industry is turning to hollow core fiber to unlock next generation latency, reliability, and better network economics. Companies must now navigate the challenges of grid distribution and the physical constraints of the modern power grid. The articles leave open who will ultimately pay for the power and the specific environmental impacts of these centers. It remains unclear how many municipalities will successfully form creative partnerships with the large tech companies and hyperscalers.

stories.Summary:
Chris J. Preimesberger and other authors wrote about AI agents in November 2026. They examined if agents need large language models to decide their next steps. These writers explored the current state of AI engineering and model deployment. They focused on how agents function within various software development environments. The articles discuss the evolution of autonomous agents and their security.

The research by Jing, Chen, Sun, He, and Si requires provenance-gated tool invocation. This method defends agents against indirect prompt injection in the year 2026. The study appears in Advances in Engineering Innovation, volume 17, issue 12, pages 1 to 7. It references Toolformer from 2023 and InjecAgent from 2024 to explain security. The authors used specific datasets to analyze these tool-integrated large language model agents.

The authors of the provenance-gated study are responsible for the data provided. They stated that the datasets used in their current study are available. These contributors claim that the opinions in the publication are solely their own. They noted that EWA Publishing in Oxford, UK, is the licensee. The authors maintain that the editor is not responsible for the ideas.

Other researchers like Greshake and Fritz discussed compromising real-world applications in 2023. They found that indirect prompt injections affect users of LLM-integrated software applications. Deng and Xiang noted that AI agents are under threat from security challenges. Zhan and Liang benchmarked these injections to see how they affect tool-integrated agents. These security flaws impact any organization deploying autonomous agents in production.

The background includes a 2026 report stating 75% of cloud-native developers ship AI code. DuckDB 2.0 added an Agent Mode for coding agents on November 16, 2026. Linus Torvalds used Claude Code to fix the Linux page cache in October. Anthropic ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes during a red team exercise. These events show a broad trend toward integrating AI into core infrastructure.

Future steps involve implementing provenance-gated tool invocation to stop indirect prompt injection attacks. Developers must decide if they should use serverless or container frameworks for scaling. The articles leave open whether the agent stack will ever fully settle. They do not specify if all developers will adopt these new security gates. It remains unclear how many agents will move into full production.

stories.Headline: Guidepoint partners with Rogo to bring cited expert transcripts into AI financial research
stories.Summary:
Guidepoint announced a partnership with Rogo on Nov. 19, 2026, in New York, NY, according to a GlobeNewswire release. The partnership lets bankers and investors using Rogo access Guidepoint Library insights, including more than 150,000 compliance-reviewed expert transcripts. Answers that draw on Guidepoint content are cited to the original conversation. Guidepoint described itself as a global pioneer in access to expert insight. Rogo was described as the leading AI operating system for financial services and a trusted partner to the world's most prestigious financial institutions.

Through the Guidepoint MCP connector, Guidepoint clients who use Rogo can access Library insights from vetted Advisors in the same platform where they build comps, models, memos, and pitchbooks. The Guidepoint Library includes more than 150,000 compliance-reviewed transcripts of moderated conversations with vetted Advisors, and more than 5,000 new expert interviews are added every month. Guidepoint curates the content around topics relevant to clients' research needs, helping deal teams and investors screen opportunities, evaluate theses, and prepare client deliverables. Every transcript is compliance-reviewed, and Guidepoint implements custom compliance controls tailored to each firm's requirements. The connector is available now to Guidepoint clients using Rogo, who can contact their Guidepoint account team or email the address given.

Ameesh Shah, Chief Commercial Officer of Guidepoint Insights at Guidepoint, said it was clear from the first conversation that Rogo and Guidepoint share a commitment to reliable insight grounded in the firsthand experience of vetted practitioners. Shah said combining the strengths streamlines critical workflows, reduces everyday friction, and helps clients get answers faster. Shah said the partnership creates a more unified experience that helps users focus on what matters most. Strib Walker, Head of Product at Rogo, said some of the most valuable insights in finance come from people who have operated the businesses and navigated the markets customers are analyzing. Walker said the partnership brings that expertise directly into Rogo so teams can incorporate firsthand industry perspectives from diligence to investment decisions without interrupting workflows.

The partnership overview lists expert perspectives from vetted Advisors with direct operating, customer, and competitor experience. It lists traceable answers, where Guidepoint-informed answers in Rogo cite the original transcript, which users can open to validate the answer. It lists compliance review of every transcript and custom compliance controls tailored to each firm's requirements. It lists insights built into existing workflows, appearing where bankers and investors already work with no need to switch tools. The partnership is part of Guidepoint's broader effort to make its expert research available across the AI platforms and workflows its clients rely on, and Guidepoint is backed by a global network of more than 2M+ subject-matter experts serving institutional investors, consulting firms, and corporations.

Guidepoint announced Guidepoint MCP on Nov. 17, 2026, in New York, NY, a connector bringing its expert transcript Library and Advisor Network into AI platforms research teams already use. Guidepoint MCP connects Guidepoint360 to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, and is built on the Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting data sources to AI applications. Guidepoint CEO Albert Sebag said AI has made public information easy to access but firsthand practitioner insight is still the hard part. Sebag said a general-purpose AI assistant may draw on public filings, news, and web content but does not usually have access to firsthand practitioner perspectives. Sebag said a standalone research platform can provide primary research but may require teams to work in a separate environment, and Guidepoint MCP bridges both gaps subject to the firm's own entitlements and compliance protocols.

Guidepoint MCP capabilities include seamless AI incorporation, full source attribution tracing every answer to the source transcript in Guidepoint360 with a complete audit trail, compliance by design configurable to client-specific controls and topic restrictions, and a compounding dataset with 150,000+ transcripts now and 5,000+ added every month. An analyst can pull up the full transcript to confirm a quote or paraphrase, read the surrounding conversation for context, and reference the source in an investment committee memo or client deliverable. Teams can search their own completed consultations and query those transcripts in one place, subject to their permissions. Clients can pull up open projects, see Advisors submitted to them, read screening answers, filter by responses, check availability, and request or decline a consultation with a confirmation before each step. Clients can also ask about upcoming curated insights and register for roundtables, teleconferences, and moderated calls without leaving the workflow.

Sebag said one challenge researchers face is the friction of working in multiple AI environments, and he called Guidepoint MCP the first end-to-end workflow facilitator to interface with all the major existing AI platforms. Sebag said it is designed to work from a 360-degree vantage point, handling curation and selection of the right experts, booking them, and gathering the research. Guidepoint said its network of more than two million subject-matter experts serves institutional investors, consulting firms, and corporations across companies, markets, and trends. Guidepoint said it embeds expert knowledge into decision-making through live, asynchronous, and agentic workflows. The articles leave open the terms of the partnership and any further platforms Guidepoint MCP may connect to.

stories.Headline: FreshBooks releases ChatGPT for Accounting with OpenAI to give small business owners read-only answers on their finances
stories.Summary:
FreshBooks partnered with OpenAI to release ChatGPT for Accounting, a new destination that brings AI innovation to small business owners who are learning the financial side of their business and increasingly turning to AI for help, according to a GlobeNewswire announcement dated November 19, 2026. The announcement said the momentum and opportunity around AI is driving small business tech adoption, which has climbed from 56% to 86% in just two years. FreshBooks said it is meeting business owners in these AI tools, putting real answers about their financial books directly into chat conversations and making it easier for owners to run their business. The company described the release as the biggest AI launch for small business owners.

The FreshBooks-ChatGPT connection is read-only, meaning it can retrieve live data to answer questions but cannot change anything in a FreshBooks account, so owners retain control and FreshBooks remains the single source of truth. Through the plugin, owners can ask ChatGPT direct questions such as which expenses are still missing receipts before closing the books, which invoices are overdue and who needs a reminder, and whether the right amount of sales tax was collected and paid this period and whether it ties out. FreshBooks said accountants have great tools in this launch and that it is making sure business owners have ones too. The company said that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned.

Shaheen Javadizadeh, CEO at FreshBooks, said ChatGPT is one of the leading AI tools FreshBooks customers already rely on. He said that with this plugin owners can ask about their business in their own words and get answers based on their real numbers, so they stay on top of their finances all year instead of catching up at tax time. He continued that accountants have great tools in this launch and that the company is making sure business owners have ones too, adding that when owners understand their numbers they make better decisions. He said the company's mission is to make running a business easy, and that meeting owners in the AI tools they use empowers them to build the business they envisioned. FreshBooks described itself as a leader in small business management software, purpose-built to help service business owners simplify the financial complexity of running their business, from invoicing to cash flow.

In a separate announcement dated November 18, 2026, Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership to help more people discover and engage with Le Figaro's journalism. The partnership covers current reporting and archive content from Le Figaro and associated publications, spanning news, business, culture and lifestyle, and these articles will be discoverable using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories. Marc Feuillée, Chief Executive Officer of Groupe Figaro, said the partnership reflects the group's ambition to build meaningful relationships with a leader in artificial intelligence research and deployment, and that combining its editorial heritage and trusted brands supported by a team of more than 600 journalists with OpenAI's technological expertise and global reach will bring new opportunities for innovation and create long-term value for readers. Varun Shetty, Vice President of Media Partnerships at OpenAI, said Le Figaro's reporting helps readers make sense of the stories shaping France and the wider world, and that the partnership reflects a commitment to working with publishers to support quality journalism and connect it with new audiences. Le Figaro will retain full editorial independence and control over its journalism, and it also plans to introduce ChatGPT Enterprise across various teams to support their day-to-day work, exploring additional uses of OpenAI technology in its workflows and reader services guided by its AI charter and editorial standards.

stories.Headline: GAO reports AI expands cyberattack reach while giving defenders new detection tools
stories.Summary:
The U.S. Government Accountability Office reported on November 20, 2026, that artificial intelligence is expanding the reach of cyberattacks while providing new detection tools for agencies and companies. The agency noted that generative AI can create deepfakes and convincing phishing messages, while agentic systems can adapt across multiple stages with very little human involvement. These technologies allow threat actors to magnify the impact of traditional attacks against essential services like telecommunications, energy, water, and financial systems. The report cited a June 2026 instance where AI agents tested malware and a February 2026 campaign where a low-skill actor used commercial AI services.

To counter these threats, organizations are using machine learning and generative AI to inspect network traffic, find source-code flaws, and manage large volumes of information. The GAO outlined four policy goals to improve cybersecurity guidance, address research gaps, oversee the AI life cycle, and strengthen the workforce. Among sixteen suggested options, the agency recommended risk-based procurement, larger testing environments, and human authorization for consequential actions. It also advised creating backup arrangements, such as manual procedures or rule-based tools, in case AI systems fail or produce unexpected results.

The GAO stated that cyber defenders struggle because AI tools are difficult to test and lack sufficient guidance or data for proper use. The agency highlighted concerns regarding outdated governance, data privacy, high costs, and a shortage of skilled workers to manage these complex systems. It also noted that there are currently no widely accepted measures to compare the performance of offensive and defensive generative AI. In a separate October 2026 report, the agency found that prompts sent to Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude produced feasible information for planning attacks on the electrical grid and improvised explosive devices.

Inc42 reported the funding on November 18, 2026, describing it as $4 million, around ₹37 crore, from the same two investors. The startup is building indigenous foundation models focused on mathematics, coding and reasoning, according to Inc42. Soket AI recently launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter foundation model, under Project EKA, its flagship sovereign AI initiative.

The funding will support the startup in scaling its foundation model research and developing AI systems for financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. The $4 million investment will also support applied AI research and enterprise deployments, particularly across financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. Unlike Soket's reasoning-focused EKA-1, ZenteiQ's models are designed as lightweight AI assistants that can run on-premises and on edge devices, including smartphones, without requiring continuous cloud connectivity. stories.Headline: Ramaphosa urges Silicon Valley investors to help South Africa build and own AI
stories.Summary:
President Cyril Ramaphosa urged Silicon Valley investors to help South Africa develop artificial intelligence businesses, create jobs and train local workers. He spoke to investors and technology leaders in Silicon Valley in the United States, and the call was reported on 19 November 2026 by Scrolla of Johannesburg, written by Palesa Matlala. Ramaphosa warned that South Africa risks falling behind if it only buys foreign technology instead of developing and owning its own innovations. He said he wants South Africans to do more than use artificial intelligence, and to build it, own it and make money from it. He warned that South Africa could be left behind as artificial intelligence changes how people work and do business.

Ramaphosa said South Africa must not repeat past patterns where wealth and opportunities were concentrated in the hands of a few. He said the country cannot allow the artificial intelligence revolution to reproduce historical patterns of inequality and dependance, and cannot be content merely to remain consumers of technologies developed by others. He wants partnerships with international technology companies that will help South Africans gain skills, start businesses and develop technology locally. He said South Africa must have a fair relationship with countries and companies developing the technology, and that as South Africa produces it exports to them and they export to South Africa. He also warned that simply building data centres, large buildings filled with computers that store and process information, would not be enough, because they do not automatically create large numbers of permanent jobs.

Ramaphosa said the government must improve conditions that encourage companies to invest in South Africa. He said South Africa must not repeat past patterns in which wealth and opportunities were concentrated in the hands of a few. He said the artificial intelligence revolution must not reproduce historical patterns of inequality and dependance. He said South Africans cannot be content merely to remain consumers of technologies developed by others. He said that as South Africa produces, it exports to them and they export to South Africa.

The article said a developed artificial intelligence industry could create opportunities for young people looking for work, including jobs in computer programming, technical support, engineering and maintaining the equipment that powers artificial intelligence. It said small businesses could benefit from technology that helps them manage customers, improve services and reduce costs, and students could learn skills becoming more important in the workplace. It said these benefits are not guaranteed and will depend on whether investments lead to real training, jobs and opportunities for local businesses. It said there are concerns that artificial intelligence could replace some tasks currently performed by workers, making access to new skills even more important. It said the challenge for South Africa is turning investment into opportunities for people struggling to find work or unable to afford expensive technology training, and that local businesses must be able to take part instead of leaving the industry entirely in the hands of international companies.

The second article said Ramaphosa sat down on stage with Jonathan Karl at Semafor's inaugural Silicon Valley and the World Summit in Menlo Park on Monday. It said he led an approximately 300-member national delegation to a forum attended by more than 400 global chief executives and policymakers, alongside summit co-chairs Sam Altman and Ruth Porat and advisory board leaders Andy Jassy, Jane Fraser and Standard Bank's Sim Tshabalala. It said the week opened in Menlo Park ahead of engagements at Stanford University, Alphabet, Google, Cisco, Palo Alto Networks and Microsoft. It said official United States Trade Representative figures show bilateral goods and services trade between the United States and South Africa grew by 10.1 per cent in 2025 to an estimated 28.8 billion dollars. It said global hyperscalers committed roughly 650 billion dollars to artificial intelligence capital expenditure in 2026, and three-quarters of last year's 259 billion dollars in artificial intelligence venture capital was concentrated in the United States.

The second article said Semafor editor-in-chief Ben Smith observed that grid constraints across North America and Europe have opened a major opportunity for agile international partners ready to host next-generation computing infrastructure. It said Citigroup chief Jane Fraser noted on the Menlo Park stage that global investors are becoming more thoughtfully selective about backing real demand-side productivity, and OpenAI chief Sam Altman emphasised that societies want assurance that artificial intelligence remains anchored on the human team. It said South Africa is already home to roughly 40 per cent of Africa's data centres and the majority of the continent's total data-centre capacity, combining established Microsoft, Amazon Web Services and Google cloud regions with deep financial markets, world-class solar and wind resources and Operation Vulindlela reforms. It said the Department of Electricity and Energy arrived in California alongside Eskom, NECSA and SANEDI with a phased 50-megawatt flexible artificial intelligence load demonstration at Grootvlei, backed by a growing electricity surplus and plans for 14,000 kilometres of new transmission lines. It said the delegation united eight Cabinet ministries with business leaders, start-ups, science councils and postgraduate and doctoral students, and cited the President's message in San Jose that talent is born everywhere and Wits computer scientist Professor Benjamin Rosman's call to build domestic capability over the decisive next two to five years.

The second article said young innovators returning from California can build on institutional platforms including the World Economic Forum's Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution presence in South Africa through the South African Centre for Industry and Technology, hosted at the University of Pretoria, alongside Wits, the University of Cape Town, Walter Sisulu University and the CSIR. It said a landmark study published on Monday by the St Gallen Endowment's Digital Policy Alert analysed 1,756 policy developments and 84 artificial intelligence rulebooks and highlighted a fifteenfold surge in domestic policy activity and strong convergence around transparency and safety. It said the study's international benchmark shows considerable room for African leadership on worker empowerment and binding cooperation, as no African framework yet features among the nine global instruments assessed. It said the delegation proposed a focused 90-day implementation window upon its return and a standing partnership uniting government, business, students and researchers. It said the world looks towards the Geneva AI Summit 2027, and the first article said the real test will be whether these partnerships create jobs, develop South African businesses and give young people a chance to benefit from technology that is changing the world.

stories.Headline: RadixArk releases DaisyRose-27B coding model trained exclusively with reinforcement learning
stories.Summary:
RadixArk released its first open-weight agentic coding model, DaisyRose-27B, during the week of November 20, 2026. This thinking model was post-trained from Qwen3.8-27B using only reinforcement learning without any distillation or supervised fine-tuning. The development process involved 18 days of training on 144 H200 GPUs, totaling 63,000 GPU-hours. This effort utilized the open-source RL framework called Miles and a specialized sandbox environment known as AgentENV.

The model features 27.8 billion dense parameters and a context window of 262,144 tokens. It requires a single GPU to run, with memory needs ranging from 23 GB for NVFP4 on Blackwell GPUs to 52 GB for BF16. The architecture maintains the Qwen3.8-27B design, including 64 decoder layers and a 27-layer vision encoder for processing images. Performance improved across seven benchmarks, most notably on Terminal Bench 4.1, where the pass@1 score rose from 5.6 to 12.0.

RadixArk developed the model using 1,200 curated tasks created with Eigent AI to address specific failures of the base model. The company stated that their internal backend achieved a 37 percent model flop utilization, which provided a two-fold speedup in throughput. They reported that their sandbox costs were approximately 80 percent lower than those of popular cloud providers. While the model leads in IFBench with a score of 82.4, the developers admitted it still trails larger mixture-of-experts models on difficult agentic tasks.

stories.Headline: Valor Energy completes Glorious Star purchase and plans $700 million Youngstown AI data center buildout
stories.Summary:
Valor Energy Inc. completed its purchase of Glorious Star, LLC, the Ohio limited liability company that owns an operational 18 MW computing center in Youngstown, Ohio, the company announced. The deal was structured as an equity acquisition and transfers 100% of the target's equity interests to Valor Energy. Glorious Star, LLC becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary of Valor Energy after the closing. Closing came after the company completed legal, financial and technical due diligence on the target. The purchase was announced on November 17, 2026, in a report by Ashish Joshi.

The Youngstown Project comprises a facility of approximately 30,888 square feet with roughly 18 megavolt-amperes of site-level apparent power capacity. That power is delivered by Ohio Edison through an existing 23kV utility interconnection, which the Company believes is approved and energized. Valor Energy plans total investment of approximately USD 700 million, deployed in phases as the project is built out. The first phase is expected to total approximately USD 200 million, and the figures do not represent committed funding. Valor Energy Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed company trading under the symbol VAI, and Green Energy Capital Asset Inc. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.

Dave Nichols, Strategic Advisor to Valor Energy Inc., said the existing utility interconnection carrying approximately 18 MVA may reduce certain development requirements relative to starting from an undeveloped site. Nichols cautioned that conversion into an AI data center will require further development work, permits and approvals, equipment and financing. He said the Company intends to pursue that development while evaluating the project's technical requirements and commercial feasibility. Nichols said closing the acquisition is an important step in pursuing Valor Energy's AI data center strategy. He added that the Company looks forward to building the project out with the local community and creating long-term value for shareholders.

Guy Coviello, president and CEO of the Youngstown/Warren Regional Chamber, called the investment a strong vote of confidence in Youngstown and the Mahoning Valley. Coviello described the site as an ideal location for a data center, noting it has operated as a heavy industrial site for decades. He said the building is largely out of sight of residential areas and the project offers a chance to reinvest in an established industrial site. Coviello said the project could help stabilize the surrounding neighborhood, create construction jobs for the skilled trades and generate new business for local companies. The Verge reported on November 18, 2026, that AI data center projects are continuing to pop up across the US with frequent opposition from locals concerned about their impact.

The Verge cited FOX 13 News reporting that data center regulation bills are coming, according to Utah's House Speaker. The Johnson County Post asked whether a small Johnson County town should ban data centers, and voters will decide. KDFW FOX 4 reported that a Red Oak data center expansion was approved despite community pushback. The Seattle Times reported that a proposed Amazon data center near Tri-Cities gets pushback from residents. Valor Energy historically ran automobile transaction and related services businesses and is now pursuing a strategic transformation into digital infrastructure, energy and other growth sectors.

Valor Energy said it intends to work closely with local officials and community partners in Youngstown on its proposed development plans. The Company stressed that its preliminary estimates remain subject to further planning, technical assessment and the availability of financing on acceptable terms. Valor Energy stated there can be no assurance it will obtain the financing necessary for any phase of the planned development. Timing, scope and the amount of each phase will depend on further design and engineering work, required permits and approvals, construction and equipment availability, project progress, financing and market conditions. The Company added that no phase is assured of completion within an anticipated timeframe, or at all.

stories.Headline: Suregiant Technology expands capacity to target AI advanced packaging market
stories.Summary:
Suregiant Technology held a pre-OTC-listing earnings presentation on November 18, 2026, to discuss its growth. The company targets high-double-digit growth as its release film enters the advanced packaging market. This material is now used in mass production for the world's top five semiconductor manufacturers. The company is expanding its capacity to meet the rising demand for AI chip packaging. These developments aim to drive revenue and profit to new highs for the firm.

Taoyuan Plant 2 will start official mass production in December, with a scale 2.5 to 3 times Plant 1. The company expects a full-year capacity contribution in 2027 and an OTC listing in mid-December. The tentative public offering price is NT$438 per share for the upcoming listing on the market. Release film entered 2.5D packaging in 2024, FOPLP processes in 2025, and 3D advanced packaging in 2026. The company's first three quarters of 2026 saw earnings per share reach NT$6.35 for investors.

Chairman Yang Yun-pin stated that order visibility extends 2 to 3 years for the company. He noted that customer forecast orders have reached 5 to 6 years for their products. Yang explained that their precision coating experience allows them to provide customized samples to major manufacturers. He said the company does not rely on one customer because end customers are highly diversified. Yang believes long-term demand remains solid as the overall AI and high-end packaging megatrend continues.

Institutional investors noted that AI and high-performance computing demand is expanding the advanced packaging market. Yole Group estimates this market will grow from $46.1 billion in 2024 to $79.4 billion by 2030. First-tier manufacturers are affected as they expand capacity for molding and wafer grinding using these materials. Japanese manufacturers previously dominated this segment, but Suregiant is now capturing share through localized service capabilities. The company's products are already supplied for mass production use in first-tier advanced packaging plants.

Suregiant started in the optoelectronics industry and entered the semiconductor field in 2014 to build material expertise. The company currently focuses on two major product lines, which are release film and grinding tape. Grinding tape has been supplied to the world's top ten packaging plants for more than 12 years. Third-quarter revenue was NT$159 million, which represents an 80.76 percent increase over the previous quarter. After-tax net profit for the third quarter was NT$66.51 million, up 92.72 percent quarter-on-quarter.

A new-generation thick grinding tape is expected to begin contributing to company revenue in 2027. Official samples for a new hydrolyzable tape are expected to be sent to customers in mid-2027. This new tape may begin a gradual ramp-up in 2028 as the company's third growth leg. The articles leave open whether Taiwanese firms can continue capturing market share from Japanese material suppliers. Future performance depends on the ramp-up speed of Plant 2 and the verification of new products.

stories.Headline: Zscaler partners with Anthropic and Mistral to secure enterprise AI adoption
stories.Summary:
Zscaler announced collaborations with frontier AI model providers on November 20, 2026, in Santa Clara, California. The company is partnering with Anthropic and Mistral to help enterprises adopt AI securely. These efforts aim to defend against AI-driven attacks and secure the agentic enterprise. Zscaler combines its security expertise with frontier AI innovation to protect customers. The goal is to stay ahead of emerging threats while embracing AI.

The collaborations integrate Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5.1 into Zscaler's Endpoint AI Security to power Exploit Paths. Zscaler also works with Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program to advance vulnerability discovery and security research. In Europe, Zscaler's Security for AI solution integrates with Mistral through a sovereign Zero Trust Exchange. This allows European enterprises to meet their data protection, sovereignty, and security requirements. A limited preview of the Exploit Paths capability is planned.

Zscaler CEO, chairman, and founder Jay Chaudhry stated that AI is fundamentally changing the threat landscape. He argued that Zero Trust is more critical than ever to eliminate attack surfaces. Chaudhry said that lateral movement must be prevented and AI agents must only access needed tools. He believes combining Zero Trust architecture with frontier AI innovations helps customers defend against attacks. This approach ensures agents never access the entire corporate network.

Traditional firewalls and VPNs cannot adequately protect enterprises as AI accelerates vulnerability discovery and exploitation. Zscaler's Zero Trust architecture affects users, workloads, devices, and AI agents by connecting them directly to authorized tools. This method reduces risk by eliminating internet-facing attack surfaces and preventing lateral movement. The platform protects thousands of customers from data loss and cyberattacks globally. It operates across thousands of private sites and over 200 public service locations.

Zscaler is a SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange and the world's largest inline cloud security platform. The company focuses on accelerating digital transformation to make customers more agile, resilient, and secure. The platform connects applications, devices, and users securely regardless of their physical location. These security solutions are designed for the AI era to provide visibility and control. They help enterprises uncover attack paths and protect sensitive data as they scale.

Zscaler will unveil new innovations to secure the agentic enterprise on December 9, 2026, at 1:00PM ET. This launch will showcase a unified Zero Trust Platform with capabilities to protect sensitive data and AI agents. The articles do not state when the limited preview for Exploit Paths will begin. stories.Headline: Nvidia invests 58.1 billion dollars in AI companies amid booming revenue growth
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported its third quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17, showing a massive boom in its artificial intelligence business. The company achieved revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase compared to the previous year. This financial report was the first one released without Jensen Huang serving as the chief executive officer of the firm. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress announced that the company is continuing to ship its next generation platform. The company also confirmed that the roadmap for its Vera Rubin technology remains on track for future development and release.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, while the company expects fourth quarter revenue of approximately 130 billion dollars. Nvidia spent 58.1 billion dollars on other AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, during nine months ending October 25. The firm provided 105 billion dollars in credit support for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Ohio for OpenAI. Total credit guarantees reached 118 billion dollars, and future commitments to neocloud firms totaled 32 billion dollars in the quarter. The company also spent 61.2 billion dollars on stock buybacks, which is up from 36.3 billion dollars last year.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that returning value to shareholders is a super top priority for the current management team. She noted that the company intends to use its remaining 227.3 billion dollar buyback authorization by the end of 2028. Kress explained that providing capital assistance to suppliers is another priority to ensure they can build more infrastructure quickly. Regarding customer data centers, she said the company must deeply analyze the strength of plans before making any investments. She also clarified that some credit guarantees vanish if construction is delayed or if customers face building challenges.

James Kisner of Water Tower Research warned that Nvidia is double exposed if the artificial intelligence spending boom eventually slows. He suggested that the company might be fueling its own demand by investing billions into its own customer base. This strategy affects the broader AI ecosystem, including frontier labs, infrastructure financiers, and various private companies receiving Nvidia capital. Investors are affected by a valuation reset, as shares fell 6.95 percent to 135.83 dollars on a recent Friday. The company's total market valuation dropped to 3.7 trillion dollars as of November 18, down from 5 trillion dollars.

Nvidia ended 2013 with a price to earnings ratio of 19.6, which was higher than its current ratio. Historical benchmarks show the multiple was 18.3 in 2014 and 17.1 in 2018, both above the current level. The current trailing price to earnings ratio is 15.68, while the forward ratio is 9.24 and PEG is 0.178. Net income more than doubled to 65.3 billion dollars from 31.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share hit 2.70. Equity securities generated 1.8 billion dollars in net gains, though this included a 1 billion dollar non-marketable loss.

The company will monitor data center growth and gross margins to see if the lower valuation represents a real opportunity. Management will continue to evaluate whether financing select customer data centers is the right type of investment for the firm. The outlook for the next quarter assumes that Nvidia will receive no data center compute revenue from China. It remains open whether Wall Street is too cautious or if competition will intensify and slow down infrastructure spending. Investors must now watch if customers become more selective with capital investments as the AI spending boom continues.

stories.Headline: Deutsche Telekom invests 100 million euros in Mistral to develop customized AI solutions for Germany
stories.Summary:
German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom invested 100 million euros, or about 109.4 million U.S. dollars, in the French AI startup Mistral on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This financial commitment was made through the T.Capital Tech Fund, which serves as the investment arm for Deutsche Telekom, during the Series D funding round for Mistral. The two organizations intend to establish a strategic partnership to assist public institutions and businesses in Germany with the adoption of customized AI solutions. This collaboration will combine the existing AI infrastructure of Deutsche Telekom with the specialized technology developed by Mistral.

The partnership focuses on enhancing European competitiveness by integrating powerful AI tools while ensuring that businesses maintain strict control over their own data. Deutsche Telekom has already expanded its capabilities by opening an AI factory in Munich in February and pledging nearly 250 million euros, or 273.5 million dollars, to double that facility's computing power. Mistral, which was founded in 2023, previously raised 3 billion euros, or 3.28 billion dollars, in September to compete with American developers like Anthropic and OpenAI. These combined efforts aim to provide a strong European alternative to the dominant AI technologies currently offered by the United States.

Ferri Abolhassan, a board member at Deutsche Telekom, stated that the ability to develop and utilize powerful AI is essential for the future competitiveness of Europe. He emphasized that maintaining control over data is a critical requirement for businesses as they integrate these new technologies into their operations. The company believes that this strategic investment will help bridge the gap between infrastructure and software for German clients. By leveraging the strengths of both firms, they hope to accelerate the deployment of sovereign AI capabilities across the continent.

Investors piled into the initial public offering of Anthropic on Thursday, which saw the company storm onto the public markets. This event occurred while tech stocks and chipmakers faced a broad sell-off, creating a disconnect for those investing in AI. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2 percent, and the S&P 500 logged another ugly day during this period. Chip stocks were bleeding, and companies like Nvidia and AMD were getting crushed as the market faced a perfect storm. Selling pressure extended into Friday, November 20, 2026, as investors began repricing the AI trade in real time.

The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,020.97, while the S&P 500 fell to 7,021.68 and the Dow 30 dropped to 48,769.04. Anthropic, PBC shares were at 84.70, and Nvidia Corporation fell to 135.32, while Intel Corporation dropped to 52.59 on Friday. CoreWeave reported nearly 90 billion dollars in debt and liabilities, alongside a net loss of 709 million dollars in the third quarter. Nvidia reported 116 billion dollars in third-quarter revenue, 65 billion dollars in net income, 32 billion dollars in debt, and 118 billion liabilities. The Russell 2000 fell to 2,608.41, and the VIX rose to 32.10, while Bitcoin USD dropped to 58,906.46.

Executive Editor Brian Sozzi said the market is facing a perfect storm where investors are less willing to pay any price. He noted that the Democratic Blue Wave has Wall Street questioning if Washington will put brakes on AI and data center construction. Sozzi stated that the leadership fallout at Nvidia is shaking confidence, as the market does not like interim CEO Collect Crest. He mentioned that technical selling and market clearing events are forcing investors to raise cash during this period of volatility. Sozzi also cited sticky inflation, hawkish Fed rhetoric, and the prospect of tighter financial conditions as drivers of the current weakness.

Hyperscalers including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle are no longer cash-flow positive despite the billions they reap in quarterly revenue. Neoclouds, which rent compute to hyperscalers, are tens of billions in debt, with CoreWeave seeing its stock price drop over 50 percent. Short seller reports targeting AMD and fresh regulatory fears regarding China have further damaged the semiconductor trade and affected these specific chipmakers. Bethany McLean questioned if the hundreds of billions spent on AI infrastructure and data centers can be repaid when it is due. Investors who want the AI future are now facing a reality where the broader AI trade is being blown to pieces.

Nvidia previously operated under an open checkbook policy led by founder Jensen Huang, who was the face of the AI revolution. The company loaned money to neoclouds to buy Nvidia chips, a tactic that critics have described as circular financing. Nvidia essentially guaranteed it would cover the debt of neoclouds if they could not pay, making Nvidia the guarantor of last resort. Much of this debt was resold to Wall Street and held by insurance companies, creating a complex web of financial liabilities. The industry has seen aggressive financial practices and rapid data center construction that may now be reined in by new leadership.

The market is waiting for Nvidia to announce a permanent CEO, as there is currently no timeline for this specific leadership decision. Investors are watching to see if the Democratic wave will burst the AI bubble and who will be left holding debt. It remains open whether the AI dream can survive the current repricing and the potential for tighter financial conditions from the Fed. The situation leaves it unclear if Anthropic can maintain its status as a 2 trillion dollar sensation amid the broader sell-off. Future market movements depend on regulatory fears in China and the ability of neoclouds to manage their massive debt loads.

stories.Headline: AI companions could help reduce loneliness, study finds
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Durham University Business School have published a study suggesting that AI companions could help reduce loneliness by creating a greater sense of belonging and improving self-esteem among the people who use them. The research was led by associate professor Varqa Shamsi Bahar alongside colleagues from Cardiff University and The University of Manchester, and it appeared in the journal Psychology & Marketing in 2026. The team explored why some AI companions appear to help people feel less lonely, and they introduced the concept of synthetic mindfulness to describe the experience of an AI companion that seems attentive, nonjudgmental and responsive to a user's needs. Across five studies involving 1,447 participants in the United Kingdom and the United States, the researchers examined how people use AI companions and how they experience their interactions with them.

The findings suggest that synthetically mindful AI companions can reduce loneliness in two ways, first by strengthening a sense of belonging so that users feel accepted, valued and connected, and second by boosting self-esteem so that users feel worthy of attention and emotional support. Together, these experiences were associated with lower levels of loneliness among the participants. The researchers suggest that AI companions could be particularly useful during periods of temporary loneliness caused by changing life circumstances, such as moving somewhere new, experiencing difficulties at work or in relationships, or feeling disconnected from those around you. AI companions can offer personalized responses and a space where people feel able to discuss concerns without judgment, according to the study.

The researchers warn that safeguards are needed and that AI companions should complement human relationships rather than replace them. They note that deep attachments to AI companions could blur the boundaries between artificial and human relationships, and that in some cases users may begin to favor AI companionship over relationships with other people, potentially increasing social isolation. The researchers therefore stress that AI companions should complement, rather than replace, meaningful human relationships. They also recommend that developers consider well-being when designing AI companion apps, including features that support belonging and self-esteem.

The study was published in Psychology & Marketing under the title AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness, with a DOI of 10.1002/mar.70288. The work was provided by Durham University and was edited by Gaby Clark and reviewed by Andrew Zinin. The researchers identified three dimensions of the experience through exploratory graph analysis, which they labeled perceived presence, perceived non-judgementality and attuned responsiveness. The article does not say what further research or regulatory steps will follow from the findings.

stories.Headline: Education experts urge Seoul universities to invest in AI detection for high-stakes exams
stories.Summary:
Global higher education experts urged Seoul universities to embrace artificial intelligence and rethink student assessments during a November 2026 summit. These experts called for stronger detection technology for high-stakes exams like the College Scholastic Ability Test to stop AI-assisted cheating. Kuancheng Huang, a professor from Taiwan, visited Korea University to attend the Times Higher Education Innovation and Impact Summit. He told The Korea Times that authorities must invest in technology to prevent cheating because such measures are very important. This push for better security follows growing fears about the misuse of smart glasses and other wearable devices in Korea.

Authorities will deploy at least one trained supervisor at each of 1,300 test sites to identify prohibited AI glasses. Prime Minister Han Seongsook's office is considering shutting down public Wi-Fi and requiring students to hand over their smart devices. More than 500,000 students took the College Scholastic Ability Test on Thursday, November 20, 2026, amid these heightened security concerns. National Tsing Hua University president John Kao requires students and faculty to disclose AI use, similar to citing academic research sources. These changes target high-stakes exams, university admissions, campus tests, and professional licensing tests where traditional testing methods are hard to replace.

Kuancheng Huang stated that technology to counter sophisticated cheating devices is available, but the challenge is the spending level. He suggested that universities shift their focus from final answers to the reasoning and problem-solving processes of the students. John Kao argued that restricting emerging technologies would not stop cheating because those who cheat always find new tools. He emphasized the need to promote academic ethics rather than simply taking away the tools that students use to cheat. Dawn Freshwater urged universities to teach students to think independently and produce original work supported by AI, not driven by it.

Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin rejected calls from lawmakers to postpone the national exam, stating a delay would cause larger disruptions. Han Won-seok, a tax accountant test taker, admitted using a concealed camera and generative AI to receive answers on smartphones. Han scored 397.5 out of 400 on a multiple-choice test in April and 663 out of 800 in July. Other affected students include those caught using AI-powered smart glasses on an English standardized test in June and university essays. These incidents have spooked the nation and left authorities scrambling to prevent fraud before the all-important college entrance exams.

The College Scholastic Ability Test is a high-stakes annual event in a country known for its intense academic competition. Prospects for marriage, social standing, and jobs often depend on which university a person attends in the South Korean system. To ensure an ideal environment, the country delays the workday and stock market trading to ease traffic for test-takers. Police officers use motorcycles to escort late students, and the military sometimes suspends training near the various testing sites. Flights are even paused during the English listening section to prevent noise from disrupting the students during the exam.

Police are currently investigating Han Won-seok, who stated in a YouTube video that he would cooperate with the legal process. Universities must now decide how to integrate AI as an inevitable part of education while ensuring students develop ethical judgment. Experts believe traditional assessments are becoming less effective at measuring actual abilities as AI tools grow more sophisticated over time. The articles leave open whether the government will officially implement the proposed Wi-Fi shutdowns and device collections at sites. It remains unclear how much authorities are actually willing to spend on the detection technology recommended by Kuancheng Huang.

stories.Headline: California regulators bar Waymo robotaxis from freeways and Waymo pauses US freeway rides
stories.Summary:
Waymo suspended driverless freeway rides across the United States after the California Department of Motor Vehicles barred its robotaxis from the state’s freeways, an order issued on November 11, 2026, and made public on November 17. The California restrictions followed two incidents in early November, when three Waymo vehicles entered a closed construction area on US Highway 101 near Burlingame on November 5 and another vehicle on Interstate 280 reportedly failed to respond appropriately to California Highway Patrol officers conducting a traffic break on November 6. Regulators concluded that recurring problems with construction zones and emergency vehicles created an immediate public safety concern, despite corrective measures taken after similar incidents earlier in the year. Waymo said the construction zone incidents caused no injuries or collisions, and the company has not announced a date for restoring freeway rides.

Although the order applies only to California, Waymo voluntarily paused freeway operations in all its other US markets while it reviews its autonomous driving systems, and driverless rides remain available on ordinary urban streets. The company runs commercial driverless service in 15 American cities, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, and the suspension removes freeway connections such as those between San Francisco and Silicon Valley. Longer trips that once used freeways may now follow slower urban roads, which could increase travel times, particularly for airport journeys during heavy traffic. Waymo advises passengers to check estimated journey times in its app and allow enough time for security and check-in, and travelers should not assume every airport or destination is served, because pickup areas and operating boundaries differ between cities.

Waymo said it is working with the California DMV and other state authorities to address the concerns and will resume freeway operations once the necessary safety improvements have been demonstrated. The California restrictions will stay in place until Waymo shows sufficient improvements to its autonomous driving technology and can respond safely to construction zones, emergency vehicles and changing freeway conditions. The company previously suspended freeway operations in May 2026 over safety concerns involving construction zones, then introduced software improvements and began restoring freeway access in July. The latest restrictions are another setback for the company’s efforts to expand autonomous transportation across major US cities, and freeway travel remains unavailable until further notice.

stories.Headline: Fujitsu Japan and partners verify AI cuts clinical trial screening work by 89 percent
stories.Summary:
Fujitsu Japan, the National Cancer Center Hospital East, and Paradigm Health conducted joint research to streamline clinical trial candidate screening. This project used a Large Language Model and the Paradigm Platform to identify potential candidates for new drug trials. The verification study took place between June and the end of October 2026 in Kawasaki and Kashiwa. The partners confirmed that this AI approach significantly improved the efficiency of the candidate identification process. This research aimed to shorten patient recruitment timelines and expand participation opportunities for domestic and international trials.

The study used data from 22,334 patients in the Department of Respiratory Medicine to simulate a trial for EGFR gene mutations. Fujitsu Japan processed electronic medical records for 3,027 lung cancer patients through anonymization and structuring using a Large Language Model. Paradigm evaluated 540 patients with EGFR gene mutations based on five specific criteria to determine their clinical trial eligibility. The AI identified 57 priority candidates, and physicians later confirmed that 51 of these individuals were promising candidates. This automated overnight processing reduced the number of patient records requiring manual review by approximately 89 percent.

Fujitsu Japan, led by CEO Izuru Kokubu, aims to commercialize a service for candidate screening and enrollment by fiscal year 2027. The company promotes the Uvance business model to create social value and streamline clinical trials through the use of AI. Toshihiko Doi directs the National Cancer Center Hospital East, which collaborated to verify the application of the Paradigm Platform. Paradigm Health, based in Columbus, Ohio, and led by CEO Kent Thoelke, provided the matching platform for the research. These partners stated that the system allows institutions to determine eligibility based on standardized criteria without relying on individual expertise.

Medical professionals, including physicians and clinical research coordinators, are affected because they previously relied on manual reviews and personal knowledge. The research shows that AI can alleviate the burden on medical staff and expedite clinical trial opportunities for patients. Patients are affected because the system helps them avoid missing opportunities to consider new treatment options for their conditions. The process ensures that final eligibility is determined by physicians based on trial requirements and the consent of the patient. These results represent candidates identified during research and do not guarantee that these individuals will actually participate in trials.

Drug loss is a pressing social challenge where new treatments available overseas are not developed or approved within Japan. Personalized medicine based on biomarkers and genetic mutations has advanced in oncology, making clinical trial participation criteria increasingly complex. Medical staff must currently review dispersed information across genomic data, test results, treatment histories, and electronic medical records. Differences in medical data formats and unstructured data in Japanese records create obstacles for the utilization of global data. This background creates an urgent need to promote clinical trials for new drugs to expand treatment opportunities for patients.

Fujitsu Japan will now proceed with commercializing a service to support the process from candidate screening to patient enrollment. The company targets a launch by the end of fiscal year 2027 to help expand clinical trial capacity. Partners will promote the adoption of this solution at medical institutions across Japan to facilitate broader access to therapies. The company intends to use Uvance to eliminate drug loss and provide higher quality healthcare to every single patient. The articles leave open whether the identified candidates will actually enroll or if other medical institutions will adopt it.

stories.Headline: Kevin Warsh creates Fed task force to examine AI’s economic effects
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has made understanding artificial intelligence’s effects on the economy a priority, creating a task force to examine the issue as he tries to reshape how the central bank sets monetary policy. In the past week Warsh said the Fed was modeling various scenarios to gauge what the impact of AI might be on the economy. The minutes from the Federal Reserve’s October board meeting showed that nearly all officials raised concerns about negative consequences to the financial system if AI yields disappointing results. Policymakers and Wall Street are also becoming increasingly concerned about what could happen if the AI boom fails to deliver on its promises. The October meeting minutes record that nearly all officials flagged the risk that disappointing AI results could harm the financial system, a concern shared by policymakers and Wall Street.

Warsh has created a task force to examine AI’s economic effects and has said the Fed is modeling various scenarios on what the impact might be. The effort is tied to his attempt to reshape how the central bank determines its monetary policy. The articles give no further numbers, dates or names beyond Warsh, the October meeting and the task force. Warsh is the official responsible for the push, having made figuring out AI’s effects on the economy a priority and creating the task force to examine the issue. He said this past week that the Fed was modeling various scenarios on what the impact might be.

The minutes show that nearly all officials raised concerns about negative consequences to the financial system if AI yields disappointing results. Policymakers and Wall Street share the growing concern about what could happen if the AI boom fails to deliver. This model could help the United Nations create global AI governance rules.

stories.Headline: Linq raises $90M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI agent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Linq, a Birmingham-based startup that provides texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, announced on November 18, 2026 that it raised $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, according to a press release. The round, described as a Series B, included continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital and Abstract, along with new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, will join Linq's board of directors. The company said it has already processed more than 1 billion messages and counts DoorDash, Town, Tomo and hundreds of others as customers. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the round follows a $20 million Series A in February.

The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure and strategic partnerships. Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks, and HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. As an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq said it can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the startup will double its workforce across three cities next year after its revenue increased tenfold following the round.

Elliott Potter, Linq's CEO, said that clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent, "pay rent," and that the company helps developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work. Ben Horowitz said agents will communicate and get work done just like people do, and that Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale. Aryan Shah, head of AI research at DoorDash, said the best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives and that Linq gives DoorDash the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation. Linq was co-founded by Potter, Patrick Sullivan as CTO and Jared Mattsson as president.

The company framed the raise around a broader shift in how agents operate, citing Cloudflare's report that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. Linq said these agents are not simple customer-service chatbots but book, buy and make plans by communicating with people and using software on their behalf. Messaging was Linq's first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. The press release did not say what the company plans to do next beyond the product expansion and hiring the Business Journal described.
