stories.Headline: South Africa aims to move from hosting data centers to innovating AI technology
stories.Summary:
President Cyril Ramaphosa announced on November 20, 2026, that South Africa intends to become an active participant in the global artificial intelligence value chain. During a working visit to the United States, the president spoke at a fireside chat held at Stanford University in California. He explained that the nation wants to move beyond simply hosting data centers to participate in the actual origination and innovation of technology. This strategic shift aims to ensure that South Africa and the broader African continent help shape emerging technologies instead of just adopting foreign innovations.

This new approach requires that investments in data centers unlock broader opportunities for local researchers, innovators, and businesses. President Ramaphosa noted that global tech giants like Google and Amazon are already establishing data centers in South Africa alongside various domestic firms. He believes the country can integrate into the global ecosystem by leveraging its universities, research institutions, and skilled workforce. Furthermore, the president highlighted that recent improvements in the national electricity supply provide a critical advantage for attracting these digital infrastructure investments.

President Ramaphosa stated that deeper participation in the technology value chain could help the government tackle domestic challenges like inequality and unemployment. He emphasized the need to engage young people in the AI-driven economy while simultaneously recognizing and mitigating the potential risks. The president also called for closer ties with the South African tech diaspora to bring expertise and capital back to young entrepreneurs. He maintained that the country remains open to foreign investment as long as partners help build local capabilities and foster sector collaboration.

stories.Headline: Singapore and China pledge to deepen cooperation in artificial intelligence
stories.Summary:
Singapore and China launched talks to upgrade their bilateral free trade agreement on Friday, November 20, 2026. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and President Xi Jinping met at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen to discuss these ties. The leaders pledged to deepen relations between the two countries amid current global shake-ups. They also discussed how to deepen cooperation in emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. This meeting was the third between the two leaders since Wong took office in May 2024.

The upgrade, called China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement 4.0, requires a memorandum of understanding between METI and China's Ministry of Commerce. It will cover the digital economy and government procurement to open new markets for Singapore companies. The agreement will facilitate cross-border data flows and build on the 2009 original bilateral free trade agreement. It also leverages the Suzhou Industrial Park, Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City, and the Chongqing Connectivity Initiative. These efforts follow the 2023 upgrade to an All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership.

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the partnership has expanded into connectivity and green development despite a complex international environment. He noted that both nations can learn from each other to help businesses innovate and raise productivity. President Xi Jinping stated that cooperation over the past few years has brought tangible benefits to both peoples. He described the two nations as friendly neighbours and key development partners during the meeting. Xi called for closer strategic communication to take the partnership to new heights.

President Xi noted that the world is undergoing profound changes with a new round of technological revolution. Prime Minister Wong urged Apec leaders to prevent the Asia-Pacific from splitting into competing economic blocs. He stated that dialogue is valuable for peace and stability during a time of heightened geopolitical tensions. Singapore companies are affected as the upgrade aims to make it easier for them to do business. Workers are also affected as the leaders discussed preparing them for future jobs.

China was Singapore's largest merchandise trading partner from 2013 to 2024 and its third-largest services partner in 2024. Bilateral merchandise trade totalled S$162.9 billion in 2025, which was 11.7 per cent of Singapore's global merchandise trade. Singapore has been China's largest source of foreign direct investment by annual flows since 2013. It is also the largest recipient in Asia of China's outward direct investment by flows. China will provide US$20 million to support the practical cooperation of Apec.

Prime Minister Wong will next travel to Beijing for a meeting and working lunch with Premier Li Qiang. He will wrap up his trip on Saturday after attending the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting. The articles leave open the specific details of the new digital economy and government procurement rules. They do not state when the Free Trade Agreement 4.0 upgrade will be finalized. The text does not specify the exact timeline for the new artificial intelligence cooperation.

stories.Headline: Chinese investors shift capital to consumer stocks amid AI sector volatility
stories.Summary:
Investors in China began shifting their capital into beaten-down consumer stocks during November 2026 to avoid the volatility of artificial intelligence trading. This movement occurred as a significant sell-off of technology stocks created turmoil across the mainland exchanges. Many traders viewed these consumer assets as safe havens because their prices had languished during the broader economic slowdown. The shift reflects a desire to find stability while the high-growth tech sector experienced a sharp decline.

The CSI index of consumer stocks rose nearly 5 per cent this month after previously gaining 2.9 per cent in October. Meanwhile, the Star 50 index which tracks the largest AI chipmakers in China has slumped more than 40 per cent since its record high in June. This divergence shows a clear rotation of funds away from expensive technology firms toward undervalued consumer companies. These changes highlight the extreme volatility currently affecting the artificial intelligence sector compared to traditional consumer markets.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission addressed the situation on Wednesday by denying online rumours about administrative interference in mutual-fund investments. The regulator stated that it had not required fund firms to report their specific exposures to the artificial intelligence sector. According to the commission, money managers have made their own independent investment decisions while following fund mandates and relevant laws. This official statement aimed to calm the market after reports suggested the government was influencing portfolio allocations.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Hunterbrook Capital shorts AMD over alleged ties to blacklisted Chinese firms
stories.Summary:
Short sellers targeted Advanced Micro Devices on Thursday, November 20, 2026, causing the company to lose over 10 per cent of its value in a few hours. This sudden sell-off occurred after the US investment firm Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position against the chip maker. The market decline included a plunge of more than 7 per cent during regular trading and an additional 3.4 per cent drop after hours. Investors are now speculating if the company will become a primary target for regulators after Nvidia.

The turmoil began when Hunterbrook Media, an affiliate of the investment firm, claimed that AMD firmware was discovered in specific hardware. These components were allegedly found in products from IEIT Systems, which is a Chinese server maker under the Inspur Group. The US Commerce Department had previously blacklisted the Inspur Group in 2023 to restrict its access to technology. The report also alleged that three other companies with close ties to IEIT Systems were using the same firmware.

The investment firm responsible for these claims suggests that the chip maker has connections to firms blacklisted by Washington. By publishing these findings, Hunterbrook Capital aimed to highlight potential regulatory risks associated with the company's business in China. The firm implies that these ties could lead to further government scrutiny or sanctions against the supplier. This situation reflects a broader tension regarding the supply of artificial intelligence chips to Chinese entities.

Articles.Title: After Nvidia, will AMD be a target as China’s ‘2nd-choice’ supplier for AI chips? - South China Morning Post

stories.Headline: AINU AI launches a creation platform to standardize short video production for e-commerce marketing
stories.Summary:
AINU AI launched a one-stop creation platform in September 2026 to help short video creators. The platform aims to turn viral hit videos into a standardized production pipeline for users. It focuses on the entire workflow from topic selection to final production for e-commerce marketing. This system integrates script writing and generation into one single interface for its users. The platform has already served 540,000 merchants and 2.2 million influencers globally.

The platform uses a Global Viral Data Dashboard to aggregate real time videos from TikTok, Douyin, and Xiaohongshu. It includes data from TikTok influencers like ash tervino vs bri and popular Douyin food accounts. The Script Master tool offers 8 built-in official preset skills and supports storyboard scheme output. Video generation is powered by models including Wan 3.0, Seedance 2.0, and Seedance 2.5. The system also provides specialized templates for clothing detail images and product selling point images.

The AINU AI team consists of nearly 100 members who manage core research and development. They stated that the platform is designed to enable one person to do the work of three. The team independently controls model iteration and computing power operation and maintenance for the system. They believe the next stage of competition lies in connecting the whole process from start to finish. This approach relies on a self-built computing power server room to support large-scale delivery.

E-commerce practitioners, individual merchants, and small teams are the primary groups targeted by this tool. These users prioritize a fast assembly line over having the single best generation model. Professional creators may still prefer single-point depth, which the platform might not provide in every link. The system affects how users create content for catering, entertainment, tourism, and domestic services. It allows visitors to create secondary works based on others' content via AINU TV.

The platform was built on existing industry content production experience and a large computing infrastructure. It has achieved a total accumulated content play volume of over 500 million views. The system supports an annual AI content production capacity of nearly 2 million hours. It differs from Kling, Jimeng, and Runway by focusing on workflow rather than just model capability. These other tools focus on character movement, ecological collaboration, or professional film and television post-production.

AINU AI will continue to bet on the workflow as generation capability becomes public infrastructure. The company must manage risks if upstream model providers tighten authorization or raise their prices. It remains to be seen if the platform can compete with editing software developers. The articles do not state how the platform will scale its user base further. They leave open whether the tool can achieve industry-leading performance in every single production link.

stories.Headline: Chinese tech giants prioritize AI infrastructure spending over immediate profits
stories.Summary:
Chinese tech giants are facing a critical market test as AI investments reshape their cash flow. Tencent, Alibaba, and Baidu are spending heavily on infrastructure, which has shifted their financial landscapes. This trend became evident around November 19, 2026, following recent financial results. Heavy asset investment is turning operating cash flow into a source for capital expenditure. These companies are now prioritizing computing power over immediate profit amplification.

Tencent saw its share price hit HK$350.4 on November 19, a low since August 2024. Its third quarter revenue was RMB 207.3 billion, but operating cash flow fell to RMB 2.6 billion. Tencent spent RMB 81.4 billion on capital expenditure, including an RMB 86 billion advance for computing power. Alibaba reported a free cash flow outflow of RMB 34.472 billion for the quarter ended September 30. Baidu had a quarterly capital expenditure of RMB 7.35 billion and free cash flow of -RMB 4.57 billion.

Tencent CFO Lo Siu Hon said advance payments locked in GPUs for the Hunyuan Model and WorkBuddy. President Martin Lau compared this spending to building a factory for future model training. Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell stated investment levels have roughly reached their peak for 2027. Alibaba CFO Xu Hong committed to realizing positive free cash flow as soon as possible. Baidu management explained that existing production capacity can meet much of their incremental demand.

Investors are concerned whether AI brings measurable revenue growth through cloud services or advertising. Analyst Catherine Lim noted the market will remain cautious until such growth is proven. Morgan Stanley cut Tencent's target price by nearly 13 percent to HK$480. Goldman Sachs expects Alibaba to face a funding gap through fiscal 2028. These companies are affected by higher capital costs and lower recovery efficiency than US vendors.

The industry previously relied on light assets and high cash flow to support share repurchases. Bloomberg estimates 2026 capital expenditure for leading domestic internet companies will approach US$66 billion. Morgan Stanley reports Chinese server capital expenditure is about three times higher than in the United States. Alibaba announced a three-year RMB 3800 billion AI and cloud infrastructure plan in February 2025. Baidu is developing the Kunlun Core M100 chip, expected for mass production by year end.

Tencent expects a financial turning point in 2028, while Alibaba may reach balance by fiscal 2029. Companies are using debt, such as ByteDance's US$29.6 billion loan, to secure computing power. Future profits will be eroded by depreciation as current capital commitments are transferred to assets. The articles leave open whether revenue growth will eventually exceed the growth rate of depreciation. It remains unclear if these massive investments will yield the expected commercial returns.

Articles.Title: Cash Flow Never Lies: AI Forces Chinese Tech Giants Into the Same Critical Market Test - 36Kr

stories.Headline: The Challenger Team develops an AI intelligent CNC grinding machine to reduce reliance on foreign imports
stories.Summary:
The Challenger Team, a high-end equipment group founded in March 2024, developed a full hydrostatic ultra-precision AI intelligent CNC grinding machine to break overseas monopolies. This effort aims to achieve independent controllability over industrial mother machines that are critical for high-end manufacturing in China. The team focused on tackling core technologies to overcome targeted embargoes and restrictions imposed by giants from Japan, Germany, and Switzerland. These ultra-precision grinders are essential for producing components with sub-micron and nano-level precision for the aerospace and semiconductor sectors.

The project requires the integration of an ultra-precision hydrostatic spindle with a radial runout of 0.2μm and an axial play of 0.1μm. It utilizes the Huazhong AI intelligent CNC system from Huazhong University of Science and Technology to provide automatic programming and precision deviation compensation. This technology addresses the failure of domestic bearings to meet P2 grade precision and reduces the 92 percent import share of high-end bearings. The development follows the thin-film feedback hydrostatic route pioneered by Academician Zhou Qinzhi to ensure consistent machining precision.

Guan Shihe spent over 20 years developing the critical hydrostatic spindle to match the precision of European brands like STUDER and Hover. Professor Dai Huiliang, a successor to Academician Zhou, stated that the team is fulfilling the academician's wish to industrialize domestic mirror grinding technology. The team noted that a current lack of funds limits them to selling spindles and hydraulic systems to help bearing manufacturers upgrade. They believe that these advancements will finally remove the bottlenecks hindering the production of precision ball screws and machine tool spindles.

This initiative aligns with the Outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan, which identifies industrial mother machines as a strategically critical field. The government intends to use the national Industrial Mother Machine Special Fund and other fiscal policies to support these decisive technological breakthroughs. stories.Headline: Anthropic raises a record $813 billion in its Nasdaq IPO and closes up 17%
stories.Summary:
Anthropic debuted on the Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, under the ticker ANT, with a final IPO price of $83 per share. The stock opened at $111.50 and surged to an intraday peak of $115.10. On a fully diluted basis its market capitalization once reached approximately $2.08 trillion. Based on issued shares the figure was around $1.51 trillion. It closed at $97.17, roughly 17% higher than the IPO price at market close.

Its fundraising amount hit $813 billion, surpassing SpaceX and setting a new global IPO fundraising record. At its intraday peak Anthropic became the sixth largest listed company by market cap globally on a fully diluted basis. It ranked after Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet and Amazon. As of September 30, 2026, it had approximately 5,300 employees. At the peak intraday market cap, each employee created a market cap of $392.5 million, roughly 4.7 times that of Nvidia.

According to the prospectus, revenue generated per capita in the past 12 months exceeded $6.6 million. Calculated at the peak intraday stock price, the total net worth of its seven co-founders exceeded $190 billion. In October, investors were still discussing that Anthropic's listing valuation could reach around $2 trillion. As the listing approached, market discussions fell back to the $1.2 trillion to $1.4 trillion range. By the time of its listing, the market cap surged back to $2 trillion.

The three major US stock indexes all closed lower on the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 2.19%, the S&P 500 Index dropped 2.02%, and the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 2.25%. After the US midterm elections, the Democratic Party will gain a majority in Congress next January. Recent policy discussions within the party have placed more emphasis on strengthening accountability for AI companies. They also stress protecting workers and consumers and paying attention to the impact of data centers on power supply, the environment and local communities.

Anthropic's earliest publicly disclosed financing was its 2021 Series A round, led by Jaan Tallinn, Skype co-founder and investor, raising $124 million. The 2025 Series E and Series F rounds raised approximately $35 billion and $130 billion respectively. The 2026 Series G and Series H rounds raised $300 billion and approximately $650 billion respectively. After the Series H round, the company's disclosed post-money valuation reached $965 billion. According to OECD statistics, AI companies received approximately $258.7 billion in venture capital in 2025, accounting for 61% of total global venture capital, twice the proportion in 2022.

In the first half of 2026, according to WIPO statistics, the proportion of AI financing in global venture capital rose to 77%, with OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI alone accounting for nearly 43%. Before its IPO, Amazon invested approximately $18 billion through convertible bonds and preferred shares. Among the Magnificent Seven, four companies have investment and cooperative supply chain relationships with Anthropic: Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Nvidia. The proportion of revenue generated by purchasing Claude through cloud service providers' marketplace rose from 11% in 2023 to 47% in 2025, and stood at around 44% in the first nine months of 2026. According to Anthropic's latest prospectus released on November 10, seven companies including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft agreed to collectively purchase $26 billion of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price concurrently with the IPO.

In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $33.242 billion. Usage-based revenue was $26.306 billion, about 79%, and subscription revenue was $6.936 billion, about 21%. Customers who spent more than $100,000 in the past 12 months contributed about 74% of revenue in the past 9 months, and their number exceeded 11,900. In the nine months ended September 2026, Anthropic recorded an operating loss of approximately $1.26 billion and a net loss of approximately $104.039 billion. Approximately $94.324 billion of the net loss came from fair value changes of items such as convertible bonds, derivatives and SAFE, and operating cash flow was positive at approximately $6.6 billion. Computing power and infrastructure expenses in the first nine months of 2026 were approximately $18.8 billion, about 57% of revenue in the same period, and the company said this expense is expected to remain its largest operating expense for the foreseeable future.

stories.Headline: Founder seeks angel financing to build an AI-integrated primary and secondary education system
stories.Summary:
An unnamed founder launched a project to build a new primary and secondary education system for the AI era on November 20, 2026. This initiative seeks angel round financing to fund project initiation, team building, and market verification for the new educational model. The founder has already independently completed the design and content production for a full set of courses from primary school to high school. This project aims to develop inclusive basic AI education through teaching in primary and secondary schools to help the general public. The founder is now inviting partners to jointly explore and expand the market as AI education becomes a viable business.

The project targets primary and secondary students, parents, and the general public through a systematic curriculum running from primary to high school. It requires a content, platform, and system supply to help schools, teachers, and the government implement a verifiable education model. The founder seeks to integrate AI into existing Chinese, Mathematics, and English classes rather than adding a separate new course. In China, the AI education market is expected to exceed 1.8 trillion yuan in 2026, with curriculum sub-segments reaching 400 billion yuan. A government Action Plan for Artificial Intelligence plus Education targets basic popularization in schools by 2030, including AI in after-school services.

The founder believes the market lacks general literacy courses and currently focuses too much on programming, robotics, and competitions for top students. They stated that the public needs basic, clear answers on what artificial intelligence is, how to use it, and how to coexist. The founder claims that learning how AI works and knowing its red lines is as fundamental as learning to read and do arithmetic. They intend to open source all teaching materials and solutions to allow teachers to act as co-builders of the system. The founder admits that the actual quality of the courses still needs verification through feedback from the first classrooms and parents.

The general public is affected because they struggle to find their position and practical guarantees while living and working alongside artificial intelligence. Teachers are affected as the system provides them with standard teaching plans, courseware, and exercises they can use directly for classes. The project targets the B-end by treating schools as individual units to deliver courses and help them complete a digital transformation. It targets the G-end by cooperating with government departments to carry out popular science activities and digital literacy events in schools. The C-end focuses on literacy education services that acquire users for free online and monetize through offline services.

The articles state that the current supply side of AI training does not match the official policy roadmap set by government departments. There is a quantified talent gap of 2,000 to 3,600 AI teaching positions per prefecture-level city and 25,000 to 45,000 per province. This gap is expected to drive tax revenue, employment, and economic flow while providing new research topics for various universities. AI technology is presented as a tool to help teachers grade papers and assist parents in breaking down difficult tutoring problems. The system uses traditional teaching practices like listening, speaking, reading, and writing to ensure children truly master the AI content.

The project will next launch an online learning platform where all courses are free and publicly accessible to support remote home learning. The founder will continue expanding the network of collaborators for course proofreading, teaching cooperation, and general content co-creation for the system. The project aims to use online content to build awareness, school projects to generate revenue, and government cooperation for official endorsement. The articles leave the specific financing amount and the equity transfer ratio open for discussion through further communication with potential investors. It remains to be seen if the courses will be successful once they are introduced to the first actual classrooms.

stories.Headline: Oxford researcher Hao Fei proposes cognitive symbionts as the other half of physical AI
stories.Summary:
Hao Fei, a senior researcher in the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford, published a 59-page perspective paper on arXiv, 36Kr's Machine Heart reported on 2026-11-20. The paper is titled "From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence." It argues that the physical AI era has a second intelligent individual besides embodied robots: AI-augmented humans. The paper names the other half of AI's end state "AI-Augmented Human Intelligence (AHI)" and proposes "Cognitive Symbiont" as the system form to achieve it. The article was published at 15:28 on 2026-11-20.

The paper does not propose new algorithms, it advocates a framework, a map of the design space, and a set of evidence standards. AHI asks how smart a specific human being can become with the help of machines. The paper's reference image for the Cognitive Symbiont is Jarvis in Iron Man, always present, long familiar with its owner, able to participate while the owner speaks and acts, and never asking the owner to stop to explain. The paper discusses how to give everyone such a system and how far it should go beyond Jarvis. The symbiont is described as lifelong, embedded, real-time, private, low-friction, and proactive.

Hao Fei writes restrainedly that the article proposes no new algorithms but advocates a framework, a design-space map, and evidence standards. He clearly expresses his expectation that the concept can orient a new AI research paradigm. In that paradigm, the measure of progress is how capable each specific human being becomes. The paper's core thesis is that AI-augmented humans and embodied robots share a cognitive core: long-term memory, modeling of situations and other people's minds, timely intervention, and learning from experience. The two differ only on whose goals, whose body, and who is responsible.

The paper opens with an ordinary day of a researcher: an idea slips away in the morning before she writes it down, a colleague at the afternoon meeting asks for a result from three years ago and she cannot recall the number, and at night she cannot remember how she reasoned through a similar decision. Two further gaps are named: a traveler in a foreign country who does not know how to politely decline an invitation, and a person who has just failed and needs words from someone who truly understands but receives only general encouragement. The first three are failures of access, things humans already own that fail to be present when needed; the last two are gaps in knowledge and support humans cannot fill alone at that moment. None of the five incidents is an intelligence problem, and in every scenario AI that masters the relevant knowledge exists but is not present.

The paper notes that Meta's Muse, xAI's Grok Bot, and OpenAI's Dots, personal intelligences released in 2026, can already track long-term goals, run continuously in the background, and learn user preferences. It sorts four roles in the human-AI relationship: passive assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini; autonomous agents such as Claude Code and Codex; personal intelligences that do things for you in the cloud in your way; and cognitive symbionts close to humans that make humans themselves more capable. The fourth role includes the first three, and the paper distinguishes personal intelligence, which does things for humans in the cloud, from the symbiont, which thinks with humans by their side. The paper divides AI's end state into AGI, asking how smart machines can be, and AHI, asking how much intelligence a specific human can have with machine help, and says the two halves are parallel rather than successive stages, with AHI inheriting every advance of the foundation.

The paper states that human cognitive bandwidth is fixed: working memory holds only a few things, attention focuses on one place at a time, and a day has only 24 hours. AI's ability on isolated tasks keeps rising, but its coupling with a specific human has barely changed: how much it knows about this person, how fast it can intervene, how much disturbance it causes, and how much the person trusts it. The article says the bottleneck has shifted, and the paper's Figure 6 shows the augmentation that has never been realized as a shaded area. The article's text ends mid-sentence, at the gap between what the model can contribute, so the paper's account of the mechanism of relationship transformation is not given. More to follow.

stories.Headline: AI removes professional promotion ladders by eliminating middle tier roles
stories.Summary:
Ray Xian Sen wrote about a brutal workplace shift occurring in 2026. He argues that artificial intelligence is not stealing jobs but removing promotion ladders. This change eliminates workers who merely repeat one year of experience for a decade. The shift targets the disappearing middle tier of professional employment. It affects both new graduates and mid-level managers.

The State Council General Office issued a document in October 2026 with 18 tasks. ShanghaiTech University analyzed 743 million recruitment records from 2022 to July 2026. Demand fell most in basic operation, financial accounting, graphic content, and telesales. AI contraction hits those with one to three years experience earning 5000 to 8000 yuan. A Hangzhou e-commerce company saved 4 million yuan by cutting PMO, data, and test teams.

Tencent headquarters released internal notes on November 16 proposing accelerated organizational flattening. They stated that cadres who only pass on messages and occupy resources should not be obstacles. An International Labour Organization chief macroeconomist introduced the term verification tax for checking AI hallucinations. Ray Xian Sen says the real change is re-pricing people as either costs or assets. He believes value depends on taking responsibility for things AI cannot do.

New graduates are affected because companies now hire people who can take real responsibilities. Junior developers are decreasing in number while senior developers are increasing. People with three to five years of experience find the path upward has become narrower. Positions requiring over three years of experience now account for more than 70 percent. Recruitment for those with less than one year of experience decreased by about 20 percent.

The civil service examination relaxed age limits for the first time since 1994. Application limits moved from 35 to 38 years old for general applicants. Limits for fresh master and doctoral graduates moved from 40 to 43 years old. Over 20 provinces followed this loosening of the age rules. A cloud vendor now requires five years of experience instead of three for solution positions.

The articles leave open how many workers can successfully transition to roles requiring human judgment. They do not state if the civil service age relaxation will permanently solve youth unemployment. The text does not specify which other industries will follow the programming pyramid effect. It remains unclear how many companies will adopt the Tencent flattening model. The future safety line for employees depends on their ability to take overall charge.

stories.Headline: Parents drive growth of screen-free AI hardware for children to balance learning and health
stories.Summary:
Parents recently created a new product category of screen-free AI hardware for children. This trend emerged over the last year to balance AI learning with screen avoidance. Companies launched AI voice printers, painting projectors, sticker machines, and 3D printing learning machines. These devices use voice input and physical output to engage children without screens. Parents are the primary payers for these tools to avoid childhood myopia.

Stickerbox sells coloring stickers for 129 US dollars in North America and sold out 13 times. Spin Master acquired Stickerbox in August for between 35 million and 50 million US dollars. Zhiti Technology created the Huahuabao voice printer and has equity penetration from Lenovo. Zhixiaobai sells an AI-native 3D printing learning machine for 999 yuan in China. myFirst received over 8 million US dollars in financing in March of this year.

The general manager of Zhixiaobai, Guo Dongxu, believes time is the biggest barrier. He stated that competition will shift toward software and content systems as hardware converges. The Taoli Editorial Committee noted that parents fear children falling behind in the AI era. They argued that physical objects provide a closed loop for every AI interaction. This approach turns AI into a creativity tool rather than an electronic pacifier.

Parents are affected by fears regarding vision, concentration, and sleep due to screen time. They worry that AI is rewriting the definition of almost all future occupations. Children are affected by the shift from passive consumption to active creation. The products target primary school students from grades 1 to 6. These users move from talking to machines to creating physical, collectible objects.

Educational consumption in China migrated from offline tutoring to online classes and learning tablets. Generative AI entered office software and search boxes before entering children's rooms. Traditional AI toys often lose novelty within two weeks because they lack physical output. Zhiti Technology previously provided intelligent terminals for 50,000 taxis across 100 Chinese cities. Gongfudou Technology served 100 million parents as a 2D printing software provider.

Companies will now focus on building long-term content relationships to avoid becoming obsolete. Zhixiaobai developed a 3+3 Learning and Creation Growth System for science and innovation. Future success depends on whether these tools grow from simple tools into full systems. The articles leave open whether children will continue using devices after novelty fades. It remains unclear if consumables and content can support a healthy repurchase model.

stories.Headline: Jeff Bezos co-leads Prometheus to build an AI engineer for physical design
stories.Summary:
On November 17, 2026, at the Semafor "Silicon Valley and the World" Summit in Menlo Park, California, Jeff Bezos appeared jointly with physicist Vik Bajaj. Bezos is now co-founder and co-CEO of the AI startup Prometheus. It is the first time he has returned to a CEO role since handing over Amazon in 2021. Bezos invested in the project at its seed stage at the end of 2024. He said on stage that the project is advancing so fast he "could not just sit on the sidelines and watch".

Prometheus has about 250 employees and has raised approximately 14.5 billion US dollars in total capital. Its valuation has soared to 41 billion US dollars. The company disclosed a 6.2 billion dollar first round in November 2025 and a 12 billion dollar round in June 2026. It was incubated at the Foresite Labs incubator in 2024 under the early code name FL2024-008 INC. Shareholders include JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, DST Global and ARCH Venture Partners.

Bezos denied that Prometheus is building humanoid robots or chat-focused large language models. He said the goal is an "Artificial General Engineer", abbreviated AGE. He said, "You can't learn engineering just by reading." He said locking six top physicists including Newton, Einstein and Maxwell in a room to build a toaster would likely leave them at a complete loss. Bajaj, a former Google X core executive and Stanford University School of Medicine professor, said specialized division of labor is already inevitable even in pure language models.

Bezos said Prometheus's system can finish analog chip, radio equipment or valve designs that take an engineering team of 10 to 20 people 6 to 9 months in 12 hours. Blue Origin has privately tested the tool on two projects. An engineer who worked on the Mars Helicopter at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory used one prompt to redesign it, and the model converged to a coaxial counter-rotating configuration highly similar to the real craft. Bezos said of proprietary enterprise data, "never share it, and strictly prevent it from leaking out".

Bajaj said Prometheus uses its self-developed multi-physics field simulation system to generate high-quality synthetic data. The company leased a plant of about 9,300 square meters in the former American Steel Industrial Park in West Oakland, California in August 2026. It has offices in San Francisco, London and Zurich. Kyle Kosic, co-founder of xAI, joined in early 2026 to lead computing power infrastructure. In November 2025 Prometheus acquired General Agents, an agent AI lab co-founded by Sherjil Ozair.

Bezos said the global physical manufacturing industry is worth tens of trillions of US dollars and "it is impossible to build a walled garden here". He said Prometheus will invest directly in some traditional enterprises empowered by its tools. Asked about merging Amazon, Blue Origin and Prometheus, he said, "That's a funny idea, there is nothing to announce". Amazon invested an additional 25 billion US dollars in Anthropic in April 2026 in exchange for a 1 trillion US dollar cloud spending commitment.

stories.Headline: DeepSeek introduces usage limits to manage high computing costs and server stability
stories.Summary:
DeepSeek introduced usage limits for its AI services in November 2026 to manage high costs. This decision affected users who relied on the platform for companionship, consulting, and psychological healing. Many heavy users expressed distress over the potential loss of their extensive chat histories. Some people spent more than ten hours a day interacting with the AI. These users now face a shift away from unlimited free access.

The new rules stop the resumption of inactive conversations older than seven days. Single inputs are now compressed to a limit of about 40,000 words. A daily usage cap now triggers a server busy prompt when quotas are exhausted. These changes target the App and web versions used by ordinary people. The platform aims to recover HBM memory occupied by idle sessions.

DeepSeek has not issued a direct statement, but reports suggest this was a last resort. The company faced multiple service failures, including slow responses and high generation delays. Technical logic shows that long conversations accumulate KV cache in GPU memory. This resource mismatch caused queuing and stuttering during periods of peak traffic. Reallocating memory helps the platform serve active users more efficiently.

Heavy users feel these limits acutely because their deep contexts step on the quota edge. Some affected individuals have started charging fees to help others connect to the API. Many users are now actively asking DeepSeek to implement reasonable payment options. They want to pay for higher computing power priority and longer conversations. These users view the limits as a unilateral relationship downgrade.

Computing power costs have risen, with H100 contract prices increasing 65 percent by October 2026. In the first quarter of 2026, over 300 small AI companies ceased operations. Seed round financing in the domestic AI sector fell 11 percent year on year. Pure API startups struggled because they lacked computing power stockpiles or traffic ecosystems. This environment makes the old premise of infinite capital subsidies unsustainable.

Doubao now uses a layered structure where heavy functions require payment to cover free ones. OpenAI launched ChatGPT Ads on August 31, 2026, reaching a 1 billion dollar revenue run rate. The industry is shifting from a scale first strategy to a unit economic model. It remains unknown if small platforms can replicate the advertising success of OpenAI. The articles leave open how DeepSeek will retain users after these limits.

stories.Headline: Online literature platforms crack down on AI generated content to protect human creators
stories.Summary:
A viral statement calling for a one day pause on AI updates earned 43,000 likes on November 20, 2026. This movement reflects a deep divide between the short drama industry and the online literature circle. While short dramas embrace the technology, literature platforms are actively fighting against AI generated content. Multiple purges of AI texts have occurred throughout the current year. These actions aim to protect original creators from being replaced by automated systems.

Tomato targeted low quality AI content in February and May of this year. Qidian banned AI written texts in July and processed hundreds of novels in August. On October 30, Qidian and QQ Reading announced further crackdowns on AI abuse in contracted works. These platforms will now cancel welfare benefits for authors who use AI. These rules apply to works with over ten thousand paid subscribers on the Qidian platform.

Platform editors and administrators are responsible for these governance rounds to stop AI abuse. They state that AI generated works are often not good to read. Officials argue that substantial cash rewards are flowing to the wrong recipients. They believe AI books seize benefits that should belong to original human creators. Platforms want to ensure that paid readers are not paying for machine generated words.

Readers complain that works on the leaderboards are still written by AI. Nigerian writer Jerry Adedayo Farad lost a 2 million US dollar deal for his novel. Publishers now avoid novels suspected of being AI generated to protect their investments. Some penalized authors claim they only used AI for grammar and polishing. These creators feel wronged because they wrote the original manuscripts manually.

High output was once a core competition threshold for online literature authors. Top creators like Tangjiasanshao and Mai Bao Xiao Lang Jun updated 8,000 words daily. Qidian previously required 4,000 words for VIP attendance bonuses, while Jinjiang required 3,000. One Qidian author averaged 20,000 words daily using the Doubao large language model. This high volume removed the competitive edge previously held by manual writers.

Qidian uses an AI detection tool called Motong to identify machine written texts. A Nature study showed humans only identify AI poems with 46.6 percent accuracy. Research in Science Advances suggests AI makes stories similar, reducing collective creativity. Another study found AI polishing decreases writing complexity by 21 to 50 percent. The articles leave open whether AI detection tools are truly reliable for platforms.

stories.Headline: US and Singapore authorities investigate Megaspeed International over AI chip trade
stories.Summary:
The U.S. Department of Commerce and Singapore Police Force investigated Megaspeed International for its AI chip trade. This company, formerly 7 Road International, grew rapidly into a high-profile player in the NVIDIA supply chain. Investigations peaked in June 2025 with raids on the company's business site in Singapore. Investigators questioned the then CEO, Huang Le, regarding the destination of advanced chips. The probe spanned the United States, Singapore, and Malaysia.

Megaspeed shifted to cloud computing in 2023 and joined the NVIDIA Cloud Partner ecosystem. From May 2024 to February 2026, related businesses imported NVIDIA products worth 4.13 billion U.S. dollars. In November 2025, it imported 17,454 GB300 units worth approximately 787 million U.S. dollars. Total NVIDIA hardware imports reached 4.6 billion U.S. dollars and 136,000 GPUs by November 2025. Assets grew from 32.9 million U.S. dollars in 2023 to nearly 3 billion U.S. dollars in 2024.

The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security checked if chips reached restricted end users. Singapore Police investigated false declarations and whether equipment was shipped to undeclared locations. Huang Le provided inaccurate information to downplay her role and received a stern warning. She had her passport confiscated and was later barred from re-entering Singapore. The Singapore Police sought limited support from the FBI and server supplier Supermicro.

Clients used remote access to obtain computing power without owning chips or building computer rooms. Some users flew 80TB of training data on hard drives to Malaysia to rent servers. The Malaysian government now requires a strategic trade license for U.S. high-performance AI chips. This regulation, announced July 14, 2025, focuses on whether chips flow to other destinations. The business model affected brokers who converted hardware into rentable cloud computing power.

Megaspeed began as a gaming firm focused on overseas game distribution and operation. It utilized Malaysia's abundant land and power resources, especially in the state of Johor. The company posted a post-tax loss of 20 million U.S. dollars in 2024. High upfront costs included GPU procurement, data center leasing, and electricity prepayments. This growth occurred during a global GPU shortage and rapid Southeast Asian data center expansion.

The investigation into Megaspeed and six other related individuals is still ongoing. A gap of 50,000 chips exists between NVIDIA's government reports and external trade records. NVIDIA claimed this discrepancy resulted from equipment in other warehouses not previously counted. It remains unclear if the company violated specific export control requirements. The articles leave the final legal status of the company open.

stories.Headline: AI power systems integrate lighting and industrial electronics to meet rising data center energy demands
stories.Summary:
Modern AI power supply systems emerged from a mixed evolution of lighting, automotive, and industrial electronics capabilities. This technological convergence happened as AI chip power consumption and cabinet power density rose to megawatt levels. The process integrates gallium nitride, silicon carbide, and silicon based power technologies into computing infrastructure. These older industrial capabilities became important again to meet the massive power demands of AI data centers. This evolution allows for more GPUs to be deployed in the same computer room space.

The system requires rectification, backup power, and multi-level DC conversion to deliver power to GPUs. Google released a plus or minus 400V DC solution for 1MW cabinets in 2025. NVIDIA promoted an 800V high-voltage DC architecture in 2026 with Google, Microsoft, and the Open Compute Project. Texas Instruments estimates that 48V architectures for 1MW cabinets would require nearly 200 kg of copper. Higher voltages like 800V reduce current from 20833 amperes to about 1250 amperes to lower resistance loss.

Texas Instruments launched high-density power devices integrating 650V gallium nitride power transistors in 2025. Infineon released a high-voltage intermediate bus conversion reference design based on 650V gallium nitride in 2026. Innoscience cooperates with NVIDIA to promote 800V DC AI data center power supplies. These companies aim to reduce copper loss and space burdens caused by large currents. They use different materials to divide work based on voltages, power densities, and switching frequencies.

AI data center operators and GPU manufacturers are affected by these power supply architecture changes. Gallium nitride is used for high-frequency and high-power density conversion links in these systems. Silicon carbide provides advantages in high power and voltage resistance for the infrastructure. Silicon remains necessary for low-cost control, protection, and power management functions. These materials ensure that input power is effectively delivered to the chips without excessive heat.

Gallium nitride technology grew from the semiconductor lighting industry and the development of blue LEDs. Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano, and Shuji Nakamura won the 2014 Nobel Prize for their early achievements. Japan invested 550 million yen between 1987 and 1990 to commercialize blue LEDs through Toyoda Gosei. China launched the National Semiconductor Lighting Project in June 2003 to expand this industrial scale. China's semiconductor lighting industry grew from 90 billion yuan in 2003 to 4.245 trillion yuan by 2015.

Jingcan Semiconductor enabled the production of 12-inch gallium nitride wafers in China as early as 2021. Shanghai New Micro Semiconductor is building a gallium nitride power foundry platform for various voltages. Shenzhen Pinghu Laboratory provides a public pilot platform for 8-inch silicon carbide and gallium nitride chips. The articles leave open how these global technology competitions will evolve between China, the US, and Japan. Future developments will determine how these materials further integrate into the global AI power chain.

stories.Headline: Shanghai AI Laboratory releases Sage S2.1 Flash science multimodal agent
stories.Summary:
The Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory released Sage S2.1 Flash on November 16, 2026. This science multimodal agent combines tool use, coding, and search with instrument and molecular inputs. The lab published a benchmark table comparing it to Claude Opus, GPT-5.6 Sol, Qwen, and GLM. Weights for the model are available on Hugging Face under the InternLM organization. It is a full-stack science agent SKU designed for automating notebook-style machine learning engineering.

The 320B MoE model requires FP8 builds or full precision shards for hosting. It unifies ten scientific modalities, including crystal structures, molecular graphs, and protein or nucleic acid sequences. It also ingests light curves, ECG, EEG, spectra, mass spectrometry, and X-ray diffraction. The model uses a shared agent harness for tool-use and search after modality encoders. Demos show the agent using CAD, QGIS, Blender, and 3D Slicer for scientific workflows.

The Shanghai AI Laboratory claims the model is a single-model story rather than a chain. They report a 90.3 score on MLE-bench Lite and 72.2 on OfficeQA Pro. The lab states the model achieved 37.1 on SpreadsheetBench 2 and 25.0 on Harvey LAB. They report a 60.6 on SWE-bench Pro and 87.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. The lab frames the agent as a tool for multi-step workflows with visual feedback.

Third-party commentators noted that weights appeared on Hugging Face before the official marketing site launched. ML engineers are affected by the model's positioning for automating machine learning engineering tasks. Finance and operations teams may use the SpreadsheetBench 2 and Workspace-Bench productivity capabilities. Users in regulated industries must align usage with institutional IRB and export rules. Some reports mention promotional API pricing relative to GLM-5.3-Flash through early December 2026.

The lab's release follows an open-weight push similar to DeepSeek usage limits and Alibaba Qwen4 Max. Science agents intersect with biosafety and export debates, including DHS DeepSeek removal orders. Western labs have released different science agents, such as Periodic Labs Neon and Nvidia Nemotron. Terminal-Bench-Science previously showed that leading Western agents had sub-30% resolution on real research tasks. The model's design mimics how graduate students work across various tools in one afternoon.

Users should now confirm licenses, VRAM needs, and data residency rules for their jurisdictions. Teams are encouraged to run private benchmarks on their own instrument suites for verification. The articles leave open whether the vendor-reported benchmarks will be matched by independent harness logs. It remains unclear if the promotional API pricing will be maintained after December. The actual reliability of the agent depends on governed chat patterns and MCP hygiene.

stories.Headline: UK AI minister rejects calls for Britain to build its own sovereign frontier model
stories.Summary:
Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI minister, rejected calls for Britain to build its own sovereign frontier model during an event in Silicon Valley, arguing that access to American technology matters more than developing a homegrown rival. Speaking on a panel alongside representatives from OpenAI and Google DeepMind, he said he did not think the UK needed to build a frontier model from scratch to be a serious AI player. He added that if the country wanted a sovereign capability, it should focus on safety and regulation rather than competing at the frontier. His remarks drew immediate criticism from startup founders, one of whom said she was so angry she could barely speak.

The minister's position conflicts with the UK's stated ambition to build sovereign AI capability, which the articles describe as a goal the government has previously set out. Narayan argued that the UK should rely on partnerships with foreign labs rather than fund its own frontier model, and he pointed to the UK's AI Safety Institute as the country's real sovereign asset. Critics said the approach leaves British startups dependent on American companies and undermines the UK Sovereign AI Fund, a vehicle the articles mention without giving its size or budget. The articles give no date for when any policy decision will be made.

Eleanor Ward, a partner at venture firm Entrepreneurs First, said the minister's comments were a slap in the face for founders building in the UK and asked who would want to build a frontier model here under those conditions. She said the UK was outsourcing its AI future to US labs and that the government should be backing British companies instead. Another founder, whose name the articles give only as the head of a UK AI startup, said the UK risked becoming a client state of American AI. Narayan did not respond directly to the criticism in the articles.

The backlash comes as the UK government has been trying to position itself as a leader in AI safety and regulation while falling behind the US and China on frontier model development. The articles say the UK Sovereign AI Fund was set up to support domestic AI companies, though they give no figures for its funding or the number of firms it has backed. Several founders said they would reconsider building in the UK if the government's stance did not change. The articles do not say whether the government plans to review its position.

stories.Headline: Hoplite raises $5.5m to let developers run AI coding agent swarms in the cloud
stories.Summary:
Hoplite, an Irish-US startup that lets developers run teams of AI coding assistants in the cloud, has raised $5.5m in a funding round backed by Stripe founders Patrick and John Collison, Paul Graham and other investors, Sifted reported on 20 November 2026. The round was led by venture firm Khosla Ventures, with participation from Susa Ventures and BoxGroup, according to the article. Hoplite was founded by Killian Loughman and Salvatore Cagliostro, and the company says its platform is already used by more than 100 teams. The startup describes its product as the easiest way for developers to run AI coding agents, which are programmes that can write and test software largely autonomously.

The funding is intended to support Hoplite's work on letting developers run swarms of AI coding agents in the cloud, the article says. Loughman said the company wants to make it simple for developers to run many agents at once without managing infrastructure themselves. The article states that Hoplite's platform is used by teams at companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, though it does not give further details on those customers. It also says the company plans to use the money to grow its team and expand its product.

Loughman said in the article that the goal is to let developers focus on building rather than on managing agents, and he described the current tools as requiring too much setup. He said Hoplite handles the infrastructure so that developers can run many agents in parallel. Cagliostro said the company is seeing strong demand from teams that want to use AI agents for coding tasks. The article does not include further direct comments from the investors.

The article notes that Hoplite is based in Ireland and the US, and that the AI coding agent space has attracted growing investor interest. It says the company will use the funding to hire and to expand its platform. The article does not say what specific product changes are planned or when they will arrive. More to follow.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA releases 14 Nemotron-Labs-Sigma diffusion language model checkpoints at 3B and 8B scales
stories.Summary:
NVIDIA released a collection of 14 open checkpoints called Nemotron-Labs-Sigma on November 20, 2026. This new family of continuous diffusion language models denoises text within a smooth 16-D embedding space. The release includes models at 3B and 8B parameter scales to provide various options for users. This approach differs from most diffusion models that work on discrete tokens.

The system requires one NVIDIA GPU from the Ampere, Lovelace, Hopper, or Blackwell series to run in bfloat16. It offers a context window of 4,096 tokens, though the Sigma-8B-instruct version supports 8,192 tokens. The 14 checkpoints include instruct versions, self-speculative variants, and few-step distilled models at NFE 2, 4, 8, and 16. Performance varies, with the Sigma-8B-instruct model reaching 91.96 on GSM8K but only 17.00 on AIME25.

The NVIDIA research team is responsible for the project and describes Sigma as the first large-scale family of its kind. They stated that working in a smooth latent space makes trajectory steering and few-step distillation practical for text. The team noted that the 8B speculative model runs 3.46 times faster than autoregressive decoding on one GB200. They also highlighted that the 8-step distilled 8B model maintains a high average score of 70.34.

The model uses a Ministral-style decoder-only Transformer with rotary embeddings and grouped-query attention. Training involved an autoregressive warm start of 1T tokens followed by 0.3T tokens of diffusion training. Generation occurs in blocks of 64 tokens, which are committed to a KV cache. The researchers recommend using a temperature of 0.3 and guidance of 3 at 32 DDIM steps for inference.

stories.Headline: AI training platforms pay $7 to $150 an hour but gate most work behind degrees
stories.Summary:
AI training jobs pay people to write prompts, rate chatbot answers and check code, and in November 2026 published rates run from $7 an hour on one Outlier listing in the Philippines to $150+ an hour for DataAnnotation coding work. The work is remote, flexible and real, but it is also unstable, mostly gated behind a degree, and full of unpaid minutes that no landing page mentions. Every platform in the guide promises "no AI experience required", a line the guide calls true and misleading. The guide sets out the pay each platform publishes itself, checked on 10 November 2026, along with the requirements behind that pay, the unpaid time and the scams that copy the format. Outlier, DataAnnotation, Mercor, Handshake AI, Alignerr, Mindrift and Prolific are named as real companies that pay, and most publish a fixed weekly or twice-monthly payout schedule.

Outlier lists general work at up to $18 an hour and Handshake AI lists evaluation work at up to $17, while DataAnnotation's FAQ now lists $25 to $50 though reviews from mid-2026 put its base nearer $20. Outlier requires at least an associate degree and DataAnnotation a bachelor's or equivalent experience, while Prolific is the main door with no credential check. DataAnnotation's Starter Assessment takes about an hour and you get one attempt, and Handshake AI does not pay for onboarding unless the Project Terms say so. Outlier pays weekly on Tuesdays through PayPal, Airtm or ACH bank transfer, DataAnnotation pays through PayPal within a few days of a request, and Mercor pays every Wednesday through Stripe or Wise. Outlier is run by Scale AI and claims more than 900,000 experts, and its onboarding takes 30 to 90 minutes and needs a valid ID, a phone from your country, a resume and a LinkedIn profile.

DataAnnotation's trust page says plainly that it will never ask you for money or any other form of payment, and that it pays you, not the other way around. The FTC's alert on task scams describes an unexpected message on WhatsApp, Telegram, text or social media offering quick money for online "tasks" such as "optimization" or "product boosting". You watch fake earnings pile up in an app, then you are told to deposit your own money, usually in crypto, to unlock the next tasks or withdraw what you earned. Three checks catch nearly all of it: you found the platform yourself rather than being messaged, you applied on the platform's own website, and you never paid anything for a starter kit, a training course or a verification fee. Real platforms do ask for ID verification and tax forms, but only inside their logged-in dashboard.

An Oxford Economics report estimated that data annotation supported nearly 200,000 flexible earning opportunities in the US in 2024 and contributed $5.7 billion to US GDP. Outlier claims 900,000+ experts and $600M+ paid out, and Handshake AI claims $500M+ in payouts to 188,000+ fellows, though those are company figures, not audited ones. Outlier names three core tasks on its own homepage: write a challenging prompt, create grading rubrics, and rate and rank answers. DataAnnotation describes its general projects as evaluating chatbot responses, comparing AI outputs and testing image generation, and it stresses that the work needs critical thinking and fact-checking, not clicking. Independent review sites such as Breaking Even describe empty task queues, removal from projects without explanation, and unpaid assessments that never turn into paid work.

Mercor recruits domain experts such as scientists, doctors and lawyers and matches them to AI labs on contracts, and in October 2025 it told TechCrunch it had 30,000+ experts earning over $85 an hour on average and paid out more than $1.5 million a day. Its first Stripe payout has a 7-day hold, which is Stripe's rule, not Mercor's. Handshake AI runs the Handshake AI Fellowship, open to generalists as well as experts, and its AI Evaluation Specialist role tops out at $17 an hour while specialist roles in energy, finance, game development and software engineering go up to $80 to $150. The Fellowship is US-only, and Handshake says you must be based in the US and have valid work authorization. Alignerr, powered by Labelbox, claims 100,000+ experts and pays only for tasks that pass quality review on its pay-per-accepted-task projects.

Mindrift is built by Toloka and shows the price of each task before you start it, and it states openly that it is not a job, with no employment contract and no fixed hours. Prolific is a research platform, not an AI training platform first, but some of its studies ask participants to evaluate AI models, and researchers must pay at least £6 or $8 an hour while Prolific recommends £9 or $12. Asked whether you need a degree, Outlier's FAQ answers that you need at least an associate degree, and DataAnnotation's baseline is a bachelor's degree or equivalent real-world experience. Handshake AI's sign-up page says "no AI experience required" directly above listings tagged Bachelor's, Master's and PhD. DataAnnotation says someone with a bachelor's degree and no work history could qualify for its general projects, and that real-world experience counts as much as formal education.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT-6 Astra
stories.Summary:
Hebbia tested a prerelease build of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra in August and September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model, with domain experts writing or auditing the criteria against source documents. The tests covered two parts of a banker’s work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief. In the tests, GPT-6 Astra scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, and 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question. It also met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure, and it ranked first on both following the brief and presentation quality.

Hebbia’s Matrix tool links answers to the documents behind them, and users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage, while slide footnotes lead back to the source material. In a hypothetical example described in the article, a banker helping a client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company with roughly 2,000 files to review could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could then bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis and turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template. In that workflow, GPT-6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer and then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines.

Kavita Anand, a member of technical staff for product at Hebbia, said the company had been strong partners with OpenAI over Hebbia’s lifetime and that the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in quality outputs and accuracy have been truly surprising. She said traceability is really important to users because they base millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI comes back with, and citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer. She said that when looking at a data room with thousands of documents even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit, and that she wants a deck made in her firm’s branding that looks like a human-made slide. She said past models shone on one dimension or the other, while GPT-6 Astra is the first model Hebbia has seen that is number one on both craft and instruction following.

Anand described what a better first draft could make possible, saying GPT-6 Astra can create precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines and that the overnighters professionals have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing its output. She also sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess, and she said getting an important signal a few hours before competitors could let users start thinking about it and process more opportunities a human is not manually hunting. Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources, and it wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources and more time assessing a deal.

stories.Headline: OpenAI strengthens GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol safeguards, cutting reasoning extraction attack success from 54.0% to 0.2%
stories.Summary:
OpenAI published a post on November 20, 2026 titled "Combatting adversarial distillation," describing how it detects and disrupts adversarial distillation and how it strengthened protections for its models' protected reasoning. Adversarial distillation is when an actor uses a frontier model's outputs without authorization to train another model with similar capabilities. OpenAI said it combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated extraction attempts. OpenAI said it strengthened defenses against protected reasoning extraction in GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming, the average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT-6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT-6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

OpenAI said its updated safeguards align more closely with those it uses for biology and cybersecurity. OpenAI said it places particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting protected reasoning, the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought. OpenAI said these traces can contain information the final answer leaves out, making them especially valuable training data for another model. OpenAI described a September disclosure of attacks that moved encrypted reasoning from one conversation into another and asked the model to reveal the reasoning in user-readable form. OpenAI said it strengthened protections across user, workspace, organization, and model-family boundaries, including closing a pathway that could expose another user's encrypted reasoning.

OpenAI said that with GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol it ties a model's protected reasoning to the conversation history that produced it. OpenAI said that as new messages are added, the model can build on its earlier reasoning, and that if an earlier message is rewritten, its API drops the reasoning that followed it. OpenAI said it also prevents older model families with weaker safeguards from reading GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol's protected reasoning. OpenAI said that when its systems detect unauthorized adversarial distillation campaigns, which often include coordinated attempts to extract its models' reasoning, it investigates the accounts responsible. OpenAI said that when it identifies violations, it enforces against the network of accounts, consistent with its policies and terms of service.

OpenAI said that through investigations of each campaign it generates insights that allow it to upgrade its defenses to better detect similar activity. OpenAI said it shares indicators of compromise with other model providers so they can investigate related abuse on their own services. OpenAI said its consistent-standards policy establishes shared standards for safeguards and coordinated enforcement across providers offering its models. OpenAI said it works closely with partners where appropriate to uphold these standards and strengthen protections across deployments. OpenAI said sharing relevant findings across industry and government where appropriate can help disrupt campaigns and enable model developers and providers to better identify and defend against attempts to distill frontier models.

OpenAI said distillation is a common machine-learning technique in which one model learns from data produced by another, for example another model's answers, its reasoning, or its judgments about which answers are better and why. OpenAI said that beyond intellectual property concerns, unauthorized distillation poses serious safety risks, because a second model can learn advanced frontier capabilities without inheriting the safeguards that govern how the original model can use them. OpenAI said the concern is especially clear in dual-use domains like cybersecurity and biology, where a model that helps defenders find vulnerabilities in software could also help an attacker exploit them. OpenAI said that in an internal study on how cyber capabilities transfer, it used the content normally visible to users, final responses, reasoning summaries, and tool interactions, as its baseline for distillation. OpenAI said it started each training run from the same pretrained student model and created a supervised fine-tuning dataset consisting primarily of trajectories from Astra-level teacher models working on coding and defensive cybersecurity tasks.

OpenAI said each trajectory includes all of the steps a model takes as it works through a task, including any tool interactions and its final response. OpenAI said it evaluated each student after fine-tuning and again after a lightweight round of reinforcement learning in cybersecurity and coding environments. OpenAI said that after supervised fine-tuning, the student trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperformed the student trained on reasoning summaries. OpenAI said that after reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets. OpenAI said its cyber distillation results suggest that protecting reasoning traces can limit cyber capability transfer, even when the underlying task is one allowed under its usage policies.

OpenAI said that across many such interactions, exact reasoning traces can teach a student skills that generalize beyond the tasks the teacher originally performed. OpenAI said it will continue studying how much additional capability transfers across different student models and distillation training recipes. OpenAI said it defends against adversarial distillation at two complementary levels of its safeguard stack, with model behavior, classifier checks, and API controls at the request level and patterns in request-level and account-level signals at the campaign level. OpenAI said attacks uncovered in investigations become examples for training and testing its safeguards. OpenAI said its adversarial training teaches models to recognize reasoning extraction attempts and refuse to disclose protected reasoning, while preserving responses to legitimate requests for explanations and assistance.

OpenAI said adversarial training examples come from successful attacks identified through internal automated red-teaming, investigations, and responsible disclosures of potential security weaknesses from outside researchers or industry partners. OpenAI said it uses input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments, applying to both streaming and non-streaming responses. OpenAI said tool-call coverage is important because a model can expose protected reasoning in a tool's arguments without including it in its final answer, and output classifiers can block suspected leaks before that content reaches the caller. OpenAI said that in static evaluations it replays a fixed set of previously successful attacks to see which still expose protected reasoning, and in adaptive evaluations automated AI red-teamers adjust their approach based on how the system responds. OpenAI said black-box testing gives testers the same view an external user would have, while white-box testing gives them additional information about the system to help them develop stronger attacks.

OpenAI said that in its adaptive black-box evaluation it tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier request or the current one. OpenAI said that on GPT-6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards, the average attack success rate was below 1% for each attack type, and both rates were substantially lower than on GPT-6 Astra with its original safeguards. OpenAI said it is now applying selected safeguard improvements to GPT-6 Astra as well. OpenAI said it has seen multiple unauthorized adversarial distillation campaigns on its platform this year. OpenAI said it shared initial findings from those campaigns.

More to follow.
