stories.Headline: Siemens launches Eigen Engineering Agent in India
stories.Summary:
Siemens launched its Eigen Engineering Agent in India on November 20, 2026, at the Transform - Siemens India Innovation Day in New Delhi, according to TechGig. The industrial AI agent is designed to automate repetitive engineering tasks, and the company said it can autonomously perform tasks such as PLC coding and Human-Machine-Interface visualisation while adhering to industrial safety standards. Before the India launch, Eigen was piloted by 16 Siemens clients in the country. Siemens reported that the agent can execute tasks two to five times faster than manual methods, and humans remain responsible for the final deployment of tasks even with Eigen's autonomous capabilities.

Pilot results indicated that the agent reduced repetitive engineering work by over 50 per cent and boosted productivity by 20 to 30 per cent in specific cases. Small and medium enterprises can access the agent through Siemens' existing TIA Portal, which the company said gives them a route to the technology without a separate platform. The launch ties the agent to India's manufacturing sector, with the company positioning it for both large operations and smaller firms. The article gives no pricing, availability timeline or further rollout details beyond the India launch and the TIA Portal access route.

Siemens AG CTO Dr Dirk Didascalou said Eigen can help accelerate growth in India by giving engineers more time for innovation, and he added that bringing AI into the engineering workflow helps manage complexity and strengthens India's industrial transformation. Siemens India CEO Sunil Mathur highlighted Eigen's potential to drive India's manufacturing leap, especially for small and medium enterprises. The company states that automating repetitive work frees engineers for more complex work and accelerates development. Humans remain responsible for the final deployment of tasks, according to the article.

The launch was held during Transform - Siemens India Innovation Day in New Delhi, and the pilot involved 16 Siemens clients in the country before the India release. The article reports the productivity gains of 20 to 30 per cent in specific cases and the reduction of over 50 per cent in repetitive engineering work as pilot results rather than guaranteed outcomes. SMEs can reach the agent through the existing TIA Portal, which the article presents as the access path for smaller firms. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the launch and the pilot results.

stories.Headline: Cognizant opens 165,000 sq ft AI learning centre in Chennai to build global AI skills
stories.Summary:
Cognizant inaugurated Phase-1 of its Immersive Learning Center at its Siruseri campus in Chennai on Thursday, according to a company release reported by TechGig on November 20, 2026. The Nasdaq-listed technology company said the facility is meant to develop AI skills at scale and to support its commitment to an AI-ready global workforce. Cognizant stated that the centre will undergo further expansion in subsequent phases beyond this first one. The company described the centre as integrating modern workplace design with digital learning infrastructure and flexible environments for instructor-led learning, collaboration and ideation.

The facility spans 165,000 square feet and features 58 classrooms equipped with 1,822 learning seats, along with 208 multipurpose seats, collaborative spaces and meeting rooms. A work café, a library and flexible town hall spaces are also part of the new centre, the company said. Cognizant is advancing its frontier workforce model, which focuses on building the human capabilities required to translate AI investments into enterprise outcomes. Earlier this year the company committed to scaling its Frontier-certified workforce to 5,000 Frontier Certified Engineers and 10,000 Frontier Business Operators.

Rajesh Varrier, President of Global Operations and Chairman and Managing Director of Cognizant India, commented on the investment in the release. He said that as an AI Builder the company's focus is on harnessing AI to transform businesses and on developing the skills its associates need to lead that transformation. Varrier added that the facility reflects continued investment in creating spaces for learning and collaboration. He said associates will build innovative, AI-enabled solutions for clients within these spaces.

Cognizant maintains an operational presence across India, with locations including Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Coimbatore, Delhi-NCR, GIFT City, Hyderabad, Indore, Kochi, Kolkata, Mangaluru, Mumbai, Pune and Visakhapatnam. The articles do not say what the later phases of the centre will involve or when they are expected to be completed. They also do not give a timeline for reaching the targets of 5,000 Frontier Certified Engineers and 10,000 Frontier Business Operators. No further details on the next steps were provided in the reports.

stories.Headline: Hugging Face researchers create harness adapters to boost AI model performance and efficiency
stories.Summary:
Hugging Face researchers introduced harness adapters on November 20, 2026, to improve model performance and cost. They used reinforcement learning to adapt a favorite model to a specific agent harness. This process creates a custom adapter for a target harness and task distribution. The team focused on real world software engineering tasks to test their method. They aimed to share a reusable recipe for other users to reproduce these results.

The team used Qwen3.8-27B and trained LoRA adapters for Pi 1.5.2, OpenCode 2.2.7, and Hermes Agent v0.22.6. They used TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer, OpenEnv, and harbor on the Hub in Jobs for training. The process involved Terminal-Bench 2.1, the hard subset of SWE-bench Pro, and DeepSWE benchmarks. They used SWE-smith for Python and Go, SWE-Gym from TaskTrove, and Tasksmith for tasks. These tools helped them filter 1,127 candidates down to a final set of 278 tasks.

The researchers stated that models target general performance rather than specific harnesses and tasks. They explained that combining a model and harness often leaves performance and efficiency on the table. By using reinforcement learning, they claimed they could squeeze everything out of a model. They noted that RL on a custom task distribution yields more accurate and efficient models. The team provided a collection of adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, and a safeagents plugin.

The base Qwen3.8-27B model scored 39 percent on Terminal-Bench 2.1 using the pi harness. With a custom adapter, the pass@1 score rose to 55 percent for the same harness. Average token usage dropped from 2.9K to 1.5K tokens per task because the model reasoned less. The model performed better the first time and called fewer tools during its operations. Each harness adapter beat the base model on both performance and efficiency for its harness.

The team built a data pipeline using the Hub, OpenEnv, and Repo2RLEnv for agentic coding. They used Tasksmith to generate 24 tasks from 30 merged pull requests in 10 Python repositories. They filtered tasks to remove duplicates, those with restrictive licenses, and 253 tasks from target benchmarks. They used openenv validate to ensure reference solutions earned maximum rewards and canaries scored low. Qwen3.8-27B attempted 442 scored tasks to identify 171 tasks it solved only some of the time.

The researchers merged the three LoRAs into one super adapter for pi, Hermes Agent, and OpenCode. They used docker images with pre-installed harnesses to train the model inside the chosen environments. The trainer learned from exact tokens recorded by a proxy between the harness and vLLM. They repaired and complexified 522 rejected tasks with Tasksmith to repeat the validation process. The authors left open the question of what the model really learned to do.

stories.Headline: Samsung and SK hynix values dive as AI chip rally ends
stories.Summary:
The KOSPI index fell 30 percent from early October and 45 percent from its June peak. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix saw their values dive 32.82 percent and 39.33 percent respectively. These losses occurred as the AI chip rally ended in November 2026. Investors who bought equity products like ETFs now face mounting losses. The market downturn has caused a significant shift in market capitalization rankings.

Total KOSPI market capitalization shrank from 7,449.6 trillion won in June to 3,991.4 trillion won. This represents a loss of 3,458 trillion won, or 46.4 percent of the total. Samsung Biologics rose to fifth place, while Celltrion returned to the top ten at ninth. Hyundai Motor fell to eighth place as Samsung Securities cut its target price to 380,000 won. Investor deposits shrank to 81.5669 trillion won during this period of volatility.

Citibank estimates that household stock investment losses will reach 563 trillion won in the second half. This impact is comparable to a base rate increase of 0.50 to 0.75 percentage points. The South Korean government has not yet produced clear measures to stabilize the market. This differs from Taiwan's FSC, which tightened short-selling restrictions and used a stabilization fund. Officials have stood by while the market dropped 30 percent in six weeks.

Investors who used retirement savings for stocks are now affected by the market slide. Average daily KOSPI trading volume hit a 12 year low of 239 million shares on November 19. Hyundai Motor faces pressure from a stronger won and price competition with Chinese electric vehicles. Chinese passenger EV exports to South Korea jumped 99.2 percent to 3.35991 billion dollars. Korean-made passenger EV market share fell to 48.7 percent while Chinese vehicles reached 43.5 percent.

The market previously rallied in June during a surge in AI chip investments. Samsung Electronics previously trailed SK hynix in HBM3E, with its market share falling to around 20 percent. Samsung later restored its HBM market share to the high 30 percent range in the third quarter. The government is now pushing for production tax credits for domestically built electric vehicles. They also want to strengthen R&D support for autonomous-driving AI and computing hardware.

Samsung appointed President Hwang Sang-joon to lead memory and President Choi Won-joon to lead the MX division. AI glasses launch on December 10, and a humanoid robot will debut at CES 2027. Samsung aims for HBM4E next year and HBM5 in 2028 to regain its technology lead. The articles leave open the timing of the National Assembly's tax subcommittee decisions. It remains uncertain if the foundry business will turn profitable or if shares will rebound.

stories.Headline: Situational Awareness holds AI infrastructure stakes including Nebius and Sandisk at September 30
stories.Summary:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund Situational Awareness held artificial intelligence infrastructure businesses such as Nebius Group, Sandisk and Bloom Energy throughout the third quarter, before a number of positions fell in October, according to a regulatory filing reported on November 17, 2026. The fund had call options in Nebius, Sandisk, Bloom Energy and the Roundhill Memory ETF as of September 30, and the filing did not say whether those holdings were held or liquidated during the October market sell-off. The fund's position in CleanSpark was worth around $39 million, while its interests in IREN and Bitdeer were worth over $21 million and $20 million respectively, and its Fermi position was valued at more than $11 million. Several AI-linked stocks subsequently suffered significant drops, with SharonAI down 55% in October, IREN down 41% and Nebius down 35%, and Nebius and CoreWeave also saw selling pressure on Monday as investors decreased exposure to AI infrastructure businesses.

The new portfolio disclosure comes after reports that Situational Awareness lost 67% of its portfolio value in July as AI-related assets slumped, and the September holdings show its ongoing bet on data centers, memory chips and computer infrastructure notwithstanding market turmoil. Investors will be looking at the fund's next quarterly filing to see if it lowered its position during the October sell-off, or stayed with its AI-focused investment strategy. The filing lists the fund's positions as of September 30 but does not state whether those holdings were held or sold during the October declines. The article gives no further detail on the fund's plans or on the size of its current stakes.

The articles do not say who at the fund is responsible for the strategy beyond naming Aschenbrenner as its head, and they carry no direct comment from him or from the fund on the new bets. The filing itself, cited by the article, is the source for the holdings and values, and it does not address the October sell-off. No statement from the fund about its intentions appears in the material. The article also does not say what the fund plans to do next.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Together AI launches free storage accelerator to speed data pipelines for GPU clusters
stories.Summary:
Together AI launched the Together Storage Accelerator on November 19, 2026, to speed up data pipelines. Authors Pavneet Ahluwalia and Vinamra Jain introduced this distributed caching layer for Together GPU Clusters. The tool prevents compute resources from sitting idle while waiting for data downloads. It is now included for free with every Together GPU Cluster. This system alleviates the need for repeated data reads from Hugging Face Hub and object storage.

The tool requires no application changes and uses a single command to start. It works with Hugging Face Hub, Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, and Together AI's T4 object storage. T4 is an S3 compatible solution currently available in a limited preview. Users configure encrypted credentials in a secrets vault to handle authentication. The system runs on every GPU node and uses cluster NVMe for caching.

Together AI stated that GPUs are only as fast as the data pipelines feeding them. They explained that cross-cloud reads are slow, rate-limited, and expensive, such as AWS egress at $0.09 per GB. The company noted that TSA provides resilience to outages when upstream sources fail. They claimed that cold reads cost nothing extra and run within 5 percent of direct downloads. The team mentioned that a deeper technical look at ASTRA technology is coming soon.

AI teams are affected because they often keep source data in distant object storage. These users face a WAN tax that leads to failed jobs and wasted money. Measured results on an H100 node in us-central show warm reads are 20 times faster. A 2 GiB object from Cloudflare R2 dropped from 15 seconds to 0.7 seconds. Small files saw latency drop by 60 to 80 times, and egress decreased 200 times.

The background involves the ASTRA technology used for the company's own inference fleet. This architecture was built to feed some of the largest GPU fleets in the world. The company observed that Hugging Face downloads from us-central were 5 times faster than from ca-west. This proves that the caching win is largest where the origin is slowest. The system was tested on October 28, 2026, using a preview deployment chart 0.6.0.

Users can now enable the accelerator from the settings page of their GPU cluster. The documentation allows users to set up the system in under ten minutes. The company encourages users to contact sales to try the T4 managed object storage. The articles leave open the specific date for the upcoming ASTRA engineering post. They also leave open the general availability date for the T4 storage solution.

stories.Headline: AI chip demand creates structural high bandwidth memory shortage for top suppliers
stories.Summary:
A high-bandwidth memory shortage exists as of November 21, 2026, because AI chips require massive amounts of silicon. Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron are the three main suppliers facing this structural supply chain problem. TrendForce projects HBM will take 23% of DRAM wafer input in 2026 and nearly 30% in 2027. Futu News reports that current HBM supply is roughly 58% of estimated first-quarter demand. This shift reduces the wafers available for conventional memory used in phones, PCs, and servers.

HBM requires three to four times the wafer capacity of general-purpose DRAM, causing conventional contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in Q4. HBM4 prices are at least $2.05 per gigabit in 2026 and may reach $3.00 to $5.50 per gigabit in 2027. Samsung is building an HBM hub at Onyang for KRW 46 trillion to KRW 56 trillion, moving operations up to June 2028. SK hynix began HBM4 mass production in Q3 2026, while Micron produces HBM4 for the Nvidia Vera Rubin platform. Counterpoint Research puts second-quarter 2026 HBM revenue at 50% for SK hynix, 33% for Samsung, and 18% for Micron.

SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung stated that customer demand exceeds capacity and could remain higher even beyond 2030. Kim Ki-tae of SK hynix added that customers are requesting more than twice the volume the company can supply. Samsung reshuffled leadership on November 20 to elevate executives running HBM and Galaxy. Micron announced high-volume production of HBM4 and moved equipment into a Singapore advanced packaging facility. Samsung chairman Lee Jae-yong reportedly outlined the Onyang plan, though no verbatim statement is available.

Nvidia, AMD, and Google are driving demand with accelerators like the B300, MI455X, and TPU 8. Nvidia's RTX Spark line affects consumers by offering up to 128 GB of unified memory in compact desktops. Micron reports its 2026 HBM supply is sold out, covering only half to two-thirds of customer demand. SK hynix reports its HBM and related DRAM are sold out through 2029. Microsoft is also involved in the packaging race, having picked Intel's EMIB for Azure silicon.

HBM stacks DRAM dies using through-silicon vias and mounts them beside accelerators on a shared interposer for higher bandwidth. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won noted that making HBM requires using a lot of wafers. The shortage is structural because adding output requires new packaging lines and qualifying stacks with each accelerator customer. Samsung's HBM4 revenue more than tripled in Q3, making up about 60% of its HBM revenue. SK hynix reported Q3 revenue of KRW 104.62 trillion and an operating margin of about 80%.

New capacity from China's CXMT and other major memory fabs may not add meaningful output until around 2028. Samsung's Onyang investment for HBM4E creates a risk of a memory glut once that capacity lands. HBM4E prices are forecast by one source to potentially exceed $5 per gigabit. The industry is waiting to see if SK hynix's reported 70% HBM4 production yield is accurate. It remains open whether buyers with long-term agreements or spot-style purchases will drive final 2027 pricing.

stories.Headline: Experts urge Samsung and SK Hynix to expand into advanced packaging and foundry services
stories.Summary:
Semiconductor experts from the United States and Japan met on November 18, 2026, at the Global Future Technology Forum hosted by Korea Economic TV. They warned that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix cannot maintain their market dominance by relying solely on the performance of high bandwidth memory chips. These South Korean companies must now expand their capabilities into advanced packaging and foundry services to remain competitive. The experts argued that the ability to integrate memory with logic semiconductors is now as critical as the memory itself.

Success requires securing logic and memory interface capabilities, as well as mastering 2.5D packaging to bind GPUs and memory together. Takashi Yunogami noted that TSMC currently holds a near 80 percent monopoly over the 2.5D packaging market. South Korean firms must also look beyond current memory to develop technologies like High Bandwidth Flash to support agentic AI. Meanwhile, China has increased its share of domestically supplied equipment to between 20 and 30 percent in certain segments.

Paul Triolo stated that securing advanced packaging is the top priority because next generation memory is essentially a packaging and foundry problem. He also observed that Chinese companies have already surpassed several technical benchmarks for logic and memory semiconductors. Takashi Yunogami explained that Japan's Rapidus failed to build a foundation for mass production despite receiving GAA technology from IBM. He believes it is impossible for Rapidus to mass produce 2 nanometer semiconductors because they lack experience in intermediate process generations.

The competition is shifting from selling individual memory components toward total system integration and the creation of a broad industrial ecosystem. Douglas Fuller suggested that industrial policy should prioritize dynamic efficiency and technological learning over short term costs or profitability. He noted that while lithography limits may hinder China's DRAM progress, the pursuit by YMTC in the NAND market requires more vigilance. South Korean companies must accumulate yield and mass production experience to avoid being pushed to the periphery of the AI supply chain.

stories.Headline: EY, Microsoft launch agentic cyber defence centre for AI security
stories.Summary:
EY and Microsoft jointly launched an Agentic Cyber Defence Centre, according to a TechGig report published on November 20, 2026. The centre integrates Microsoft technologies with policy controls and tamper-evident records for the actions taken by AI agents. It extends the existing alliance between the two companies into agent-led security operations, with the stated aim of connecting fragmented cyber defences. EY says the platform helps organisations retain human responsibility for automated decisions while agents take on more security work.

The platform applies policy-based controls to agent actions and keeps tamper-evident records that let organisations track changes and coordinate responses. The announcement describes an integrated transformation and operations model that spans identity, data, applications, cloud and operational technology. EY plans to apply agentic blueprints across these domains, using reusable patterns to connect security capabilities rather than relying on separate deployments. The stated aim is sustained and repeatable improvement in cyber defence.

EY is implementing Microsoft security for agentic cyber defence across its global organisation as what it calls Client Zero. This internal deployment is meant to validate operating models, codify controls and develop reusable patterns, with the aim of reducing implementation risk for clients. Richard Watson, EY Global Consulting Cybersecurity Leader, said the future of cybersecurity requires an entirely new operating model. Naseem Tuffaha, Corporate Vice President, Security at Microsoft, said securing the AI-powered enterprise requires a new model for cyber defence that keeps pace as AI changes how organisations operate and are attacked.

stories.Headline: South Korea surpasses one trillion dollars in annual exports driven by AI chip demand
stories.Summary:
South Korea surpassed one trillion dollars in annual exports for the first time this year on Thursday, driven largely by a boom in artificial intelligence chips. This milestone makes the nation the fourth country ever to reach this threshold, following the United States and Germany in 2006 and China in 2007. The achievement occurred despite significant global trade headwinds, including higher tariffs from the administration of President Donald Trump and ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. This growth follows a previous record of 709.3 billion dollars last year, which narrowed the gap with Japan's 738.3 billion dollars.

The surge was led by semiconductor exports, which rose 193.1 percent to 396.8 billion dollars between January and October, representing 42.7 percent of total exports. This demand for memory chips used in data centers benefited major companies like Samsung Electronics Co. and SK hynix Inc. The cumulative trade surplus for the first ten months reached 294.9 billion dollars, more than triple the 2017 record of 95.2 billion dollars. Consequently, the economy is expected to grow by more than 3 percent in 2026, the first such expansion since 2021.

Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan credited the workers and businesses for this success and promised continued government support for exporters. He stated that the government would help companies overcome various challenges in financing, logistics, and trade to maintain this growth. Meanwhile, Professor Lee Jae-min of Seoul National University School of Law called the event historic but warned about potential trade restrictions. He noted that managing these risks is essential to ensure the sustainability of growth driven by semiconductors and artificial intelligence.

While shipbuilding, defense, and biohealth industries grew, automakers and electronics manufacturers faced pressure from Chinese rivals and American tariffs. Experts warn that a heavy reliance on semiconductors makes the economy vulnerable to price drops or a slowdown in global AI investment. To mitigate these external shocks, the country must develop new markets and diversify its export industries beyond traditional heavy manufacturing. South Korean companies are currently reviewing their supply chains and overseas production plans to adapt to these uncertainties.

stories.Headline: Commerce Department approves sales of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies
stories.Summary:
The Commerce Department approved sales of over 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies as of May 2026. The Bureau of Industry and Security handled these approvals for Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Documents released on Thursday by the House Foreign Affairs Committee revealed these specific sales figures. This news emerged following the resignation of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. The release occurred amid increasing scrutiny regarding the export of chips to China.

The Bureau of Industry and Security licensed H200 sales to ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent. Approvals included sales to firms the Department of Defense designated as Chinese Military Companies. Between December and May, companies requested 3.4 million AI chip sales to China. License requests also included firms like Baidu and Tesla Shanghai. Some approvals went to Maginfra and New Matrix, which are suspected smuggling fronts.

Representative Gregory Meeks said the administration's handling of export controls put national security at risk. He stated the Bureau of Industry and Security failed to enforce rules and requires oversight. A Bureau of Industry and Security spokesperson said licensing decisions resulted from multiple agency consultations. Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo stated that approvals were subject to strict conditions and limited volumes. AMD stated it maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance with all export laws.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon said the number of approved chips is not that many. He noted that the government approved about one out of every four requested sales. Analyst Patrick Moorhead said Beijing did not approve large scale imports, which limited sales. Hunterbrook Media alleged AMD has a China problem involving firmware for blacklisted IEIT Systems. Lawmakers are concerned that Jensen Huang's relationship with a spy jeopardized American AI dominance.

Export controls on AI chips began under the Biden administration in 2022. In December, Trump said Nvidia could ship H200s if the U.S. got 25 percent. Nvidia reported 2.4 billion dollars in quarterly revenue from H200 sales in China. Former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed. Investigators suspect Megaspeed diverted Nvidia chips to China before Alice Huang left in 2025.

Jensen Huang will have a closed door interview with three committees on December 1. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter is scheduled to appear before the panels December 2. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has also agreed to testify before the Senate banking committee. The Commerce Department issued a rule Monday to stop Chinese companies leasing computing power. The articles leave open whether the new rule will successfully close the leasing loophole.

stories.Headline: Nebius revenue grows 571% as analyst upgrades stock to strong buy
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group N.V. shares have fallen about 65% from their all-time high and roughly 45% since the author's last coverage, a decline the article attributes to a general sell-off in AI-related stocks. The author upgraded the stock from Buy to Strong Buy on November 19, 2026, arguing that Wall Street is overlooking the company's AI infrastructure platform and its inference software. In the third quarter, Nebius revenue grew 571% to $981 million, and the AI Cloud EBITDA margin reached 53%, supported by demand and higher pricing. The article also describes an algorithmic compute marketplace that adjusts offers for demand and lease duration, with current prices running 15% below estimated customer willingness to pay.

The company cut its fiscal 2026 revenue guidance to between $3 billion and $3.2 billion after third-party delays at Microsoft's New Jersey data center. More than half of the contracted capacity is expected by year-end, with the remainder scheduled for the second quarter of 2027. Fiscal 2027 capital expenditure guidance is $40 billion to $45 billion, against expected customer prepayments of $17 billion to $20 billion and $7.4 billion in cash. Asset-backed financing is anticipated to cover 75% to 85% of that capital expenditure, though the article says additional debt or equity issuance may still be needed.

The author, a risk management business analyst at a Greek bank, wrote the article himself and discloses a beneficial long position in Nebius shares through stock ownership, options or other derivatives. He states that he received no compensation for the article beyond Seeking Alpha and has no business relationship with any company mentioned. He argues that the sell-off overlooks the company's infrastructure, software and funding model, while noting that execution risk on the marketplace is high and that short-term leases may constrain growth in remaining performance obligations. The article says valuation sits near the low end of Nebius's one-year EV/Sales range, and it advises investors to watch how the guidance cut and the financing plan develop.
